B9.name: Time on Task / Time on Learning

modules.title: Establishing classroom routines
modules.teacher_line_en: Get the first 5 minutes back: teach an entry routine your class runs every single day
modules.teacher_line_ur: کلاس کے پہلے پانچ منٹ واپس لیں: داخلے کی ایک روٹین بنائیں جو بچے روز خود کریں
modules.summary_en: A trainer names five routines a crowded class can run on autopilot: an entry routine (walk in quietly, take out copies, sit), an exit routine (pack up, homework reminder, line up), transition signals (clap pattern, bell, hand signal), attention cues ('1-2-3, eyes on me', 'Focus, focus' / 'Everyone focus' x3) and an end-of-day goal check-in. The teacher learns to install a routine the way a skill is taught: model it in first person, practise it with the class calling out each step, let children do it alone with feedback, repeat daily and praise the routine by name.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ کلاس میں داخلے، چھٹی، سرگرمی بدلنے اور توجہ لینے کی روٹین کیسے بنائیں اور اسے خود کر کے دکھا کر، بچوں کے ساتھ مشق کروا کر روز دہرا کر عادت کیسے بنائیں۔
symptoms: several minutes of noise at the start before any teaching ('baith jao', 'copiyan nikalo' repeated)
teacher says 'chup' / 'khamosh' many times to get attention between activities
each switch between activities takes long stretches of instructions with no signal
lesson ends at the bell with no look back at what was learned
modules.not_for: Teachers whose class already starts and switches smoothly; it gives no help on questioning or subject explanation.

segments.title_en: What routines are for
segments.title_ur: روٹین کیوں ضروری ہیں
segments.summary_en: The trainer introduces routines as the way to cut disruptions such as chatting, movement and late entry.

segments.title_en: Entry, exit, transition and attention routines
segments.title_ur: داخلے، چھٹی، تبدیلی اور توجہ کی روٹین
segments.summary_en: Four routine types with words to use: walk in quietly and take out copies; pack up and line up; clap/bell signals between activities; '1-2-3, eyes on me' and the 'Focus, focus' / 'Everyone focus' call-and-response.

segments.title_en: End-of-day goal check-in
segments.title_ur: دن کے آخر میں اہداف کا جائزہ
segments.summary_en: Goals written on the board in the morning are reviewed quickly with students at the end of the day; every routine gets a clear name, e.g. homework copies on the desk = entry routine.

segments.title_en: Why each routine pays off
segments.title_ur: ہر روٹین کا فائدہ
segments.summary_en: The purpose of each routine: smooth start and end, less time lost in switches, longer focus, and a 'What I learned today' reflection that lets students summarise their learning.

segments.title_en: Model, practise, repeat, praise a routine
segments.title_ur: روٹین کو خود کر کے دکھائیں اور مشق کروائیں
segments.summary_en: How to install one routine: the teacher performs it in first person, then practises it with the class calling out each step, then lets children do it alone with feedback, repeats daily, re-teaches if it slips, and praises by naming the routine.

segments.title_en: Recap: four keys to routines
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ: روٹین کی چار باتیں
segments.summary_en: Recap of clear definition, visible purpose, modelling and consistent practice, then goodbye.

modules.title: Establishing classroom rules
modules.teacher_line_en: Stop saying 'chup' all period: three board rules and a calm 'remember, hands first'
modules.teacher_line_ur: بار بار 'چپ' کہنے کے بجائے: بورڈ پر تین رولز اور نرمی سے 'پہلے ہاتھ اٹھائیں'
modules.summary_en: A trainer sets out three short class rules (raise your hand before speaking, respect each other, finish work on time), writes them on the board with a simple icon such as a hand, and explains to children why each rule matters. The teacher learns a calm script for a child who calls out ('we all want to hear you, but do you remember our class rule?'), how to model the rule, and to praise or give a chalk star to children who follow it, the same way every day.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ سیکھیں گے کہ تین مختصر کلاس رولز بورڈ پر کیسے لکھیں، بچوں کو ان کی وجہ کیسے سمجھائیں، اور بغیر ڈانٹے نرمی سے یاد دہانی اور تعریف کے ذریعے انہیں عادت کیسے بنائیں۔
symptoms: teacher says 'chup ho jao' / 'khamosh' many times in the lesson
many children answer at once and the teacher accepts called-out answers
teacher repeats 'haath uthao' but never names a rule or praises a child who follows it
no class rules are stated or referred to at any point
modules.not_for: Teachers whose class already follows hand-raising and turn-taking; it has nothing on questioning or subject teaching.

segments.title_en: Three short rules, written up and explained
segments.title_ur: تین مختصر رولز: بورڈ پر لکھیں اور وجہ بتائیں
segments.summary_en: The trainer gives three short rules (hand up before speaking, respect each other, finish work on time), says to write them in order on the board, and to tell children why each one matters.

segments.title_en: Calm reminder when a child calls out
segments.title_ur: جب بچہ بغیر ہاتھ اٹھائے بولے تو نرمی سے یاد دہانی
segments.summary_en: When a child speaks without raising a hand, the teacher stops them gently with a set line ('we all want to hear you, but do you remember our class rule?'), models raising a hand, pins a hand icon beside the rule, and smiles while prompting 'remember, hands first'.

segments.title_en: Praise the rule-follower, every day the same
segments.title_ur: رول ماننے والے کی تعریف، ہر دن ایک جیسا ردعمل
segments.summary_en: Acknowledge a child who follows the rule regularly with praise or a small star, remind calmly when a rule is broken, and keep both responses identical every day until the rule is a habit.

modules.title: How to use attention cues in classroom
modules.teacher_line_en: Get a noisy class listening in seconds with a clap-back or 'Eyes on me' cue
modules.teacher_line_ur: تالی یا 'Eyes on me' کے اشارے سے شور والی کلاس کو چند سیکنڈ میں متوجہ کریں
modules.summary_en: The presenter lists five quick attention cues with the exact teacher words and the children's reply: 'Eyes on me' / 'Yes, teacher', the '1, 2, 3!' / 'Eyes on me!' chant, a clap-back pattern, a raised-hand signal and a 2-second light switch-off, then shows a short demo of the chant and clap-back. Teachers learn to pick ONE cue, practise it 2-3 times with the class and use it consistently so they never need to raise their voice.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ تالی، ہاتھ اٹھانے یا '1، 2، 3 — Eyes on me' جیسے چھوٹے اشاروں سے پوری کلاس کی توجہ چند سیکنڈ میں کیسے واپس لائی جائے۔
symptoms: teacher says 'chup', 'khamosh' or 'suno' many times in the lesson
teacher raises voice or repeats an instruction because children are still talking
long noisy gaps between activities with no signal to refocus the class
no call-and-response or clap signal anywhere in the lesson
modules.not_for: Teachers whose class already settles quickly on a signal; it does not cover questioning or lesson content.

segments.title_en: Intro: why attention slips
segments.title_ur: تعارف: بچوں کی توجہ کیوں ہٹتی ہے
segments.summary_en: Greeting and the problem: children get busy talking and cannot hear the teacher.

segments.title_en: Five attention cues, why they work, and a demo
segments.title_ur: توجہ کے پانچ اشارے، ان کا فائدہ اور عملی مظاہرہ
segments.summary_en: Five cues with the teacher's words and the children's reply ('Eyes on me'/'Yes, teacher', '1, 2, 3!'/'Eyes on me', clap-back, raised hand, light switch-off), why a clear signal cuts noise and speeds transitions, then a short demo of the chant and clap-back.

segments.title_en: Pick one cue and practise it
segments.title_ur: ایک اشارہ چنیں اور مشق کریں
segments.summary_en: Choose one cue, practise it with the class 2-3 times until it is a habit; consistency means no raised voice. Ends with a recap.

modules.title: Inclusive Classroom
modules.teacher_line_en: What an inclusive classroom means: every child, including shy ones, takes part
modules.teacher_line_ur: انکلوسیو کلاس روم کیا ہے: ہر بچہ، شرمیلا بھی، سبق میں حصہ لے
modules.summary_en: A trainer defines an inclusive classroom and 'diverse learners' (shy children, children with another home language, learning disabilities), then lists features: everyone participates, content linked to children's lives, thinking time, think-pair-share, group work and respect for every voice. Practices such as level-wise tasks, an accessible layout and a strong-weak peer-support pairing are only named, never shown.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں بتایا گیا ہے کہ انکلوسیو کلاس روم کیا ہوتا ہے اور ہر بچے کو سیکھنے کے عمل میں کیسے شامل کیا جائے، مگر کوئی عملی مثال نہیں دکھائی گئی۔
symptoms: the same few children answer every question while most of the class is never heard
teacher takes the first answer immediately after asking, with no thinking time
one task for the whole class with no easier or extension version
children who speak another home language are never addressed or called on
modules.not_for: Teachers who need a concrete differentiation or participation technique to try tomorrow; it only defines terms and names practices.

segments.title_en: What is an inclusive classroom; who are diverse learners
segments.title_ur: انکلوسیو کلاس روم اور مختلف طرح کے سیکھنے والے بچے
segments.summary_en: Greeting, then a definition of an inclusive classroom and of diverse learners (shy children, other home languages, learning disabilities); also repeats the learning-styles myth.

segments.title_en: Features: participation, thinking time, think-pair-share
segments.title_ur: خصوصیات: سب کی شرکت، سوچنے کا وقت، تھنک پیئر شیئر
segments.summary_en: Lists the features of an inclusive classroom: every child participates and asks questions, content is linked to children's lives, thinking time before answers, think-pair-share, group work and respect for every voice. Named, not demonstrated.

segments.title_en: Inclusive practices named, and recap
segments.title_ur: انکلوسیو طریقوں کے نام اور خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Names level-wise tasks, an accessible classroom layout, strong-weak peer support and supportive language, then recaps the definition.

modules.title: Diverse learners in classroom
modules.teacher_line_en: 2-minute reminder: one class holds many learning paces and home languages
modules.teacher_line_ur: دو منٹ کی یاد دہانی: ایک ہی کلاس کے بچے مختلف رفتار اور زبان سے سیکھتے ہیں
modules.summary_en: A presenter speaks to camera about three kinds of diverse learners: children who learn faster or slower, children whose home language (Punjabi, Pashto) differs from the classroom's Urdu/English, and 'learning styles'. The only advice is to guide each child at their own pace and give extra language support; no technique, question or activity is shown.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں بتایا گیا ہے کہ کلاس میں بچے مختلف رفتار اور مختلف گھریلو زبان کے ساتھ آتے ہیں، مگر کوئی عملی طریقہ نہیں دکھایا گیا۔
symptoms: every child gets the same task at the same pace; no easier or harder version is mentioned
teacher explains only in English or textbook Urdu and never checks whether children with another home language followed
slower children's wrong answers are skipped and the teacher moves on with the fast group
modules.not_for: Any teacher who needs a concrete differentiation or language-support move for tomorrow; this is definitions only and repeats the learning-styles myth.

segments.title_en: Why classes are diverse: levels and home languages
segments.title_ur: کلاس میں فرق کیوں: سیکھنے کے لیول اور گھریلو زبان
segments.summary_en: Greeting and framing: children come at different learning levels and from homes where Punjabi or Pashto is spoken, so Urdu/English can be a second or third language for them.

segments.title_en: Three kinds of diverse learners (definitions)
segments.title_ur: مختلف طرح کے سیکھنے والے بچے: تعریفیں
segments.summary_en: Defines faster/slower learners (guide each at their pace), children needing extra language support, and visual/auditory/kinaesthetic 'learning styles', then closes. No how-to is shown.

modules.title: Understanding child psychology
modules.teacher_line_en: Why Grade 1 needs short instructions and Grade 5 can handle thinking tasks
modules.teacher_line_ur: گریڈ ون کو مختصر ہدایات اور گریڈ پانچ کو سوچنے والے کام کیوں دیں
modules.summary_en: A trainer explains child development stages (motor, language, social-emotional) with infant milestones, then draws classroom implications: movement-based tasks like arranging blocks or drawing for young classes, short clear instructions for KG/Grade 1, no long readings for Grade 2, critical-thinking tasks for Grade 5. It is a principle (match the task to the child's age) rather than a demonstrated technique.
modules.summary_ur: یہ ویڈیو بتاتی ہے کہ بچوں کی عمر اور نشوونما کے مرحلے کے مطابق آپ کام اور ہدایات کیسے ترتیب دے سکتے ہیں۔
symptoms: Grade 1-2 children given long multi-step instructions and many ask 'kya karna hai?'
long reading passage set for an early grade with most children unable to read it
same task for every child with no easier or harder version mentioned
modules.not_for: Teachers who already adapt tasks by age and level; it shows no classroom technique, only the developmental principle.

segments.title_en: Why some children race ahead and others fall behind
segments.title_ur: کچھ بچے آگے اور کچھ پیچھے کیوں رہ جاتے ہیں
segments.summary_en: Opens on the problem of mixed paces in one class and defines child psychology as knowing what a child can do and understand at each age.

segments.title_en: Motor, language and social stages in the classroom
segments.title_ur: جسمانی، لسانی اور سماجی نشوونما کلاس روم میں
segments.summary_en: Walks through motor, language and social-emotional development with infant milestones, linking each to movement tasks, short clear instructions for KG/Grade 1, and play-based group activities.

segments.title_en: Adjust tasks to the child's age
segments.title_ur: بچے کی عمر کے مطابق کام ترتیب دیں
segments.summary_en: Gives the age-matching principle: no long readings for Grade 2, critical-thinking tasks for Grade 5, know who will need support, and design age-appropriate tasks.

modules.title: Auditory aids
modules.teacher_line_en: Children stop mid-paragraph? Rewrite it: bold key words, one short line each
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے پیراگراف کے بیچ میں رک جاتے ہیں؟ اہم الفاظ نمایاں کریں، لمبے جملے توڑیں
modules.summary_en: A trainer explains why children in crowded classes stop halfway through reading a passage or word problem: long, complex lines. The teacher sees a passage on the solar system rewritten with key terms in bold, long sentences broken onto separate lines and space between sections, plus maths word problems split into three short lines with numbers clearly spaced, and learns to simplify one paragraph on the board before class.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ مشکل پیراگراف یا ورڈ پرابلم کو اہم الفاظ نمایاں کر کے، لمبے جملے توڑ کر اور جگہ چھوڑ کر کیسے آسان بنائیں تاکہ کمزور قاری بچے بھی پڑھ سکیں۔
symptoms: children stop partway through reading aloud and the teacher reads the rest for them
teacher reads the textbook passage and children only repeat after the teacher
a word problem is read out twice and no child can say what is being asked
teacher explains many unknown words one by one during a long passage
modules.not_for: Teachers of early readers still learning letter sounds, or classes that already read grade-level text fluently; it is a text-preparation tip, not a reading-strategy lesson.

segments.title_en: Why children stop halfway through a passage
segments.title_ur: بچے پڑھتے پڑھتے بیچ میں کیوں رک جاتے ہیں
segments.summary_en: The trainer describes struggling readers in crowded classes losing interest when a 10-12 line passage or word problem uses long, unfamiliar language, and says the text itself should be simplified.

segments.title_en: Bold, break, space: the method and two worked passages
segments.title_ur: اہم الفاظ نمایاں، جملے مختصر، جگہ: طریقہ اور دو عملی مثالیں
segments.summary_en: The trainer names the method (highlight key words, break long sentences into short lines, use visuals, write word problems on three short lines) and then shows it on a Pakistan-climate passage and a solar-system passage rewritten with bold terms, separate lines and spacing, plus clear number spacing in word problems; ends with a challenge to simplify one paragraph for the next lesson.

modules.title: Differentiated reading materials
modules.teacher_line_en: One reading lesson, three levels: give each group of readers its own task
modules.teacher_line_ur: ایک ہی سبق، تین سطحیں: ہر گروپ کو اس کی پڑھنے کی سطح کا مواد دیں
modules.summary_en: The trainer explains how to give children at different reading levels different material on the same theme: picture/word cards for beginners, short repeated-pattern sentences for intermediate readers, a paragraph with comprehension questions for advanced readers. A Grade 2 'My Family' example shows three groups: picture-word matching, 'This is my mother. She cooks food.', and a short paragraph with questions; it ends with pre-teaching new words with pictures and pairing strong with weak readers.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ ایک ہی سبق ('My Family') کے لیے کمزور، درمیانے اور تیز پڑھنے والے بچوں کو الگ الگ مواد کیسے دیا جائے۔
symptoms: the whole class reads the same textbook passage in chorus
a few fluent children read while others sit silent or stuck on letters
teacher says 'sab parho' with no different task for weak readers
fast readers finish early and have nothing further to read
modules.not_for: Maths or science teachers and Grade 6+ classes; it is about early reading material, not about decoding instruction itself.

segments.title_en: Intro: one class, many reading levels
segments.title_ur: تعارف: ایک کلاس، پڑھنے کی مختلف سطحیں
segments.summary_en: Greeting and the problem: the same text loses beginners and bores advanced readers.

segments.title_en: Age-matched book lists and choice
segments.title_ur: عمر کے مطابق کتابوں کی فہرست اور انتخاب
segments.summary_en: Give an age-matched book list before reading time, choose books for children first, later let them pick; differentiation means adjusting material to need.

segments.title_en: Material for three reading levels
segments.title_ur: پڑھنے کی تین سطحوں کے لیے مواد
segments.summary_en: Beginners: picture books, flashcards, rhyming charts; intermediate: short repeated-pattern sentences, bilingual support; advanced: paragraphs and comprehension passages.

segments.title_en: Grade 2 'My Family' in three groups
segments.title_ur: گریڈ 2 'My Family' تین گروپس میں
segments.summary_en: Group 1 matches picture cards to words, Group 2 reads short sentences in a booklet, Group 3 reads a paragraph and answers comprehension questions: same theme, different material.

segments.title_en: Pre-teach words and pair readers
segments.title_ur: نئے الفاظ پہلے سکھائیں اور بچوں کی جوڑیاں بنائیں
segments.summary_en: Pre-teach new words with pictures and repeat them; pair good readers with weak readers. Closes with a recap.

modules.title: Group activity
modules.teacher_line_en: Only 2-3 children talk in group work? Pick the grouping to fit the task's goal
modules.teacher_line_ur: گروپ ورک میں صرف دو تین بچے بولتے ہیں؟ سرگرمی کے مقصد کے مطابق گروپ بنائیں
modules.summary_en: A trainer explains flexible grouping: choose mixed-ability, same-ability or task-based groups according to the activity's goal instead of keeping fixed groups. One poem-writing example is run three ways: fluent and beginner readers mixed to think of rhymes together; beginners given simple rhyming words while advanced children write longer verses; and groups with roles (one writes rhymes, one checks, one presents). The rule a teacher can copy: decide the goal first, then the grouping.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ گروپ ورک میں سرگرمی کے مقصد کے مطابق مکس، ایک جیسی سطح یا کام کی بنیاد پر گروپ کیسے بنائیں تاکہ ہر بچہ حصہ لے۔
symptoms: group work where the same two or three children answer for every group
fast finishers sit idle while other children are still confused
groups are always the same seating rows regardless of the task
every group gets the identical task with no roles assigned
modules.not_for: Teachers who have never run group work and need how to launch it (instructions, roles, timing); it shows no classroom footage.

segments.title_en: Why group work fails: introducing flexible grouping
segments.title_ur: گروپ ورک کیوں ناکام ہوتا ہے: فلیکسیبل گروپنگ کا تعارف
segments.summary_en: Opens with the problem (some children confused, some finish at once, only two or three speak) and introduces flexible grouping: groups change with each activity's goal.

segments.title_en: Three ways to group: mixed, same-level, task roles
segments.title_ur: گروپ بنانے کے تین طریقے: مکس، ایک سطح، کام کے کردار
segments.summary_en: Mixed-ability groups so children learn from each other, same-ability groups to give weaker children extra practice on one skill, and task-based groups (brainstorm, edit, present); right grouping gives quiet children a role and keeps fast learners busy.

segments.title_en: One poem task, three groupings: goal first, then groups
segments.title_ur: ایک نظم، تین طرح کے گروپ: پہلے مقصد، پھر گروپ
segments.summary_en: A short-poem writing task grouped three ways: mixed readers think of rhymes together, beginners get simple rhyming words while advanced children write longer verses, and role groups write, check and present. Ends with the rule: decide the activity's goal, then the grouping.

modules.title: 5 step lesson plan
modules.teacher_line_en: Plan any lesson in 5 steps, from a riddle at the start to an exit ticket at the end
modules.teacher_line_ur: کسی بھی سبق کو پانچ حصوں میں بنائیں: پہیلی سے آغاز، ایگزٹ ٹکٹ پر اختتام
modules.summary_en: A voice-over walks through the five sections of a Taleemabad lesson plan: opening, explanation, guided practice, independent practice and conclusion, with two or three named strategies for each (a riddle or short story to open, bundling sticks or a board diagram to explain, pair and 4–5-child group worksheets while the teacher circulates, a short individual worksheet, and an exit ticket, quick quiz or 'what did you learn today?' to close). It ends by asking the teacher to plan their next lesson in these five steps.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں پانچ حصوں والا سبق کا منصوبہ سمجھایا گیا ہے: آغاز، وضاحت، رہنمائی میں مشق، خود مشق اور اختتام، ہر حصے کے لیے آسان طریقوں کے ساتھ۔
symptoms: lesson opens with 'open page N' and no recall of the last lesson or a real-life example
teacher explains then goes straight to homework; children never practise in pairs or groups with the teacher's help
no closing question or recap; the lesson stops when the bell rings
one long stretch of teacher talk with no visible phases or 'now we will…' transitions
modules.not_for: Teachers who already run a clear opening–practice–closure sequence; it names strategies but never shows them with children.

segments.title_en: Opening: recall, real-life example, story or riddle
segments.title_ur: آغاز: پچھلا سبق یاد کروائیں، کہانی یا پہیلی سے شروع کریں

segments.summary_en: Recap and planning homework: use the 5-step template and decide the opening question, explanation aid, guided and independent activities and closing review for any topic; then farewell.

modules.title: Group Activities
modules.teacher_line_en: Get 40 children reading in groups: build words from pictures, read line by line
modules.teacher_line_ur: چالیس بچوں کو گروپس میں پڑھائیں: تصویر سے لفظ بنانا اور باری باری پڑھنا
modules.summary_en: Despite the title, this is group READING for early English literacy in a crowded class: a warm-up revising rhyming, sounds and blending, an interactive read-aloud where children predict what happens next, then small groups build words (net, bin) by placing letters on a mat under a picture. With no materials, groups read the same paragraph in alternate lines while the teacher circulates to correct fluency and pronunciation, and groups present at the end.
modules.summary_ur: آپ دیکھیں گے کہ بھری ہوئی کلاس میں بچوں کو چھوٹے گروپس میں تصویر سے لفظ بنانے اور باری باری پڑھنے کی مشق کیسے کروائیں۔
symptoms: reading lesson where only the teacher reads and the class repeats in chorus
children never sound out or build a word themselves
a 40+ class with no small groups or pairs during the literacy period
story read aloud with no 'what will happen next?' question
modules.not_for: Teachers of maths, science or Grade 4+ classes looking for general group-work structure; the whole module is early-grade reading.

segments.title_en: Warm-up revision and an interactive read-aloud
segments.title_ur: دہرائی اور سوال جواب کے ساتھ کہانی پڑھنا
segments.summary_en: Frames group reading in an overcrowded class, then step 1 revises rhyming words, sounds and blending, and step 2 reads a short story aloud, asking children to guess what happens next and re-read new words.

segments.title_en: Groups build words from pictures on a letter mat
segments.title_ur: گروپس تصویر دیکھ کر حروف سے لفظ بنائیں
segments.summary_en: Children in small groups look at a picture (net, bin), say the sounds and place the matching letters on a mat, extending to digraphs like ch and sh learned earlier.

segments.title_en: No materials? Collaborative reading in alternate lines
segments.title_ur: سامان نہیں؟ گروپ میں باری باری سطریں پڑھیں
segments.summary_en: Each group reads the same paragraph with members taking alternate lines while the teacher visits groups to guide fluency and pronunciation; groups can present their part to the class at the end.

modules.title: Drawing Diagrams
modules.teacher_line_en: Only chalk? Go from toffees in hand to circles to a bar graph children draw themselves
modules.teacher_line_ur: صرف چاک؟ ہاتھ میں ٹافیوں سے دائروں اور پھر بار گراف تک، جو بچے خود بنائیں
modules.summary_en: With only board and chalk, the teacher holds 7 toffees in one hand and 4 in the other, draws 7 and 4 circles, then a bar diagram (hands on one axis, quantity on the other): 'the longer the bar, the bigger the amount'. Children then collect class data (boys vs girls, shoes vs sandals), draw their own bar diagrams, and answer 'Which group is bigger? What did the bars show you?' The teacher learns the concrete-pictorial-abstract chain and closing interpretation questions.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ صرف بورڈ اور چاک سے ٹافیوں جیسی اصل چیزوں سے دائروں کی تصویر اور پھر بار ڈایاگرام تک کیسے جائیں اور بچوں سے اپنی کلاس کا ڈیٹا جمع کروا کر ڈایاگرام بنوائیں۔
symptoms: numbers compared only as written figures on the board, no objects or drawing
teacher repeats the same explanation when children do not follow comparison
children never draw or make a diagram themselves in the maths lesson
no question like 'which is bigger and how do you know from the bars?'
lesson ends without children saying what the diagram showed
modules.not_for: Teachers of non-maths lessons or of upper grades already teaching graphs formally; this is an early-primary comparison/data clip.

segments.title_en: Teaching with only board and chalk
segments.title_ur: صرف بورڈ اور چاک سے پڑھانا
segments.summary_en: Greeting and the problem: a crowded government class with no charts or aids can still explain hard concepts with chalk.

segments.title_en: Open with 'what do we compare in daily life?'
segments.title_ur: روزمرہ زندگی میں موازنہ: آغاز کا سوال
segments.summary_en: The teacher opens by asking what children compare in daily life (toffees, pencils, attendance) and says a diagram shows how numbers relate.

segments.title_en: Toffees to circles to a bar diagram
segments.title_ur: ٹافیوں سے دائرے اور پھر بار ڈایاگرام
segments.summary_en: 7 toffees in one hand and 4 in the other become 7 and 4 drawn circles, then a simple bar diagram: the longer the bar, the more there is.

segments.title_en: Children collect data and draw their own bars
segments.title_ur: بچے ڈیٹا جمع کر کے خود بار بنائیں
segments.summary_en: Groups count boys and girls, draw a diagram, a representative explains it at the board; the teacher asks 'Which group is bigger? What did the bars show?'; then each child draws shoes vs sandals while the teacher checks labels and bars.

segments.title_en: Closing questions: what does a bar diagram show?
segments.title_ur: اختتامی سوال: بار ڈایاگرام کیا بتاتا ہے؟
segments.summary_en: The lesson closes with children answering 'What does a diagram show? What does a bar diagram mean? How does it help when we compare numbers?', then a recap of the object-picture-diagram steps.

modules.title: Number Sense
modules.teacher_line_en: Show 36 as three bundles of ten sticks and six singles: place value children can see
modules.teacher_line_ur: 36 کو دس دس تنکوں کے تین بنڈل اور چھ الگ تنکے بنا کر دکھائیں: دہائی اکائی آسان
modules.summary_en: A trainer names why children who can count still get confused in addition and subtraction: they read 47 as 40 + 7 but do not see 4 tens and 7 ones. The teacher sees four chalk-friendly models for one number each (two ten frames for 23, three bundles of ten sticks plus 6 for 36, base-ten rods and cubes for 47, jumps of ten on a number line for 58) with a guiding question for each, such as 'if I add ten more dots, what is the number?'.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ ٹین فریم، تنکوں کے بنڈل، بلاکس اور نمبر لائن سے بچوں کو دہائی اور اکائی کا تصور کیسے سمجھائیں اور ساتھ رہنما سوال کیسے پوچھیں۔
symptoms: two-digit numbers taught as digits only, with no 'tens' and 'ones' language
children count on from one to add instead of using tens
carrying or borrowing errors in a Grade 1-3 addition or subtraction lesson
no object, drawing, ten frame or number line used in a place value lesson
modules.not_for: Teachers of Grade 4 and above or of non-maths lessons; it is only for early place value up to 100. Do not send together with module 15, which overlaps heavily.

segments.title_en: Why counting is not place value
segments.title_ur: گنتی آ جانا دہائی اکائی سمجھنا نہیں
segments.summary_en: The trainer names the misconception: children know 47 is 40 + 7 but not that the 4 means four tens, because they miss that after 9 a new group of ten forms. Introduces four tools: ten frames, bundling sticks, base-ten blocks, number line.

segments.title_en: Ten frames and bundles of sticks
segments.title_ur: ٹین فریم اور تنکوں کے بنڈل
segments.summary_en: Draw two full ten frames and three extra dots for 23 and ask 'if I add ten more dots, what is the number?'; then make 36 as three bundles of ten sticks and six singles and ask how many bundles and how many singles.

segments.title_en: Base-ten blocks and the number line
segments.title_ur: بیس ٹین بلاکس اور نمبر لائن
segments.summary_en: Show 47 as four ten-rods and seven unit cubes and ask what happens if one more rod is added; then reach 58 on a number line with five jumps of ten and eight small jumps, and ask where two more small jumps land. Can be done outside in the playground.

segments.title_en: Your turn, and recap
segments.title_ur: اب آپ کی باری، اور خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: The trainer asks the teacher to show one number between 50 and 75 with all four models and ask how many tens and ones it has, then recaps the four tools.

modules.title: Using Visual Tools
modules.teacher_line_en: Show 408 vs 480 with tens and ones columns: place value children can see
modules.teacher_line_ur: سیکڑہ، دہائی، اکائی کے کالموں سے 408 اور 480 کا فرق بچوں کو دکھائیں
modules.summary_en: The presenter shows four low-cost tools for place value: ten frames (47 as four full frames and 7 dots), bundling sticks (136 as bundles of ten plus singles), place-value blocks (100 + 30 + 6) and a hundreds/tens/ones chart, with questions like 'If I add one more ten rod, what number is it?'. The clearest part draws the columns on the board to compare 408 and 480 column by column; it ends with substitutes (matchsticks, boxes drawn in notebooks, columns on the board) so no kit is needed.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ ٹین فریم، تیلیوں کے بنڈل اور سیکڑہ-دہائی-اکائی کے کالم سے بچوں کو مقامی قدر اور اعداد کا موازنہ (408 اور 480) کیسے سمجھایا جائے۔
symptoms: place value taught only by naming the columns; children never place or move anything
comparing numbers taught as a spoken rule with no chart, objects or board columns
children confuse numbers like 408 and 480 or read 47 as 4 and 7
teacher says there are no materials for maths and teaches from the book only
modules.not_for: Teachers of Grade 4 and above or of non-maths lessons; it is only about 2-3 digit place value and comparing numbers.

segments.title_en: Intro: four visual tools
segments.title_ur: تعارف: چار بصری ٹولز
segments.summary_en: The presenter names the four tools (ten frames, bundling sticks, place-value blocks, charts) and what a ten frame is.

segments.title_en: Ten frames for 47 and 59
segments.title_ur: ٹین فریم سے 47 اور 59
segments.summary_en: Fill four full ten frames and 7 dots to show 47 = 4 tens 7 ones; repeat with 59 and ask the class how many tens and ones.

segments.title_en: Bundles and blocks for 136
segments.title_ur: بنڈل اور بلاکس سے 136
segments.summary_en: Bundle sticks in tens and build 136 with blocks as 100 + 30 + 6, then challenge: 'add one ten rod, what is the number? remove a hundred, what is left?'

segments.title_en: Compare 408 and 480 on a chart
segments.title_ur: چارٹ پر 408 اور 480 کا موازنہ
segments.summary_en: Draw hundreds/tens/ones columns (on the board if no chart), place 408 and 480, compare column by column to show 480 is bigger.

segments.title_en: Children place blocks; compare 274 and 249
segments.title_ur: بچے خود بلاکس رکھیں؛ 274 اور 249
segments.summary_en: Let children put blocks or sticks on the chart themselves; compare 274 and 249 by hundreds, then tens, then ones.

segments.title_en: No kit? Matchsticks and board columns
segments.title_ur: سامان نہیں؟ ماچس کی تیلیاں اور بورڈ کے کالم
segments.summary_en: Use one tool at a time; substitute matchsticks or strings for blocks, notebook boxes for ten frames, board columns for charts. Ends with a recap.

modules.title: Solve Basic Operations
modules.teacher_line_en: Teach 'carry one' with ice-cream sticks and place-value columns, not as a rule
modules.teacher_line_ur: حاصل اور ادھار کو تیلیوں اور مقامی قدر کے کالموں سے سمجھائیں، صرف اصول سے نہیں
modules.summary_en: A trainer walks through the concrete-pictorial-abstract (CPA) sequence for the four operations, grounded in place value. 368 + 457 is built with ice-cream sticks, straws and matchsticks (hundreds, tens, ones), then written in hundreds-tens-ones columns where 8 + 7 = 15 becomes 5 ones and 1 ten carried; subtraction with borrowing (6543 - 2789), 23 x 15 split into 23 x 5 + 23 x 10, and division by breaking 468 into 400 + 60 + 8 follow. A teacher learns to show carrying and borrowing as regrouping, not a trick.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ جمع، تفریق، ضرب اور تقسیم کو تیلیوں، کالموں اور مقامی قدر کی مدد سے مرحلہ وار کیسے سمجھائیں تاکہ بچے 'حاصل' کو صرف ایک ترکیب نہ سمجھیں۔
symptoms: teacher says 'ek hasil' / 'carry one' or 'borrow one' as a rule with no reason given
no sticks, blocks or drawings used for a two- or three-digit sum
no hundreds/tens/ones columns named or written on the board
children get the carry or borrow step wrong and the teacher just repeats the procedure
modules.not_for: Teachers of non-maths lessons or Grades 6+ whose maths lesson is not on the four operations; it is content for column arithmetic only.

segments.title_en: Operations as place value; the CPA approach
segments.title_ur: چار بنیادی عمل اور مقامی قدر: سی پی اے طریقہ
segments.summary_en: Introduces the aim: the four operations are an extension of place value, taught through concrete, pictorial and abstract stages.

segments.title_en: 368 + 457 with sticks and straws: regrouping
segments.title_ur: تیلیوں اور اسٹرا سے 368 جمع 457: دوبارہ گروپ بنانا
segments.summary_en: Represents 368 and 457 with ice-cream sticks (hundreds), straws (tens) and matchsticks (ones), counts ones, tens and hundreds, and uses 8 + 7 = 15 to show regrouping (carry) with objects.

segments.title_en: Place-value columns: carrying step by step
segments.title_ur: مقامی قدر کے کالم: حاصل مرحلہ وار
segments.summary_en: Draws hundreds, tens and ones columns, decomposes both numbers and solves 368 + 457 = 825, explaining that 15 is 5 ones and 1 ten carried to the tens column.

segments.title_en: Division by breaking the number apart: 468 / 4
segments.title_ur: عدد کو توڑ کر تقسیم: 468 تقسیم 4
segments.summary_en: Decomposes 468 into 400 + 60 + 8, divides each part by 4 (100, 15, 2) and adds them to get 117.

segments.title_en: Abstract stage on the board, and why carrying is logical
segments.title_ur: بورڈ پر علامتی مرحلہ، اور حاصل کیوں منطقی ہے
segments.summary_en: Shows the abstract stage: children write numbers in hundreds-tens-units columns in their copies and add ones with ones, tens with tens; recaps the three CPA steps and stresses that carrying is logical regrouping, not a trick.

segments.title_en: Subtraction with borrowing: 6543 - 2789
segments.title_ur: ادھار کے ساتھ تفریق: 6543 منفی 2789
segments.summary_en: Aligns thousands, hundreds, tens and ones and explains borrowing from the neighbouring digit (3 - 9 becomes 13 - 9). Note: the 'small minus big is impossible' phrasing holds only for whole numbers.

segments.title_en: Multiplying 23 x 15 by splitting; dividing 468 / 6
segments.title_ur: 23 ضرب 15 کو توڑ کر حل کرنا؛ 468 تقسیم 6
segments.summary_en: Splits 23 x 15 into 23 x 5 and 23 x 10 (objects like stones or leaves can be used) and adds the products; divides 468 by 6 as equal sharing into 6 groups by breaking it into 420 and 48 (one spoken slip: 48/6 said as 80; final 78 correct).

segments.title_en: Recap: four operations as one place-value journey
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ: چاروں عمل مقامی قدر کا ایک سفر
segments.summary_en: Recaps what each operation shows and urges using CPA in the next maths lesson.

modules.title: Word problems
modules.teacher_line_en: Stop children guessing 'plus or minus?': circle, underline, box, then solve
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے 'جمع یا تفریق؟' کا اندازہ نہ لگائیں: دائرہ، لکیر، ڈبہ، پھر حل
modules.summary_en: A presenter introduces the CUBES routine for word problems (Circle the numbers, Underline the question, Box the keywords, Evaluate the operation, Solve and check) and applies it aloud to local stories: samosas sold in Ramadan, fun-fair tickets, cricket matches, Eid mithai boxes. For the addition and subtraction problems they then solve with Concrete-Pictorial-Abstract steps (bundle sticks, place-value chart, column sum).
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں دکھایا گیا ہے کہ عبارتی سوال میں عدد پر دائرہ، سوال کے نیچے لکیر اور اہم لفظ پر ڈبہ لگا کر عمل کیسے چنیں، پھر تیلیوں اور خاکے سے حل کریں۔
symptoms: teacher reads the word problem aloud and immediately writes the sum on the board
children are asked 'plus karna hai ya minus?' and answer by guessing
no one marks the numbers, the question or the key word in the problem text
word problems use only textbook contexts, never a shop, Eid or cricket story
modules.not_for: Teachers of non-maths lessons or of maths lessons not on word problems; also not a fix for two-step problems, where keyword-to-operation matching misleads.

segments.title_en: Why word problems are hard: from story to number sentence
segments.title_ur: عبارتی سوال مشکل کیوں: کہانی سے عددی جملے تک
segments.summary_en: Greeting and framing: children struggle to translate a story into numbers; real-life stories shown as objects, drawings and number sentences (the CPA approach) make each step easier.

segments.title_en: CUBES: circle, underline, box, evaluate, solve (samosa problem)
segments.title_ur: کیوبز طریقہ: دائرہ، لکیر، ڈبہ، عمل کا انتخاب، حل (سموسوں کا سوال)
segments.summary_en: Names the five CUBES steps, then models them on a Ramadan samosa addition problem: circle 234 and 567, underline 'how many in total', box 'total', decide it is addition.

segments.title_en: Solve with sticks, place-value chart, then the column sum
segments.title_ur: تیلیوں، مقامی قیمت کے چارٹ اور پھر کالم میں حل
segments.summary_en: Solves the samosa problem with bundle sticks, a place-value chart and a number sentence (801), then runs CUBES and CPA on a fun-fair ticket subtraction with borrowing shown on ten-frames and arrows (3,754).

segments.title_en: CUBES for multiplication and division with Eid and cricket stories
segments.title_ur: ضرب اور تقسیم کے سوالوں پر کیوبز: عید اور کرکٹ کی کہانیاں
segments.summary_en: When the class has mastered operations, skip the full CPA cycle and focus on extracting information: CUBES on 15 cricket matches × 48 students and 60 Eid mithai boxes shared among 6 classes; closes by linking problems to children's own lives.

modules.title: Calenders
modules.teacher_line_en: Teach calendars through Eid, birthdays and 14 August, with a two-calendar group table
modules.teacher_line_ur: کیلنڈر کو عید، سالگرہ اور چودہ اگست سے جوڑ کر پڑھائیں
modules.summary_en: A trainer recaps the solar calendar (365/366 days, fixed 30/31-day months) and the Hijri calendar (354/355 days, months start with the moon, 29/30 days), then links both to children's lives: birthdays, the August-to-June school year, 14 August and 23 March, Eid and Muharram. Children compare when Ramadan started last year and this year, fill a group table of five events in both calendars, and discuss why Eid's date moves but Pakistan Day's does not.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ شمسی اور ہجری کیلنڈر کو بچوں کی سالگرہ، عید اور قومی دنوں سے جوڑ کر کیسے پڑھائیں۔
symptoms: months or days recited in chorus from the book
no example from children's own lives (birthday, Eid, 14 August) in a calendar lesson
no task where children write or compare dates themselves
never asks why Eid falls on a different date each year
modules.not_for: Teachers whose lesson is not about calendars, months or time; it is a content module, not a general engagement fix.

segments.title_en: Solar and Hijri calendars: the key facts
segments.title_ur: شمسی اور ہجری کیلنڈر: بنیادی حقائق
segments.summary_en: Recaps days per year, leap years and month lengths in the solar calendar, and the moon-based Hijri calendar with its 12 months of 29 or 30 days.

segments.title_en: Link calendars to birthdays, holidays and Eid
segments.title_ur: کیلنڈر کو سالگرہ، چھٹیوں اور عید سے جوڑیں
segments.summary_en: Asks children which calendar their birthday and Eid follow, ties the solar calendar to the school year and national days and the Hijri calendar to Eid and Muharram, then has them compare Ramadan's start date last year and this year.

segments.title_en: Group table: five events in both calendars
segments.title_ur: گروپ کام: پانچ واقعات دونوں کیلنڈروں میں
segments.summary_en: Groups make a table of five events (birthday, Eid ul Fitr, Pakistan Day, Eid ul Azha, sports day) with dates in both calendars and discuss why Eid's solar date changes each year.

modules.title: 2D shapes
modules.teacher_line_en: Shapes off the page: have children find each 2D shape in their own classroom
modules.teacher_line_ur: شکلیں کتاب سے باہر: بچے ہر شکل اپنی کلاس روم کی چیزوں میں خود ڈھونڈیں
modules.summary_en: The teacher draws a circle, square, triangle and rectangle on the board, has children say each name, and states the features (a circle has no sides; a square has 4 equal sides and 4 corners; a triangle 3 sides and 3 corners; a rectangle 4 sides with opposite sides equal). Then shapes are matched to objects in the classroom and school (clock dial, floor tile, flag, door, notebook cover) and children build a shape-to-object list on the board.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ دائرہ، مربع، مثلث اور مستطیل کی پہچان اور خصوصیات کیسے دہرائیں اور ہر شکل کو کلاس روم کی اصل چیزوں سے جوڑ کر بچوں سے فہرست کیسے بنوائیں۔
symptoms: shape names chanted in chorus with no object from the room pointed to
sides and corners never counted or named, only the shape name
no recall of shapes learned earlier before new ones
children never find or list shapes around them
modules.not_for: Teachers whose lesson is not on 2D shapes, or who teach Grade 4 and above.

segments.title_en: Recall 2D shapes, then find each one in the classroom
segments.title_ur: دو جہتی شکلیں یاد کریں، پھر ہر شکل کلاس روم میں ڈھونڈیں
segments.summary_en: The teacher draws circle, square, triangle and rectangle, children name each and its sides and corners; then each shape is matched to a real object (clock dial, floor tile, flag, door) and written next to it on the board, a list children can build themselves.

modules.title: Assessment tools
modules.teacher_line_en: Before a new topic, two quick questions show what the class already knows
modules.teacher_line_ur: نیا سبق شروع کرنے سے پہلے دو سادہ سوال بتا دیتے ہیں کہ بچے پہلے سے کیا جانتے ہیں
modules.summary_en: A trainer defines diagnostic, formative and summative assessment and argues for an ungraded diagnostic test at the start of a new class or course, listing sources: textbook tests, downloadable tests from foreign publishers, anonymous questionnaires and teacher-made tests. The only classroom example is two fraction questions (is 1/2 or 1/4 bigger? is 2/4 equal to 1/2?) asked before starting fractions.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں تشخیصی، تشکیلی اور مجموعی جائزے کی تعریف اور نئے سال کے آغاز پر بغیر نمبر والے تشخیصی ٹیسٹ کے ذرائع بتائے گئے ہیں۔
symptoms: a new topic starts with no check of what children already know
teacher re-teaches from zero assuming last year's skills are missing (or present) without checking
modules.not_for: Not a next-step clip for any classroom report: definitions and test sources only; send module 21 for the diagnostic-question move.

segments.title_en: Three kinds of assessment; why diagnose
segments.title_ur: جائزے کی تین اقسام اور تشخیصی جائزہ کیوں
segments.summary_en: Definitions of diagnostic, formative and summative assessment, and why a teacher receiving a new Grade 6 class should not assume all Grade 5 skills are in place.

segments.title_en: When to run a diagnostic and where to find one
segments.title_ur: تشخیصی ٹیسٹ کب لیں اور کہاں سے لیں
segments.summary_en: Diagnostics belong at the start of a class or course, ungraded and never used against students; sources are textbook tests, downloadable publisher tests and anonymous quick questionnaires.

segments.title_en: Teacher-made diagnostic: two fraction questions
segments.title_ur: اپنا تشخیصی سوال: کسور کے دو سوال
segments.summary_en: Teacher-made diagnostics take effort; the example is asking which is bigger, 1/2 or 1/4, and whether 2/4 equals 1/2 before starting fractions. Ends by deferring details to the next video.

modules.title: Pre-Assessment
modules.teacher_line_en: Before a new topic, 3 quick board questions show what children already know
modules.teacher_line_ur: نیا سبق شروع کرنے سے پہلے بورڈ پر 3 سوال: بچے پہلے سے کیا جانتے ہیں؟
modules.summary_en: The presenter explains pre-assessment: a short, ungraded check of 3-5 questions before a new topic to find out what children already know. Three zero-prep formats are shown (a 3-question quick quiz like 1+3, 2+5, 10+7; a word bank of 5-6 words on the board; a matching activity of plant parts and functions), then a Grade 3 subtraction example where the teacher writes 15-5, 20-8, 12-12 and children write answers fast. Teachers learn to make it a routine at the start of each lesson and use the results to plan.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ نیا سبق شروع کرنے سے پہلے 3 سے 5 سوالوں کی چھوٹی سی جانچ سے کیسے پتہ لگائیں کہ بچے پہلے سے کیا جانتے ہیں۔
symptoms: lesson opens with 'aaj hum parhenge' and goes straight into new explanation
no question about the previous lesson or the topic's basics before teaching
no moment where every child writes a quick answer before the new content
teacher re-explains things children already answer instantly
modules.not_for: Teachers whose lessons already open with a recall or quick check; it is about the start of a lesson, not mid-lesson feedback.

segments.title_en: Intro: three types of assessment
segments.title_ur: تعارف: جانچ کی تین اقسام
segments.summary_en: Greeting and definitions of diagnostic, formative and summative assessment.

segments.title_en: What a pre-assessment is and why
segments.title_ur: پری اسیسمنٹ کیا ہے اور کیوں
segments.summary_en: A short ungraded check of 3-5 questions before the topic (e.g. 'what is the difference between day and night?' before the solar system); it shows readiness, lets you plan for strong and struggling learners, and saves time.

segments.title_en: Three zero-prep pre-checks, then a Grade 3 example
segments.title_ur: بغیر تیاری کے تین ابتدائی جانچ کے طریقے اور جماعت سوم کی مثال
segments.summary_en: Three under-5-minute pre-checks (a 3-question quiz, a word bank, a matching activity), then before a subtraction lesson the teacher writes 15-5, 20-8, 12-12 on the board, children answer fast, and the teacher uses who got them wrong to plan support.

modules.title: Quick checks for understanding
modules.teacher_line_en: Who really understood? Thumbs, exit slips and 1-line summaries, then re-teach or move on
modules.teacher_line_ur: کس کو سمجھ آئی؟ انگوٹھے کا اشارہ، ایگزٹ سلپ، ایک جملہ؛ پھر دوبارہ سمجھائیں یا آگے بڑھیں
modules.summary_en: A presenter explains quick checks for understanding as fast, informal formative checks and runs through four of them: thumbs up / down / sideways after 'kya sab ko samajh aaya?', an exit slip 'write one thing you learned today', a one-word or one-sentence summary (fractions: 'half is one part out of two'), and a hand signal. The teacher learns when to use them (mid-lesson, end of lesson, after group work so not only the group leader understood) and what to do next: if 4 of 10 children show thumbs down in 2-digit addition, revise the concept for 5 minutes; if most understood, move on to harder practice.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ انگوٹھے کے اشارے، ایگزٹ سلپ اور ایک جملے کے خلاصے سے سبق کے دوران فوراً جانچیں کہ بچوں کو سمجھ آئی یا نہیں، اور نتیجے کے مطابق دوبارہ سمجھائیں یا آگے بڑھیں۔
symptoms: teacher asks 'samajh aa gaya?' and accepts a chorus 'jee' with no individual signal
no thumbs, slip, or one-line summary from students anywhere in the lesson
lesson ends with no student saying or writing what they learned
teacher moves to the next exercise without checking whether the group work was understood by each child
modules.not_for: Teachers who already run quick checks and need a new way to re-explain; it lists checks with a presenter and shows no classroom footage.

segments.title_en: Intro: what a quick check is
segments.title_ur: تعارف: فوری جانچ کیا ہے
segments.summary_en: Greeting, link to pre-assessment and diagnostic assessment, and a definition: a fast, non-exam formative check that tells the teacher how far students understood and where they struggle.

segments.title_en: Four quick checks: thumbs, exit slip, one-line summary, signals
segments.title_ur: چار فوری جانچیں: انگوٹھا، ایگزٹ سلپ، ایک جملے کا خلاصہ، اشارے
segments.summary_en: Shows the exact words for thumbs up / down / sideways, an end-of-class slip 'write one thing you learned today', a one-word or one-sentence summary (fractions: 'half is one part out of two'), and a hand signal when the idea is clear.

segments.title_en: When to check and what to do with the result
segments.title_ur: کب جانچیں اور نتیجے کے بعد کیا کریں
segments.summary_en: Use checks mid-lesson, at the end and after group work; in 2-digit addition, if 4 of 10 show thumbs down, revise the concept for 5 minutes, re-teach if most are confused, give harder practice if most understood.

modules.title: Positive verbal feedback
modules.teacher_line_en: Swap 'good job' for praise that names what went well plus one next step
modules.teacher_line_ur: «گڈ جاب» کی جگہ بتائیں کیا اچھا ہوا اور اگلی بار کیا بہتر کریں
modules.summary_en: A presenter contrasts a bare 'good job' with specific feedback such as 'Great job, you read the passage loud and clear; if you pause a little more at full stops it will be even better.' The teacher learns a two-part formula: praise the effort or achievement by naming exactly what was done well, then add one simple next-step suggestion, always starting with the positive (e.g. 'Your sentences are very good; focus a little on spelling').
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ سیکھیں گے کہ صرف «شاباش» کہنے کے بجائے بچے کو بتائیں کہ کیا اچھا کیا اور اگلی بار کیا بہتر کرے۔
symptoms: teacher responds to answers only with 'shabash', 'good', 'theek hai' or 'ghalat'
teacher repeats the correct answer instead of saying what the student did well
no 'next time try…' or 'agli dafa…' suggestion after checking a student's work
mistakes are pointed out with no praise of what was right first
modules.not_for: Teachers who already give specific praise plus a next step; it is a short talk with spoken examples and no classroom footage.

segments.title_en: Why 'good job' is not enough: a specific example
segments.title_ur: صرف «گڈ جاب» کافی کیوں نہیں: مخصوص فیڈبیک کی مثال
segments.summary_en: Explains that 'theek hai' or 'ghalat' leaves children unsure what they did well, then rewrites 'good job' as specific praise for reading loud and clear plus a tip to pause at full stops.

segments.title_en: Two parts: name what went well, then one next step
segments.title_ur: دو حصے: اچھائی کا نام لیں، پھر اگلا قدم بتائیں
segments.summary_en: Gives the two-part formula (praise effort and achievement, then a simple suggestion) with examples for maths sums, neat writing, adding detail, quoting one more sentence from the text, and spelling, always starting with the positive.

segments.title_en: Why starting positive works; try it today
segments.title_ur: مثبت بات سے آغاز کیوں مؤثر ہے؛ آج آزمائیں
segments.summary_en: Explains that people listen better when feedback starts with praise, asks the teacher to try it in class today, and signs off.

modules.title: Checklist
modules.teacher_line_en: Know by the end of class which child is stuck on which skill, with one tick-sheet
modules.teacher_line_ur: ایک چیک لسٹ سے کلاس کے آخر تک جانیں کہ کون سا بچہ کس سکل پر اٹکا ہے
modules.summary_en: A trainer shows a one-page skills checklist: children's names down the side, skills across the top (circle, square, triangle, rectangle for a Grade 2 shapes lesson), and a tick or cross the teacher marks while watching the children do an activity. By the end of the lesson the sheet shows who needs more practice on which shape, so the teacher can decide between revision and a new concept; a thumbs-up/down check ('who can recognise a circle?') feeds the same list.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ سرگرمی کے دوران ایک سادہ چیک لسٹ پر ٹک یا کراس لگا کر ہر بچے کی سیکھنے کی پیش رفت کیسے دیکھیں اور اگلا قدم کیسے طے کریں۔
symptoms: teacher asks 'samajh aa gaya?' and moves on after a choral 'jee'
no individual child is checked or named during the activity; teacher only watches the whole class
lesson ends with no record or mention of who has or has not got the skill
next lesson starts a new concept with no reference to who struggled last time
modules.not_for: Teachers whose need is questioning or feedback in the moment; this is about recording and tracking each child's progress, not about what to say to them.

segments.title_en: Why track each child's progress
segments.title_ur: ہر بچے کی پیش رفت کیوں ٹریک کریں
segments.summary_en: Names the doubt every teacher has (are they really learning, who is left behind) and why memory or guesswork lets children slip through.

segments.title_en: Tick-sheet checklist: a Grade 2 shapes example
segments.title_ur: ٹک والی چیک لسٹ: گریڈ 2 شیپس کی مثال
segments.summary_en: Shows the checklist and progress chart, then fills a real one for a Grade 2 shapes lesson (tick for circle and square, cross for triangle) by observing the activity, and uses it to choose revision or a new concept next time.

segments.title_en: Thumbs up/down straight into the checklist
segments.title_ur: تھمز اپ/ڈاؤن سے فوراً چیک لسٹ میں نوٹ
segments.summary_en: Places the checklist in assessment for learning: ask 'who can recognise a circle?', children show thumbs up or down, and the teacher notes names on the list in one or two minutes.

modules.title: How to use youtube for classrooms
modules.teacher_line_en: Show a short phone video the right way: what to watch for before, questions after
modules.teacher_line_ur: فون پر مختصر ویڈیو صحیح طریقے سے دکھائیں: پہلے بتائیں کیا دیکھنا ہے، بعد میں سوال
modules.summary_en: The trainer shows how to use a short YouTube video from a phone when children are stuck on a concept: search with topic plus grade ('fractions grade 2'), download at home for offline use, and pick a video by three checks (clear simple language, visuals at the children's level, short and relevant). The classroom move: tell children what to watch for before playing, pause to re-explain key points, and ask afterwards 'What did you learn? Which example was clearest?'
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ سیکھیں گے کہ فون پر یوٹیوب سے جماعت کے مطابق مختصر ویڈیو کیسے ڈھونڈیں، گھر سے ڈاؤن لوڈ کریں، اور کلاس میں دکھانے سے پہلے بتائیں کہ کیا دیکھنا ہے اور بعد میں سوال پوچھیں۔
symptoms: teacher repeats the same explanation when children stay confused and uses no picture or video
teacher mentions a phone or video but plays it with no task before and no question after
children are never asked what they learned from material shown to them
modules.not_for: Teachers with no smartphone or download access, or whose next step is about questioning or behaviour rather than using a video in class. Ruled not recommendable by m-catalog (18:3xZ): app how-to that needs a device and data (RUBRIC ⛔7 lists "how to use YouTube"); consistent with 26, 124, 127.

segments.title_en: Why a short video can help
segments.title_ur: مختصر ویڈیو کیوں مددگار ہے
segments.summary_en: Intro: when children do not understand a concept a short video can help; it frames this with 'learning styles' (a myth, not a move) and notes a phone is enough without a projector.

segments.title_en: Search by grade, plan questions, use offline
segments.title_ur: جماعت کے ساتھ تلاش، سوالات کی تیاری، آف لائن استعمال
segments.summary_en: Three skills: search with topic plus grade ('fractions grade 2'), give guiding questions before, pause mid-video to re-explain, ask reflective questions after, and download at home for weak internet.

segments.title_en: Finding a video and the three checks for choosing it
segments.title_ur: ویڈیو تلاش کرنا اور انتخاب کی تین باتیں
segments.summary_en: How to open YouTube, search, play/pause; then check a video for clear simple language, visuals at the children's level, and short relevant length.

segments.title_en: Before and after the video: what to watch, what you learned
segments.title_ur: ویڈیو سے پہلے اور بعد: کیا دیکھنا ہے، کیا سیکھا
segments.summary_en: Do not just press play: tell children what to watch for ('see how the shapes are explained'), then ask 'What did you learn? Which example was clearest?'; closing remarks.

modules.title: How to find educational resources online
modules.teacher_line_en: Find a ready worksheet online in minutes, and check it fits your grade before printing
modules.teacher_line_ur: چند منٹ میں انٹرنیٹ سے ورک شیٹ ڈھونڈیں اور پرنٹ سے پہلے جانچیں کہ جماعت کے مطابق ہے
modules.summary_en: A presenter walks through a browser search for 'Grade 2 Solar System Worksheet': write specific keywords, prefer educational or school websites, open a subject category, download the PDF and print it for class. It closes with three quality checks before printing: is the source educational, does the sheet match the subject and grade, and will its examples and questions be easy for your children and build the concept.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں دکھایا گیا ہے کہ آپ انٹرنیٹ پر درست الفاظ لکھ کر تعلیمی ویب سائٹ سے اپنی جماعت اور مضمون کے مطابق ورک شیٹ کیسے ڈھونڈیں، جانچیں اور ڈاؤن لوڈ کریں۔
symptoms: teacher says there is no worksheet or practice sheet, so children only copy from the board
whole lesson is copying exercises from the book with no prepared task sheet
modules.not_for: Not a next-step clip for any classroom report: a web-search and download how-to with no classroom move; skip for teachers without internet or a printer.

segments.title_en: Intro and searching with clear keywords
segments.title_ur: تعارف اور واضح الفاظ سے تلاش
segments.summary_en: Greeting, why worksheets take time, then typing a specific search such as 'Grade 2 Solar System Worksheet' because clear keywords give relevant results.

segments.title_en: Choose an educational site and download
segments.title_ur: تعلیمی ویب سائٹ چنیں اور ڈاؤن لوڈ کریں
segments.summary_en: Check which website a link belongs to, prefer educational ones, open a subject category, pick the grade and download the PDF to print and distribute.

segments.title_en: Three checks before you print a worksheet
segments.title_ur: ورک شیٹ پرنٹ کرنے سے پہلے تین جانچیں
segments.summary_en: Use educational sources, match the sheet to subject and grade, and ask whether its examples will be easy for your children and its questions will build the concept; ends with a 'next video' outro.

modules.title: How to make simple slides
modules.teacher_line_en: Make 3-5 simple lesson slides with a picture and one line each in PowerPoint
modules.teacher_line_ur: پاورپوائنٹ میں تصویر اور ایک لائن والی 3 سے 5 سادہ سلائیڈز بنانا سیکھیں
modules.summary_en: A screen walkthrough of Google Slides / PowerPoint: the menu bar, the slides panel and three key buttons (Insert > Text box, Insert > Image, Themes/Layout), then building a 'My lesson on plants' deck with 'Plants need sunlight and water' plus a plant picture saved from a Google search. Teachers learn to keep 3-5 slides with one small picture and 1-2 short points each, and to pause on each slide in slideshow mode to explain and ask the class questions.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ گوگل سلائیڈز یا پاورپوائنٹ میں تصویر اور ایک دو مختصر نکات والی 3 سے 5 سادہ سلائیڈز کیسے بنائیں اور کلاس میں ہر سلائیڈ پر رک کر سوال کیسے پوچھیں۔
symptoms: teacher writes long notes on the board for most of the period while the class waits ('likh lo')
teacher mentions a projector or LCD in the room but the lesson uses only the board
no picture, chart or object is shown for a concept that is visual (plants, parts of the body)
modules.not_for: Not a next-step clip for a classroom report: a software how-to that needs a computer and a projector; skip for teachers without them.

segments.title_en: Intro and the PowerPoint screen
segments.title_ur: تعارف اور پاورپوائنٹ کی اسکرین
segments.summary_en: Greeting, why writing everything on the board tires the teacher and bores students, then the menu bar, slides panel and three key buttons: Insert Text box, Insert Image, Themes/Layout.

segments.title_en: Build a slide and add a picture
segments.title_ur: سلائیڈ بنائیں اور تصویر لگائیں
segments.summary_en: A title slide 'My lesson on plants', a new slide with the text 'Plants need sunlight and water', then searching 'Plant pictures for classroom', saving the image and inserting it via Insert > Image > Upload from computer.

segments.title_en: A 3-slide deck and presenting it
segments.title_ur: تین سلائیڈز کا سیٹ اور کلاس میں دکھانا
segments.summary_en: Keep 3-5 slides, each with one small picture and 1-2 short points (title; sunlight + image; water + image), then present in slideshow mode, pausing on each slide to explain and ask questions.

modules.title: Reflective Journaling
modules.teacher_line_en: 5 minutes a day: What? So what? Now what? A simple journal to improve tomorrow's lesson
modules.teacher_line_ur: روزانہ پانچ منٹ: کیا ہوا؟ مطلب کیا؟ اب کیا؟ کل کے سبق کو بہتر بنانے کا آسان طریقہ
modules.summary_en: A presenter introduces a daily 5-minute reflective journal built on three prompts: What (what happened), So what (what it means), Now what (what I will do tomorrow). The worked example: two students did not join the group activity, so they need more guidance, so tomorrow the teacher will assign clear roles before the activity starts; viewers are then asked to pick one moment from today and write the three lines in a notebook.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ روزانہ پانچ منٹ میں 'کیا ہوا، اس کا مطلب کیا ہے، کل کیا کروں گا' لکھ کر اپنی تدریس کیسے بہتر کریں۔
symptoms: the same problem (e.g. some children not joining group work) recurs across several of the teacher's lessons with no change in approach
teacher's post-lesson comments describe what happened but name no change for the next lesson
teacher has no stated plan or adjustment carried over from a previous lesson
modules.not_for: Teachers whose lesson shows a specific classroom move missing; this is a professional habit, not a classroom technique, so send a move video instead.

segments.title_en: What / So what / Now what: a 5-minute daily reflection
segments.title_ur: کیا ہوا / مطلب کیا / اب کیا: روزانہ پانچ منٹ کی ریفلیکشن
segments.summary_en: Explains the three-prompt cycle, models it on a group activity where two students did not take part (fix: assign clear roles tomorrow), then asks viewers to write their own three lines; short greeting and recap included.
segments.recommendable_reason: panel_veto: not_a_move (a teacher's own reflection habit, no classroom move; v6 Z150 ⛔2, ped/vetoes.json module 28, COS 20261024T002603 1a)

modules.title: Ethical responsibilities and code of conduct
modules.teacher_line_en: Handle a cheating student fairly, calmly and without shaming, per the code of conduct
modules.teacher_line_ur: نقل کرنے والے بچے کو سختی یا شرمندگی کے بغیر انصاف سے کیسے سنبھالیں
modules.summary_en: A presenter lists five duties in a teacher's code of conduct: integrity, fairness to every child whatever their background, gender or level, keeping students' personal matters confidential, respect towards students, parents and colleagues, and commitment to duty. A worked dilemma follows: a student tries to cheat in a class test, and the teacher stops it calmly, explains why it is wrong without public harshness, involves parents and the counsellor later, and considers a class discussion on why honesty matters. The video ends by asking teachers to recall one ethical situation of their own and ask what they would do better now.
modules.summary_ur: آپ ٹیچر کے ضابطۂ اخلاق کی پانچ ذمہ داریاں اور امتحان میں نقل کے ایک واقعے کو انصاف اور عزت سے سنبھالنے کی مثال دیکھیں گے۔
symptoms: teacher publicly shames a student caught copying or cheating ('sab dekho isne nakal ki')
teacher compares children by family background or calls some 'nalaiq' in front of the class
teacher discusses a child's private home matter aloud in class
modules.not_for: Any teacher whose report is about a classroom teaching move (questioning, closure, feedback); this is an ethics-code talk with nothing to try in tomorrow's lesson.

segments.title_en: Five duties in a teacher's code of conduct
segments.title_ur: ٹیچر کے ضابطۂ اخلاق کی پانچ ذمہ داریاں
segments.summary_en: Lists integrity, fairness to every student, confidentiality of students' personal matters, professional respect, and commitment to duty.

segments.title_en: Dilemma: a student cheats in a class test
segments.title_ur: مثال: کلاس ٹیسٹ میں بچہ نقل کرتا ہے
segments.summary_en: The teacher neither ignores nor punishes harshly: stops the cheating, calmly explains why it is wrong, then involves parents and the counsellor; punishment alone would only frighten the child.

segments.title_en: Turn the incident into learning, then reflect
segments.title_ur: واقعے کو سیکھنے کا موقع بنائیں اور خود احتسابی کریں
segments.summary_en: Suggests a class discussion on why honesty matters in exams, then asks teachers to recall one ethical situation of their own and what they would do better today.

modules.title: Phonic strategies part 1
modules.teacher_line_en: Children say s-a-t but not 'sat'? Try clap-and-blend and robot voice tomorrow
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے آوازیں الگ الگ بولتے ہیں مگر لفظ نہیں بنا پاتے؟ تالی اور روبوٹ آواز آزمائیں
modules.summary_en: A trainer lays out an English phonics progression for children who can say single sounds but cannot join them: start with s-a-t-p-i-n, teach each sound by hearing, saying, air-writing and an action, then blend and then digraphs (sh, ch, th). The teacher sees zero-material blending routines with the exact teacher and class lines (clap-and-blend, robot voice to smooth voice, a blend chain of letters on the board including nonsense words) and digraph games ending in decodable reading ('The ship is in the shop').
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ سیکھیں گے کہ انگریزی کی آوازیں سکھانے کے بعد تالی، روبوٹ آواز اور بورڈ پر حروف کی زنجیر سے بچوں کو آوازیں ملا کر لفظ بنانا کیسے سکھائیں۔
symptoms: children say letter sounds one at a time and never produce the whole word
teacher uses letter names (ay, bee, see) instead of sounds when reading words
class repeats whole words after the teacher in chorus with no blending step
sh/ch/th words read letter by letter
modules.not_for: Not for maths, science or Urdu lessons, nor for Grade 4+ teachers whose children already decode; it teaches early English phonics only.

segments.title_en: Sounds, then blends, then digraphs
segments.title_ur: پہلے آوازیں، پھر ملانا، پھر دو حرفی آوازیں
segments.summary_en: The trainer names the problem (children know single sounds but get confused joining them) and the order to teach: individual sounds starting from s-a-t-p-i-n, then blends, then digraphs.

segments.title_en: Hear it, say it, air-write it
segments.title_ur: سنیں، بولیں، ہوا میں لکھیں
segments.summary_en: Teacher says 'sss' and children repeat three times; random children are called on to give a letter's sound; the letter is written on the board and traced in the air with a chant while saying the sound.

segments.title_en: An action for every sound
segments.title_ur: ہر آواز کے ساتھ ایک اشارہ
segments.summary_en: Each sound gets a gesture (snake hand for s, bubble-blowing for p, head scratch, nose hold), and the trainer then introduces blending s-a-t, p-i-n.

segments.title_en: Clap-and-blend, robot voice, blend chain
segments.title_ur: تالی سے ملانا، روبوٹ آواز، حروف کی زنجیر
segments.summary_en: Teacher says each sound with a clap and the class says the whole word with one clap; teacher speaks in a robot voice and children answer in a smooth voice; children pick three letters from a board chain to build words, nonsense words included, to practise blending.

segments.title_en: Digraphs: sort, blend game, decodable sentence
segments.title_ur: دو حرفی آوازیں: پہچان کا کھیل اور جملہ پڑھنا
segments.summary_en: Two letters making one sound ('best friends'): a picture listening sort for sh, a sound-blend game ('sh + op = shop'), word building, then the decodable sentence 'The ship is in the shop' with partners underlining digraphs; the board and notebooks are enough.

segments.title_en: Recap of the progression
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Recap of sounds, blends and digraphs and a sign-off.

modules.title: Blending and Segmenting
modules.teacher_line_en: Say, tap, blend: children break 'cat' into sounds and join them back
modules.teacher_line_ur: Say, tap, blend: بچے 'cat' کو آوازوں میں توڑیں اور پھر جوڑیں
modules.summary_en: A teacher runs short oral phonics games with children: 'Say, Tap and Blend' (a child names the picture 'cat', the class says each sound slowly after the teacher, then blends it back to 'cat'), a 'sound train' where three children each hold one sound of 'bat' and the class blends them, and matching sounds to pictures ('bus'). Teachers learn to break short classroom words (bag, mat, cup, pen) into sounds and join them again every day, with nothing to prepare.
modules.summary_ur: آپ دیکھیں گے کہ 'cat' اور 'bus' جیسے چھوٹے الفاظ کو آوازوں میں توڑ کر اور پھر جوڑ کر بچوں کو پڑھنا کیسے سکھایا جائے۔
symptoms: children name letters (bee, ay, tee) but never say the sounds or blend them into a word
teacher reads each word and the class repeats the whole word only
spelling practised by reciting letter names with no breaking of the word into sounds
all sound work is chorus; no child ever says one sound alone
modules.not_for: Maths, science or Grade 4+ teachers, and Urdu-only teachers without on-screen support; it is spoken in English for early English reading.

segments.title_en: Intro: segmenting and blending
segments.title_ur: تعارف: آوازوں کو توڑنا اور جوڑنا
segments.summary_en: Greeting; phoneme, segmentation and blending defined; the 'Say, Tap and Blend' activity is named.

segments.title_en: Say, tap and blend 'cat'
segments.title_ur: 'cat' کو بولیں، تھپتھپائیں اور جوڑیں
segments.summary_en: A child names the picture, the class says the sounds of 'cat' slowly after the teacher, then blends them back into the word.

segments.title_en: Sound train: blend 'bat'
segments.title_ur: ساؤنڈ ٹرین: 'bat' جوڑیں
segments.summary_en: Three children are carriages of a sound train and each says one sound when pointed to; the class blends them into 'bat'. Use pen, jug, cup, bus.

segments.title_en: Match sounds to pictures
segments.title_ur: آوازوں کو تصویروں سے ملائیں
segments.summary_en: The teacher says the sounds of 'bus', children find the picture and say the word; then segment classroom objects like mat, cup, bag.

segments.title_en: Stretch 'sun'; keep it daily
segments.title_ur: 'sun' کو کھینچ کر بولیں؛ روزانہ مشق
segments.summary_en: Children stretch and then say 'sun' together; tips to keep it short, fun and daily with classroom words. Ends with a recap.

modules.title: Key components of phonological awareness
modules.teacher_line_en: Rhyme, syllables, onset-rime, phonemes: one quick class game for each
modules.teacher_line_ur: رائم، سلیبل، آن سیٹ رائم، فونیم: ہر ایک کے لیے کلاس کی ایک آسان سرگرمی
modules.summary_en: A subject-knowledge primer for English reading teachers: the four parts of phonological awareness, each with a quick class activity: a rhyme game (the teacher says a word, children answer with a rhyming word), clapping syllables (man-go, Pak-i-stan), writing '-at' on the board and asking which sound in front makes a word (cat, bat, sat), and finger-tapping the phonemes of 'sit'. It then explains vowels as open sounds and consonants as blocked sounds, and building CVC words (c-a-t).
modules.summary_ur: آپ انگلش ریڈنگ کے لیے رائمنگ، سلیبل، آن سیٹ رائم، فونیم اور سی وی سی الفاظ کو سمجھیں گے اور ہر ایک کے لیے کلاس کی ایک آسان سرگرمی دیکھیں گے۔
symptoms: teacher names letters ('bee', 'see') instead of their sounds in an English reading lesson
CVC words taught by whole-word repetition with no sound-by-sound breaking
no rhyme, clapping or word-family activity in a Grade 1-2 English lesson
teacher calls sounds 'syllables' or mixes up vowels and consonants
modules.not_for: Maths, science or Grade 4+ teachers, and teachers whose reading lessons already use sound-level games; it is teacher knowledge, not a demonstration.

segments.title_en: Subject knowledge as a superpower; phonics vs phonological awareness
segments.title_ur: مضمون کا علم بطور سپر پاور؛ فونکس اور فونولوجیکل اویرنس
segments.summary_en: Frames subject knowledge as the teacher's superpower, defines phonics as letter sounds blended into words (c-a-t), and calls phonological awareness an umbrella with four components.

segments.title_en: Rhyming game and clapping syllables
segments.title_ur: رائمنگ گیم اور تالی سے سلیبل گننا
segments.summary_en: Rhymes end on the same sound (cat/bat); play a game where the teacher says a word and children answer with a rhyme. Syllables are clapped: man-go is two claps, Pak-i-stan three.

segments.title_en: Onset-rime on the board and finger-tapping phonemes
segments.title_ur: بورڈ پر آن سیٹ رائم اور انگلیوں سے فونیم گننا
segments.summary_en: Write '-at' on the board and ask which sound in front makes a word; if children cannot answer, give cat, bat, sat and write them. Then break 'sit' into three phonemes with finger tapping, before moving to blending and segmenting.

segments.title_en: Vowels as open sounds, consonants as blocked sounds
segments.title_ur: واولز کھلی آوازیں، کانسوننٹس رکی ہوئی آوازیں
segments.summary_en: Explains the five vowels as open sounds with the mouth open (a as in apple, o as in orange) and the other 21 letters as consonants where tongue, mouth and lips block the air (b as in ball).

segments.title_en: Building CVC words: c-a-t
segments.title_ur: سی وی سی الفاظ بنانا: ک-ا-ٹ
segments.summary_en: Once vowels and consonants are clear, build consonant-vowel-consonant words by adding a vowel and a consonant to a starting sound (c + a + t = cat); closes the module.

modules.title: Phonological awareness
modules.teacher_line_en: Five 1-minute sound games (rhyme, clap syllables, word families) for weak readers
modules.teacher_line_ur: کمزور پڑھنے والوں کے لیے آواز کے پانچ ایک منٹ والے کھیل: قافیہ، تالی، ورڈ فیملی
modules.summary_en: A presenter explains three oral sound activities for struggling early readers: rhyming (cat, hat, mat), counting syllables by clapping beats (ap-ple, ba-na-na, wa-ter-mel-on) and word families (-at, -ig). They then run them to camera as quick zero-prep games: rhyme with 'sun', clap 'table', build the -ig family, find classroom objects that start with /b/, blend three sounds into 'cat'.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں ہم قافیہ الفاظ، تالی سے سلیبل گننے اور ورڈ فیملی جیسی آسان زبانی سرگرمیاں دکھائی گئی ہیں جو کمزور پڑھنے والے بچوں کی آوازوں کی پہچان مضبوط کرتی ہیں۔
symptoms: Grade 1-2 English lesson where struggling readers are asked to read whole words with no sound work first
teacher spells words only by letter names ('c-a-t') and never says the sounds
no rhyme, clapping or sound game anywhere in an early-reading lesson
children read the textbook line in chorus after the teacher with no blending of sounds
modules.not_for: Teachers of Grade 4 and above or of maths, science, grammar or comprehension lessons; it is early-reading sound work only.

segments.title_en: Why weak readers need sound work; rhyming
segments.title_ur: کمزور پڑھنے والوں کو آوازوں کی مشق کیوں چاہیے؛ قافیہ
segments.summary_en: Greeting: children who do not know letter sounds cannot recognise words; three activities are promised (rhyming, syllable counting, word families) and rhyming is introduced with cat, hat, mat.

segments.title_en: Clap the beats: one- to four-syllable words
segments.title_ur: تالی سے بیٹس گنیں: ایک سے چار سلیبل والے الفاظ
segments.summary_en: A syllable is one beat you can count on fingers or clap; models breaking cat, ap-ple, pa-per, ba-na-na, com-pu-ter and wa-ter-mel-on and asking 'how many beats?'.

segments.title_en: Word families and why these three games build reading
segments.title_ur: ورڈ فیملی اور یہ تین سرگرمیاں پڑھائی کیسے مضبوط کرتی ہیں
segments.summary_en: Word families are words with the same ending (cat, hat, mat, sat, rat); rhyming builds sound awareness, syllable counting builds segmenting, word families build pattern recognition for new words.

segments.title_en: Five quick sound games to run tomorrow
segments.title_ur: کل کلاس میں کروانے والے آواز کے پانچ فوری کھیل
segments.summary_en: Runs the games to camera: rhyme with 'sun' (bun, run), clap 'ta-ble', build the -ig family, find classroom objects starting with /b/ (book, bag, board), blend three sounds into 'cat'; add them to daily lessons.

modules.title: Grammar elements
modules.teacher_line_en: Teach nouns, verbs and adjectives from one real sentence plus a group word sort
modules.teacher_line_ur: ایک جملے اور گروپ میں الفاظ چھانٹنے سے اسم، فعل اور صفت سکھائیں
