modules.summary_en: A trainer defines five parts of speech (noun, verb, adjective, pronoun, preposition), then labels each word in 'Ali is reading a big book in the library' and has viewers try 'She plays with the red ball on the ground'. The classroom activity: write 8-10 mixed words on the board, small groups sort them into the five categories, one child per group writes the answer on the board, and the class corrects it together, using children's names and classroom objects for examples.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ انگریزی گرامر کے پانچ حصے ایک جملے اور گروپ میں الفاظ چھانٹنے کی سرگرمی سے کیسے پڑھائیں۔
symptoms: grammar lesson is definitions read out then a textbook fill-in exercise
children label parts of speech wrongly and the teacher repeats the definition
no example sentence uses children's names or classroom objects
children only copy; nobody sorts words or builds a sentence
modules.not_for: Teachers of Urdu, maths or reading-fluency lessons; it is for an English lesson on parts of speech only.

segments.title_en: Five parts of speech in one line each
segments.title_ur: گرامر کے پانچ حصے، ہر ایک کی مختصر تعریف
segments.summary_en: Names the problem of children's incomplete sentences and gives a one-line meaning for noun, verb, adjective, pronoun and preposition.

segments.title_en: Label every word in a real sentence
segments.title_ur: ایک جملے کے ہر لفظ کی پہچان
segments.summary_en: Breaks down 'Ali is reading a big book in the library', saying why each word is a noun, verb, adjective or preposition and how 'he' becomes a pronoun, then a second sentence for viewers to try.

segments.title_en: Group sort: mixed words into five categories
segments.title_ur: گروپ سرگرمی: الفاظ کو پانچ قسموں میں چھانٹیں
segments.summary_en: Write 8-10 mixed words on the board; small groups sort them by part of speech in notebooks, one child per group writes the answer on the board and the class corrects it, using children's names and classroom objects.

modules.title: Echo Reading
modules.teacher_line_en: Children read word by word with no expression? Try echo reading, one sentence at a time
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے اٹک اٹک کر بغیر اظہار پڑھتے ہیں؟ ایکو ریڈنگ آزمائیں، ایک ایک جملہ
modules.summary_en: The trainer explains that phonics teaches words but fluency (pausing at punctuation, intonation, expression) is what lets children understand a text, then defines echo reading: the teacher reads one sentence with expression, children repeat it exactly, pointing at each word so they read rather than parrot. A short English story (Ali and Tariq) is echo-read on screen, then a real classroom clip shows choral reading ('finger on first word', reading slowly together) and stopping to break a hard word into chunks (per-fect-ly) and find it again in the story.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ ایکو ریڈنگ میں ٹیچر ایک جملہ اظہار کے ساتھ پڑھتے ہیں اور بچے انگلی رکھ کر وہی جملہ دہراتے ہیں، اور پوری کلاس مل کر پڑھتے ہوئے مشکل لفظ کو حصوں میں توڑ کر کیسے پڑھیں۔
symptoms: children read aloud word by word, flat, ignoring full stops and question marks
teacher reads the whole passage and children only listen, or children chorus-recite without looking at the text
no pointing at words while reading; children repeat from memory
when a child stumbles on a long word the teacher just says it for them
modules.not_for: Teachers whose class cannot yet decode single words (start with phonics), or teachers of maths/science lessons.

segments.title_en: Is reading only decoding words?
segments.title_ur: کیا پڑھنا صرف الفاظ پہچاننا ہے؟
segments.summary_en: The trainer asks how to build a love of reading and whether reading words through phonics is enough.

segments.title_en: Why fluency matters for understanding
segments.title_ur: روانی سے پڑھنا سمجھنے کے لیے کیوں ضروری ہے
segments.summary_en: Phonics gives words but not text; fluency means attending to punctuation, intonation and expression, which builds understanding and enjoyment.

segments.title_en: What echo reading is and why it works
segments.title_ur: ایکو ریڈنگ کیا ہے اور اس کے فائدے
segments.summary_en: The teacher reads one sentence with correct fluency and expression, children repeat it right after; works with one child, groups or the whole class, links spoken and written words and gives a chance for immediate correction.

segments.title_en: Echo reading demonstrated, pointing at each word
segments.title_ur: ایکو ریڈنگ کی مثال: ہر لفظ پر اشارہ
segments.summary_en: The trainer echo-reads a short English story sentence by sentence and warns that children must actually read, so the teacher points at each word as it is read.

segments.title_en: Classroom clip: choral reading and chunking a hard word
segments.title_ur: کلاس کی مثال: مل کر پڑھنا اور مشکل لفظ کے حصے
segments.summary_en: In a real (English-medium) class, children read together slowly with a finger on the first word; the teacher stops at a word someone struggled with, children name its chunks (per-fect-ly), blend it and find it in the story.

segments.title_en: Choosing a text for reading aloud together
segments.title_ur: مل کر پڑھنے کے لیے متن کا انتخاب
segments.summary_en: Pick a short text at a level children can read without difficulty and give each child a copy or show it on screen; goodbye.

modules.title: Vocabulary Building
modules.teacher_line_en: Children say 'good' for everything? A zero-prep group game for synonyms and antonyms
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے ہر بات میں 'اچھا' کہتے ہیں؟ ہم معنی اور متضاد الفاظ کا آسان گروپ کھیل
modules.summary_en: A trainer tackles children who use the same word every time ('good good good', 'achha achha') by teaching synonyms and antonyms in English and Urdu. The teacher sees three activities: a flash-card game asking for a word's synonym and then its antonym, a two-column matching task in copies, and a group sentence challenge where each group says a sentence with its word, then with the antonym, then with a synonym ('we are very happy / sad / joyful').
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ سیکھیں گے کہ فلیش کارڈ، میچنگ اور گروپ میں جملے بنانے کے کھیل سے بچوں کو ہم معنی اور متضاد الفاظ کیسے سکھائیں۔
symptoms: children reuse one word ('good', 'achha') in every answer
vocabulary taught as a word-meaning list copied from the board
no child makes their own sentence with a new word
teacher supplies the opposite or synonym instead of asking the class
modules.not_for: Not for maths or science lessons, or for teachers whose lesson is not about words and meanings; the flash-card game needs cards prepared beforehand.

segments.title_en: Why children need synonyms and antonyms
segments.title_ur: ہم معنی اور متضاد الفاظ کیوں ضروری ہیں
segments.summary_en: Children repeat the same word; teaching synonyms and antonyms in both languages doubles their word bank. Definitions with examples: happy/joyful, hot/cold and Urdu pairs.

segments.title_en: Flash-card game: synonym, then antonym
segments.title_ur: فلیش کارڈ کھیل: پہلے ہم معنی، پھر متضاد
segments.summary_en: Show a card ('happy', or an Urdu word), ask the class for a synonym, then an antonym, and accept the different answers children offer.

segments.title_en: Matching columns and the group sentence challenge
segments.title_ur: میچنگ اور گروپ میں جملے بنانے کا چیلنج
segments.summary_en: Children match words in two columns in their copies; then each group gets one word and must say a sentence with it, with its antonym and with its synonym ('we are very happy / sad / joyful'). Oral, no materials.

modules.title: Guided Reading
modules.teacher_line_en: Before the passage: ask, predict, pre-teach words. After: questions and a summary
modules.teacher_line_ur: سبق سے پہلے سوال اور پیشین گوئی، بعد میں سوال اور خلاصہ: سمجھ کر پڑھنا
modules.summary_en: A narrated walkthrough of guided reading in three steps: a pre-reading discussion, independent reading, and a post-reading discussion. Teachers learn what to do before the text (ask what children already know, ask for predictions, pre-teach new words, preview pictures and headings, set key questions to find while reading), how to listen and support during reading, and how to check understanding after it with questions or a child's summary. Nothing is enacted with children.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ سبق پڑھنے سے پہلے پیشین گوئی اور نئے الفاظ، پڑھنے کے دوران مدد، اور بعد میں سوالوں یا خلاصے سے سمجھ کیسے جانچیں۔
symptoms: teacher starts reading the passage aloud, or children read in chorus, with no question before the text
no question about the title, pictures or what children already know before reading
after reading, the lesson moves to copying or writing with no comprehension question or summary
new words are read out but never explained before or after the text
modules.not_for: Maths or science teachers, and teachers wanting to see a real classroom; it is a narrated outline with no children shown.

segments.title_en: What guided reading is: three steps
segments.title_ur: گائیڈڈ ریڈنگ کیا ہے: تین مراحل
segments.summary_en: Definition of guided reading in levelled small groups and its three steps (before, during, after) and purpose.

segments.title_en: Before reading: questions to ask
segments.title_ur: پڑھنے سے پہلے: کیا پوچھیں
segments.summary_en: Ask what children already know about the topic, what they predict, which words are new; preview pictures, headings and titles; set key questions to find while reading.

segments.title_en: During reading: listen and support
segments.title_ur: پڑھنے کے دوران: سنیں اور مدد کریں
segments.summary_en: Children read on their own while the teacher listens, checks they use the discussed points, helps those who struggle, corrects and encourages, and notes what to work on next.

segments.title_en: After reading: questions and a summary
segments.title_ur: پڑھنے کے بعد: سوال اور خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Discuss the text, check understanding by questions or by having children summarise, ask their opinion, answer the key questions and work on new words. Ends with a recap.

modules.title: Tools for building vocabulary and comprehension skills
modules.teacher_line_en: Grow children's word bank with a semantic map and an A-Z animal board game
modules.teacher_line_ur: سمنٹک میپ اور اے سے زیڈ جانوروں کی سرگرمی سے بچوں کے الفاظ بڑھائیں
modules.summary_en: A trainer reads a short passage (a crocodile by the river, a bee drinking nectar, a turtle at the water's edge), asks simple recall questions, then introduces three vocabulary tools: a semantic map (write 'animal' and link every related word from the passage), alphabetical order, and the dictionary. The tools come together in an 'animal alphabet challenge': A-Z on the board, children name an animal for each letter, a semantic map helps when they are stuck, then the list is read aloud and copied in alphabetical order.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ سمنٹک میپ، حروفِ تہجی کی ترتیب اور ڈکشنری کے ذریعے بچوں کا ذخیرۂ الفاظ کیسے بڑھائیں، اور 'اینیمل الفابیٹ چیلنج' سرگرمی کیسے کروائیں۔
symptoms: new words are read aloud or translated but never grouped, mapped or used again
children copy word meanings from the board with no activity around the words
no dictionary or alphabetical-order practice in an English vocabulary lesson
after a reading passage the teacher asks only 'kaun?' / 'kya?' recall questions
modules.not_for: Teachers looking for comprehension-strategy instruction (prediction, inference) or for questioning beyond recall; the passage questions here are literal only.

segments.title_en: Read-aloud passage and simple recall questions
segments.title_ur: پیراگراف بلند آواز سے پڑھنا اور آسان سوالات
segments.summary_en: Introduces the module, reads a short animal passage aloud and asks literal recall questions (who sat by the river? what was the bee doing?).

segments.title_en: Three tools: semantic map, alphabetical order, dictionary
segments.title_ur: تین ٹولز: سمنٹک میپ، حروفِ تہجی کی ترتیب، ڈکشنری
segments.summary_en: A semantic map links every word from the passage to one key word ('animal': crocodile, bee, turtle, dolphin); alphabetical order helps arrange and spell words; the dictionary gives meaning, spelling and pronunciation.

segments.title_en: Animal alphabet challenge on the board
segments.title_ur: بورڈ پر اینیمل الفابیٹ چیلنج
segments.summary_en: Writes A-Z on the board, children name an animal for each letter, a semantic map helps those who are stuck, a dictionary search adds names, then the class reads the list aloud and copies it in alphabetical order (alligator, bee, crab, dolphin... zebra). Ends with a recap.

modules.title: بھاری اور ہلکی آوازیں
modules.teacher_line_en: Hear the Urdu letter sounds from alif to ye recited in order
modules.teacher_line_ur: الف سے یے تک اردو حروف کی آوازیں ترتیب سے سنیں
modules.summary_en: A presenter notes that children often mispronounce Urdu letters or swap heavy and light sounds, says the first step is recognising every letter from alif to ye by its correct name, then plays/recites the Urdu letter sounds in sequence. The heavy/light sound distinction in the title is never actually taught and no classroom activity is shown.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں اردو کے حروف کی آوازیں الف سے یے تک دہرائی گئی ہیں، مگر بھاری اور ہلکی آوازوں کا فرق سکھانے کا کوئی طریقہ نہیں دکھایا گیا۔
symptoms: children in an Urdu lesson confuse heavy and light letters (e.g. ت/ٹ, د/ڈ) and the teacher does not correct the sound
teacher names letters but never has children say the letter sounds aloud
Urdu reading lesson with no letter-sound practice before reading words
modules.not_for: Anyone looking for how to teach heavy vs light Urdu sounds or a phonics activity; it only recites the alphabet sounds, and it does not suit Grade 3+ or non-Urdu lessons.

segments.title_en: The problem: children swap heavy and light Urdu sounds
segments.title_ur: مسئلہ: بچے اردو کی بھاری اور ہلکی آوازیں بدل دیتے ہیں
segments.summary_en: Greeting; children mispronounce Urdu letters or swap heavy and light sounds because letter names and shapes are not clear; the first step is naming every letter alif to ye correctly.

segments.title_en: Urdu letter sounds recited from alif to ye
segments.title_ur: اردو حروف کی آوازیں: الف سے یے تک
segments.summary_en: The Urdu letter sounds are recited in order for repetition, followed by a reminder that children cannot read well until they recognise all these sounds. No activity with children is shown.

modules.title: اردو کی حرکات
modules.teacher_line_en: Show children how zabar, zer and pesh change a word's sound and meaning
modules.teacher_line_ur: زبر، زیر اور پیش لفظ کی آواز اور مطلب کیسے بدلتے ہیں، بچوں کو دکھائیں
modules.summary_en: A trainer shows zabar, zer and pesh, where each sits and the short sound it gives, then shows how harakat change meaning with three readings of the same letters (bin = without, ban = forest, bun = root), each in a sentence. For practice, groups get words without harakat, add the marks, read the words aloud, and say which mark changed the sound and which changed the meaning.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ زبر، زیر اور پیش کی آواز اور مطلب کا فرق گروپ میں حرکات لگا کر پڑھنے سے کیسے سکھائیں۔
symptoms: children write Urdu words correctly but read them with the wrong vowel sound
teacher reads the word and children repeat, with no zabar/zer/pesh named
no task where children add harakat or read unmarked words themselves
words that differ only by harakat are never contrasted
modules.not_for: Teachers of English, maths or older Urdu classes whose children already read harakat fluently.

segments.title_en: Zabar, zer, pesh: where each sits and its sound
segments.title_ur: زبر، زیر، پیش: کہاں لگتی ہیں اور کیا آواز دیتی ہیں
segments.summary_en: Names the problem (children write a word but cannot pronounce it), then shows on the board where zabar, zer and pesh sit and the short vowel sound each gives.

segments.title_en: Bin, ban, bun: harakat change meaning, then groups try it
segments.title_ur: بِن، بَن، بُن: حرکات سے مطلب بدلنا، پھر گروپ مشق
segments.summary_en: Reads the same letters ب ن three ways (without, forest, root), each in a sentence, to show harakat change meaning; then groups add harakat to unmarked words, read them aloud and say which mark changed the sound and which changed the meaning.

modules.title: ارکان سازی
modules.teacher_line_en: Children read letter by letter? Teach them to blend sounds into syllables with flash cards
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے حرف حرف پڑھتے ہیں؟ فلیش کارڈ سے آوازیں ملا کر ارکان بنانا سکھائیں
modules.summary_en: For children who read every Urdu letter separately and cannot join them, the teacher explains two-letter and three-letter syllables (با، نا / بنا، کتب) and sound blending (بے + الف = با; ک + ت + ا = کتا). Then a three-step guided practice: flash cards of two-letter syllables sounded out, three-letter syllables where children say which letters join, and groups building two- and three-letter words from letter sets while the teacher corrects pronunciation.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ دو حرفی اور تین حرفی ارکان کی آوازیں ملا کر لفظ بنانا کیسے سکھائیں اور فلیش کارڈ اور حروف کے سیٹ سے گروپ میں مشق کیسے کروائیں۔
symptoms: children read Urdu words letter by letter and cannot join them
teacher reads the word aloud and children repeat it whole, with no blending of sounds
no flash cards or letter sets; reading practice is only chorus repetition from the book
mispronounced syllables are not corrected
modules.not_for: Teachers of fluent readers (Grade 4+) or of non-Urdu lessons.

segments.title_en: Why some children read letter by letter; two kinds of syllables
segments.title_ur: بچے حرف حرف کیوں پڑھتے ہیں؛ دو حرفی اور تین حرفی ارکان
segments.summary_en: Intro: the problem of children reading each letter separately, and the definitions of two-letter (با، نا) and three-letter (بنا، کتب، لکھ) syllables.

segments.title_en: Blend sounds into syllables, then practise with flash cards
segments.title_ur: آوازیں ملا کر ارکان بنائیں، پھر فلیش کارڈ سے مشق کروائیں
segments.summary_en: Blending is modelled (بے + الف = با; ک + ت + ا = کتا), then three guided steps: sound out two-letter flash cards, say which letters join in three-letter syllables, groups build words from letter sets while the teacher corrects pronunciation.

modules.title: متشابہ آوازیں
modules.teacher_line_en: Children mix up س، ص، ث in spelling? Three 2-minute board drills to fix it
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے س، ص اور ث میں الجھتے ہیں؟ بورڈ پر دو منٹ کی تین آسان مشقیں
modules.summary_en: A trainer addresses children who read a word correctly but misspell it because some Urdu letters sound alike (س، ص، ث). The teacher sees three quick drills: a flash card with the letter and a picture cue, a strip of words with only these letters read at speed, and a spot-the-letter board game where children circle only one of the three letters at a time.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ سیکھیں گے کہ س، ص اور ث جیسی ملتی جلتی آوازوں والے حروف کو فلیش کارڈ، الفاظ کی پٹی اور حرف ڈھونڈنے کے کھیل سے کیسے پہچان کروائیں۔
symptoms: children write the wrong letter among س/ص/ث in dictation or copy work
teacher corrects a misspelt word by rewriting it without pointing to the confusable letter
Urdu reading lesson with no letter-recognition or fluency drill
modules.not_for: Not for English, maths or science lessons, or for upper-grade Urdu classes that already spell these letters correctly.

segments.title_en: Why similar-sounding letters cause spelling errors
segments.title_ur: ملتی جلتی آوازیں ہجے کی غلطیاں کیوں بنتی ہیں
segments.summary_en: Children read words but misspell them because س، ص، ث sound alike; the trainer names fluency drills (repeated, paced, paired reading) and colour-coded flash cards and charts as the remedy.

segments.title_en: Flash card, word strip, spot-the-letter
segments.title_ur: فلیش کارڈ، الفاظ کی پٹی اور حرف ڈھونڈو کھیل
segments.summary_en: Hold up a card with the letter and a sun picture and ask the class to name it; have children read a strip of words containing only these letters at speed; write mixed letters on the board and ask children to circle only ث, then only س, then only ص.

modules.title: بصری الفاظ
modules.teacher_line_en: Flashcards and a quick game so children read یہ، وہ، ہے، ہیں at sight
modules.teacher_line_ur: فلیش کارڈ اور تیز کھیل سے بچے 'یہ، وہ، ہے، ہیں' فوراً پہچانیں
modules.summary_en: The presenter explains Urdu sight words (بصری الفاظ) through four high-frequency words: یہ، وہ، ہے، ہیں. Teachers learn a four-step routine: show each flashcard and read it aloud for children to repeat, match each word to a picture, have children read short repeated sentences ('یہ میری کتاب ہے', 'وہ میرا بستہ ہے') 3-4 times, and play a fast flashcard game ('یہ کون سا لفظ ہے؟') for speed and accuracy.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ 'یہ، وہ، ہے، ہیں' جیسے بصری الفاظ فلیش کارڈ، تصویر، بار بار پڑھنے اور فوری جواب والے کھیل سے کیسے پکے کروائیں۔
symptoms: children sound out or stall on very common words like یہ، وہ، ہے in every sentence
reading lesson is only the teacher reading and the class repeating the whole passage
no flashcards, word wall or word game for high-frequency words
children read slowly word by word and cannot read a short sentence fluently
modules.not_for: Teachers of Grade 4+ or of maths and science, and English-reading lessons; it covers four Urdu sight words for early readers.

segments.title_en: Intro: what sight words are
segments.title_ur: تعارف: بصری الفاظ کیا ہیں
segments.summary_en: Greeting; sight words defined with the four target words یہ، وہ، ہے، ہیں; why flashcards and repeated reading help children recognise them fast.

segments.title_en: Four steps: flashcards to quick game
segments.title_ur: چار مراحل: فلیش کارڈ سے تیز کھیل تک
segments.summary_en: Show and read each flashcard for children to repeat, match words to pictures, read short sentences like 'یہ میری کتاب ہے' 3-4 times, then a quick-response flashcard game.

modules.title: جملے
modules.teacher_line_en: Children write Urdu left to right or off the line? Model, copy, then peer-check
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے اردو الٹی یا لائن سے ہٹ کر لکھتے ہیں؟ بورڈ پر لکھ کر دکھائیں، پھر ساتھی سے چیک کروائیں
modules.summary_en: Despite the title ('sentences'), this is about the mechanics of early Urdu writing: three rules (write right to left, keep every word on the baseline, use zabar/zer/pesh because they change a word's meaning). The teacher then sees three quick practices: model-write a word such as 'کتاب' on the board for children to copy, write a short sentence ('یہ میرا گھر ہے') while children watch before writing it, and peer review where partners check each other's orientation, alignment and harakat.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ اردو لکھائی میں دائیں سے بائیں لکھنا، لفظ کو سیدھی لائن پر رکھنا اور زیر زبر پیش کیسے سکھائیں، اور بچے ایک دوسرے کا کام کیسے چیک کریں۔
symptoms: in an Urdu writing lesson the teacher only says 'saaf likho' with no model on the board
children copy words from the board without seeing the teacher write them first
zabar/zer/pesh never mentioned while children write or read Urdu words
the teacher checks every copy alone; children never check a partner's writing
modules.not_for: Teachers of English, maths or Grade 4+ Urdu wanting sentence construction or grammar; despite the title it does not teach how to build sentences.

segments.title_en: Three rules of Urdu writing: direction, baseline, harakat
segments.title_ur: اردو لکھائی کے تین اصول: سمت، سیدھی لائن، اعراب
segments.summary_en: Names common errors (writing left to right, words off the line) and three rules: right-to-left orientation, alignment on the baseline, and harakat (zabar, zer, pesh change a word's meaning).

segments.title_en: Model writing, copy-and-check, peer review
segments.title_ur: بورڈ پر لکھ کر دکھانا، نقل اور جانچ، ساتھی سے چیک
segments.summary_en: Write 'کتاب' on the board for children to copy; write a short sentence while children watch, then they write it; partners check each other's orientation, alignment and harakat to build accuracy and self-checking.

modules.title: Five step lesson plan
modules.teacher_line_en: Turn one SLO into a 5-step lesson: open, explain, group, solo, close
modules.teacher_line_ur: ایک SLO سے پانچ مرحلوں کا سبق بنانا مثال کے ساتھ دیکھیں
modules.summary_en: A presenter writes one measurable SLO ("identify at least 3 healthy foods from pictures with 80% accuracy") and walks it through the five steps: opening, explanation, guided practice, independent practice and conclusion. Each step has a ready example: a chips-or-apple question to open, a two-column board explanation, groups sorting book pictures into healthy and not healthy, worksheet circling, and a closing "who can name 3 healthy foods?". The teacher learns how to make every step serve the objective.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں ایک واضح اور قابلِ پیمائش SLO لکھ کر اسے پانچ مراحل (آغاز، وضاحت، گروپ مشق، انفرادی مشق، اختتام) کے ذریعے حاصل کرنا مثالوں سے دکھایا گیا ہے۔
symptoms: no objective stated; the teacher only names the topic or page number
lesson is one block of teacher talk with no group or individual practice
teacher never says 'now we move to…' between phases
lesson ends with the bell or homework, no question to students about what they learned
modules.not_for: Teachers who already plan in opening / explanation / guided / independent / closure phases; it is a planning template, not a questioning or management clip.

segments.title_en: Write a clear, measurable SLO
segments.title_ur: واضح اور قابلِ پیمائش SLO لکھیں
segments.summary_en: Sets the SLO 'identify at least 3 healthy foods from pictures with 80% accuracy', explains why specific and measurable matters, and names the five lesson steps.

segments.title_en: Step 1: open with a quick picture question
segments.title_ur: پہلا مرحلہ: تصویر والے سوال سے آغاز
segments.summary_en: Grab attention with a question, picture or short activity; example: show food pictures and ask 'chips or apple, which is healthy?' with a show of hands.

segments.title_en: Step 2: explain with a two-column board
segments.title_ur: دوسرا مرحلہ: بورڈ پر دو کالم بنا کر وضاحت
segments.summary_en: Explain the concept with examples and pictures; the teacher draws healthy / not healthy columns and says why the apple is healthy and the chips are not.

segments.title_en: Step 3: guided group sorting activity
segments.title_ur: تیسرا مرحلہ: گروپ میں تصویریں چھانٹنے کی مشق
segments.summary_en: Guided practice in groups or pairs with on-the-spot correction; each group sorts book pictures into healthy / not healthy and sticks them in the right column on chart paper.

segments.title_en: Step 4: independent practice and checking
segments.title_ur: چوتھا مرحلہ: انفرادی مشق اور جانچ
segments.summary_en: Students work alone (circle healthy foods on a worksheet, pick 3 healthy foods from the board, write 2 favourites) while the teacher observes, checks answers and gives feedback.

segments.title_en: Step 5: close by asking students what they learned
segments.title_ur: پانچواں مرحلہ: بچوں سے پوچھ کر سبق ختم کریں
segments.summary_en: Conclusion checks whether the SLO was met: 'What did we learn today? Who can name 3 healthy foods?' plus a picture check; then a short wrap-up of the five-step format.

modules.title: Blooms Taxonomy
modules.teacher_line_en: Turn 'name the provinces' questions into why, compare and which-is-better questions
modules.teacher_line_ur: صرف یاد والے سوالوں سے آگے: کیوں، موازنہ اور کون بہتر ہے والے سوال بنائیں
modules.summary_en: A trainer walks through Bloom's six levels, giving each a one-line meaning and a classroom question or task: 'name the states of matter' (Remember), retell a story in your own words (Understand), a new multiplication word problem (Apply), 'what happens to a plant with no sunlight?' or two similarities and differences of amphibians and reptiles (Analyze), 'which of two story endings is better and why?' (Evaluate), and designing a growth plan or mini-garden (Create). Teachers write one task for their own subject at each level as the video goes.
modules.summary_ur: آپ بلوم کی چھ سطحوں کے مطابق اپنے مضمون کے لیے یاد کرنے سے لے کر نئی چیز بنانے تک کے سوال اور کام لکھنا سیکھیں گے۔
symptoms: every question asks for a name, a definition or a number from memory
no 'why', 'what would happen if' or 'compare' question in the whole lesson
children never use the concept in a new situation or problem
children's answers are one word; none gives a reason or a judgement
modules.not_for: Teachers who already ask a range of open why/compare/judge questions; the video gives question types, not how to run discussion or follow up on answers.

segments.title_en: What Bloom's taxonomy is for
segments.title_ur: بلوم ٹیکسونومی کس لیے ہے
segments.summary_en: Introduces Bloom's as the framework for thinking levels, states the session objectives, and asks teachers to note one task per level for their own subject.

segments.title_en: Remember and Understand: recall vs own words
segments.title_ur: یاد رکھنا اور سمجھنا: یاد سے بتانا یا اپنے لفظوں میں
segments.summary_en: Remember = recall facts ('name the states of matter', 'name the provinces'); Understand = explain in own words, such as retelling a story or explaining fractions.
segments.recommendable_reason: panel_veto: ladder only, not a next-step pick (a definition chapter; 0/8 in the R7 panel, ped/REVIEW_r7_scale.md §6.2)

segments.title_en: Apply: use it in a new situation
segments.title_ur: اطلاق: سیکھی چیز نئی صورتحال میں
segments.summary_en: Apply = use learning in a new context: a new multiplication word problem after the concept, or using 'because' and 'therefore' in new sentences; teachers write an Apply task for their grade.

segments.title_en: Analyze: cause-effect and compare questions
segments.title_ur: تجزیہ: وجہ اور اثر، موازنے کے سوال
segments.summary_en: Analyze = break ideas down and connect them: 'why is photosynthesis important, what happens to a plant with no sunlight?' and 'two similarities and two differences between amphibians and reptiles'.
segments.recommendable_reason: panel_veto: ladder only, not a next-step pick (a definition chapter; 0/8 in the R7 panel, ped/REVIEW_r7_scale.md §6.2)

segments.title_en: Evaluate: judge with criteria and give reasons
segments.title_ur: جانچنا: معیار سے فیصلہ اور وجہ
segments.summary_en: Evaluate = judge against criteria and give reasoning, e.g. which of two story endings is better and why.
segments.recommendable_reason: panel_veto: ladder only, not a next-step pick (a definition chapter; 0/8 in the R7 panel, ped/REVIEW_r7_scale.md §6.2)

segments.title_en: Create: design something new
segments.title_ur: تخلیق: کوئی نئی چیز بنانا
segments.summary_en: Create = design a new product: a growth plan for a plant (soil, light, water) or a mini-garden model, then a short wrap-up that Bloom's gives structure to what teachers already do.

modules.title: Students-centered instructional strategies
modules.teacher_line_en: Big noisy class? Give every group of four a role: recorder, timekeeper, reporter
modules.teacher_line_ur: بڑی اور شور والی کلاس؟ چار بچوں کے ہر گروپ کو کردار دیں: ریکارڈر، ٹائم کیپر، رپورٹر
modules.summary_en: A narrated story of a teacher with 32 noisy students who moves from lecturing to designing: visual routine charts for transitions, materials and questions, practised daily; 8 groups of four with rotating roles (recorder, timekeeper, reporter); and peer teaching, where students who mastered a skill circulate as expert guides. It ends with the teacher coaching drifting groups and two reflection questions.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں ایک کہانی کے ذریعے دکھایا گیا ہے کہ بڑی کلاس میں معمولات کے چارٹ، کرداروں والے گروپ (ریکارڈر، ٹائم کیپر، رپورٹر) اور بچوں سے ایک دوسرے کو سکھوانا کیسے شور کو سیکھنے میں بدلتا ہے۔
symptoms: teacher talks for most of the period with no student task
a few children finish early while others sit stuck or misbehave
no group task with roles; children never explain to each other
repeated calls for quiet during transitions and materials handout
modules.not_for: Urdu-medium teachers who cannot follow English narration, or teachers who already run structured group work.

segments.title_en: The problem: 32 students, lecture not working
segments.title_ur: مسئلہ: بتیس بچے اور لیکچر کام نہیں کر رہا
segments.summary_en: Story setup: a crowded, noisy room; fidgeting during lectures; fast finishers idle while others are stuck.

segments.title_en: Visual routine charts, practised daily
segments.title_ur: معمولات کے تصویری چارٹ، روزانہ مشق
segments.summary_en: Routine charts for transitions, materials and questions, practised until automatic so students know what comes next; reflection: which one routine would you practise for two weeks?

segments.title_en: Groups of four with roles, and peer teaching
segments.title_ur: چار کے گروپ، کردار، اور بچوں کا ایک دوسرے کو سکھانا
segments.summary_en: Eight groups each with a clear task and rotating roles (recorder, timekeeper, reporter); students who master a skill become expert guides; when groups drift, the teacher coaches collaboration as a skill.

segments.title_en: What changed, and a reflection question
segments.title_ur: کیا بدلا، اور ایک سوال غور کے لیے
segments.summary_en: Outcome of the story (noise becomes busy learning, a restless child becomes reporter) and a closing reflection question; no new technique.

modules.title: Peer Learning
modules.teacher_line_en: Only the same few children answer? Try think-pair-share with planned pairs
modules.teacher_line_ur: ہمیشہ چند بچے ہی جواب دیتے ہیں؟ سوچی سمجھی جوڑیوں کے ساتھ تھنک پیئر شیئر آزمائیں
modules.summary_en: A podcast-style conversation in which an experienced government-school teacher explains think-pair-share in three steps (think alone and write an answer, discuss in pairs, share a joint explanation with the class) and then describes a Grade 4 subtraction lesson using three kinds of pairs: a stronger child explaining step by step to a weaker one who then repeats it, two average children swapping methods, and a shy child paired with a confident one. The teacher learns to plan who sits with whom and to act as a facilitator who monitors answers and gives gentle feedback.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ سنیں گے کہ تھنک پیئر شیئر کے تین مرحلے کیا ہیں اور جوڑیاں (کمزور اور مضبوط، ہم سطح، شرمیلا اور پُراعتماد) سوچ سمجھ کر کیسے بنائیں۔
symptoms: teacher asks a question and takes the first hand-up answer immediately, no think time
the same two or three children answer every question while the rest stay silent
answers come only in chorus; no child explains their method to a partner
no pair or partner talk at any point in the lesson
modules.not_for: Teachers who already run pair talk routinely, or who need a classroom demonstration: this is a conversation about pairs, no children are shown.

segments.title_en: Podcast intro: peer teaching in government schools
segments.title_ur: تعارف: سرکاری اسکولوں میں ساتھیوں سے سیکھنا
segments.summary_en: The host introduces the episode and the guest teacher and asks what peer-teaching strategies such as think-pair-share are and how to run them.

segments.title_en: Think-pair-share in three steps
segments.title_ur: تھنک پیئر شیئر کے تین مرحلے
segments.summary_en: Think: the teacher gives a question and each child thinks for 2-3 minutes and writes an answer; Pair: partners discuss and explain their point of view; Share: the pair presents a joint explanation to the class.

segments.title_en: Three kinds of pairs in a Grade 4 maths class
segments.title_ur: جماعت چہارم کی ریاضی میں تین قسم کی جوڑیاں
segments.summary_en: On a subtraction problem the teacher pairs a stronger child with a weaker one (explain step by step, weaker child repeats), two average children (swap methods), and a shy child with a confident one who invites them to share.

segments.title_en: The teacher's role and what changed
segments.title_ur: ٹیچر کا کردار اور نتائج
segments.summary_en: The teacher acts as facilitator: monitors whether answers are correct, gives gentle feedback, and varies pair types; then describes results (more confidence, collaboration, easier to spot misunderstandings) and the sign-off.

modules.title: Open-Ended Questions
modules.teacher_line_en: Turn 'Is water necessary?' into 'Why is water necessary?' and get every group talking
modules.teacher_line_ur: 'کیا پانی ضروری ہے؟' کو 'پانی کیوں ضروری ہے؟' میں بدلیں اور ہر گروپ کو بولنے دیں
modules.summary_en: A short dramatised conversation between two teachers: one asks how to get children thinking, the other contrasts 'Is water necessary?' (yes/no) with 'Why do you think water is necessary for our life?'. It gives a what-if question for science, maths, Urdu and social studies, then shows how to use open questions in a crowded class: give each group one question to discuss, let one child explain their idea to another, and use a three-clap signal before sharing.
modules.summary_ur: آپ دیکھیں گے کہ ہاں/نہیں والے سوال کو 'کیوں' اور 'اگر ایسا ہو تو' والے کھلے سوال میں کیسے بدلیں اور بڑی کلاس میں گروپوں کو ایک سوال دے کر بات کیسے کروائیں۔
symptoms: almost every teacher question is yes/no or has the answer in it ('yeh zaroori hai na?')
the class answers in chorus ('jee', 'haan') and no child gives a reason
no 'why', 'how' or 'what if' question anywhere in the lesson
only the same two or three children answer while the rest of the large class is silent
modules.not_for: Teachers who already ask several why/how questions and follow up on answers; it does not cover follow-up probes or wait time.

segments.title_en: Yes/no question vs. a 'why' question
segments.title_ur: ہاں/نہیں والا سوال بمقابلہ 'کیوں' والا سوال
segments.summary_en: A teacher asks how to build critical thinking; the colleague contrasts 'Is water necessary?' (answer: yes/no) with 'Why do you think water is necessary for our life?' so the child thinks and shares ideas.

segments.title_en: Open questions for every subject
segments.title_ur: ہر مضمون کے لیے کھلے سوال
segments.summary_en: Examples by subject: 'What would the world be like without trees?', 'Where do you use numbers in daily life?', 'How would you change the story's ending?', 'If you were a leader, what would you change in your community?'.

segments.title_en: Open questions in a crowded class
segments.title_ur: بھری ہوئی کلاس میں کھلے سوال
segments.summary_en: For a large class: give each group one open question to discuss, let one child explain their idea to another, and use a three-clap signal before groups share; the teacher plans 'What would change if water ran out?' for tomorrow.

modules.title: Visuals Aids
modules.teacher_line_en: Swap rote for pictures: a half-roti for 1/2, flashcards, charts kids draw
modules.teacher_line_ur: رٹے کی جگہ تصویر: آدھی روٹی سے 1/2، فلیش کارڈ اور چارٹ
modules.summary_en: Two teachers talk through a problem: children memorise maths and English without understanding. The experienced teacher shows how a coloured half-roti drawing explains 1/2, picture cards explain synonyms, flashcards and a shape hunt teach circle, a multiplication chart drives group work, a subject-verb-object chart helps children build sentences, and children draw and colour their own fraction shapes. For large classes, children explain a picture card to a partner and link shapes to things at home.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں دکھایا گیا ہے کہ ریاضی اور انگریزی میں تصویری کارڈ، چارٹ اور بچوں کی اپنی بنائی ہوئی ڈرائنگ سے رٹے کے بجائے سمجھ کیسے پیدا کی جائے۔
symptoms: teacher writes '1/2' or a definition on the board with no drawing, object or picture
students repeat definitions in chorus (rote) and cannot give an example
teacher repeats the same explanation louder when children do not understand
no chart, card or drawing is mentioned anywhere in a maths or English lesson
modules.not_for: Teachers who already use pictures and charts routinely, or secondary teachers; the examples are primary maths and English and it does not teach questioning in depth.

segments.title_en: The problem: children memorise without understanding
segments.title_ur: مسئلہ: بچے رٹا لگاتے ہیں، سمجھتے نہیں
segments.summary_en: One teacher says children only memorise in maths and English; a colleague suggests visual aids because children understand more clearly when they learn by seeing.

segments.title_en: Half a roti for 1/2, picture cards for synonyms
segments.title_ur: 1/2 کے لیے آدھی روٹی، مترادف کے لیے تصویری کارڈ
segments.summary_en: Writing 1/2 on the board confuses children; drawing a round roti with half coloured makes 'half' instant. In English, picture cards of a happy and a joyful child explain synonyms better than a definition.

segments.title_en: Flashcards: shape hunt and picture-word cards
segments.title_ur: فلیش کارڈ: شکل ڈھونڈیں اور تصویر سے لفظ
segments.summary_en: Stick a circle card on the board and ask children to find something circle-shaped in the classroom; show an apple card with the word and ask who will write the spelling on the board.

segments.title_en: Charts: times-table groups and S+V+O sentences
segments.title_ur: چارٹ: پہاڑے کے گروپ اور S+V+O جملے
segments.summary_en: Use a multiplication chart with groups finding the 3 and 4 tables; build a subject + verb + object chart from 'Ali eats mango' and have children make their own sentences.

segments.title_en: Children draw their own visual aids
segments.title_ur: بچے اپنی تصویری مدد خود بنائیں
segments.summary_en: Children draw shapes, divide them into equal parts, colour some and write the fraction; in English they draw a part or character from their story, which gives ownership.

segments.title_en: Large class: pair explaining, questions, daily-life links
segments.title_ur: بڑی کلاس: جوڑی میں سمجھانا، سوال اور روزمرہ مثال
segments.summary_en: In a big class, give a pair one picture card to explain to each other, ask 'if this circle is halved, how many parts?', and link to life: 'what shape is the TV at home?'.

segments.title_en: Plan your next lesson with one visual aid (recap)
segments.title_ur: اگلے سبق میں ایک تصویری مدد شامل کریں (خلاصہ)
segments.summary_en: The teacher decides to choose a topic and a visual aid for the next class; a recap that learning by seeing lasts longer.

modules.title: Misconceptions in basic operations
modules.teacher_line_en: Spot and fix the 4 classic errors: borrowing over zero, carrying, 23x4, remainders
modules.teacher_line_ur: ادھار، حاصل، 23 ضرب 4 اور باقی والی عام غلطیاں پہچانیں اور درست کریں
modules.summary_en: A trainer lists the four common errors (borrowing across zero in 402 - 187, forgetting to carry in 27 + 15, multiplying only the ones in 23 x 4, dropping the remainder in 37 / 5) and three quick ways to find them: ask 'why did you take the bigger number from the smaller?', look for a pattern in copies, and a 3-4 item diagnostic quiz. Each error is then corrected step by step on the board with place-value headings (2 tens + 3 ones, 20 x 4 + 3 x 4; 37 shared into groups of 5 gives 7 R 2), followed by a guided example, a 'find the mistake' problem, an independent problem and a reflection question.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ جمع، تفریق، ضرب اور تقسیم میں بچوں کی عام غلط فہمیاں کیسے پہچانیں اور بورڈ پر مرحلہ وار، مقامی قیمت کے ساتھ کیسے درست کریں۔
symptoms: teacher marks a wrong subtraction or carrying answer 'galat' and gives the right answer without asking how the child got it
column sums written without ones/tens/hundreds headings
teacher never asks 'how did you get this?' after a wrong answer
division answers given with no mention of the remainder
no problem where children have to find the mistake in a worked example
modules.not_for: Teachers of older grades or non-maths subjects; it assumes children are still learning column addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.

segments.title_en: Misconceptions are where learning starts
segments.title_ur: غلط فہمیاں سیکھنے کا دروازہ ہیں
segments.summary_en: Introduces the module: children's errors show where their concept is wrong, and the teacher's job is to diagnose and give a clear correction.

segments.title_en: Four common errors and three ways to diagnose them
segments.title_ur: چار عام غلطیاں اور پہچاننے کے تین طریقے
segments.summary_en: Names the borrowing, carrying, multiplication and remainder errors, then diagnoses them by asking 'why did you subtract this way?', checking copies for patterns, and a 3-4 item quick quiz.

segments.title_en: Fix borrowing across zero: 402 - 187
segments.title_ur: صفر سے ادھار درست کریں: 402 - 187
segments.summary_en: Solves 402 - 187 vertically on the board with ones, tens and hundreds headings, showing how to borrow from the next place when the neighbour is zero (answer 215).

segments.title_en: Fix forgotten carrying: 27 + 15
segments.title_ur: حاصل بھول جانا درست کریں: 27 + 15
segments.summary_en: Shows the error (writing 2 and dropping the 1), then the correct step: 12 ones = 2 ones and 1 ten carried to the tens column, giving 42, said aloud while written.

segments.title_en: Fix partial multiplication: 23 x 4
segments.title_ur: ادھوری ضرب درست کریں: 23 ضرب 4
segments.summary_en: Children multiply only 3 x 4; the fix splits 23 into 2 tens and 3 ones, multiplies each (12 and 80) and adds to 92.

segments.title_en: Fix the missing remainder: 37 / 5 with equal groups
segments.title_ur: باقی بھول جانا درست کریں: 37 تقسیم 5
segments.summary_en: Shares 37 into equal groups of 5 to show 7 groups and 2 left over (7 R 2), and asks teachers to use words like remainder, leftover and altogether in every lesson.

segments.title_en: After the fix: guided, find-the-mistake, independent, reflect
segments.title_ur: اصلاح کے بعد: رہنمائی، غلطی ڈھونڈیں، خود حل، سوچیں
segments.summary_en: Practice after correction: a guided example with questions at each step, a wrong worked problem where children find the mistake, an independent problem that sets the same trap, and 'what did you learn about borrowing today?'.

modules.title: Fractions
modules.teacher_line_en: Fractions only as numbers on the board? Fold paper strips so children see which is bigger
modules.teacher_line_ur: کسریں صرف بورڈ پر ہندسے؟ کاغذ کی پٹیاں موڑ کر بچوں کو دکھائیں کون سی بڑی ہے
modules.summary_en: The teacher states the objective (compare like and unlike fractions), shows a fraction as a roti cut into equal parts drawn on the board, and names numerator and denominator (3/4 = 3 of 4 equal parts). Children fold and shade paper strips to see 5/7 > 2/7 and 1/6 > 1/8, then solve a pizza/roti sharing question; the lesson closes with 'Which is bigger, 1/2 or 1/3? How do you prove it?' and a board sort of like vs unlike fractions.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ روٹی کی مثال اور کاغذ کی پٹیاں موڑ کر رنگنے سے بچے یکساں اور غیر یکساں کسروں کا موازنہ کیسے کرتے ہیں۔
symptoms: fractions written and compared only as symbols, with no object, drawing or strip
teacher states 'bigger numerator means bigger fraction' and children chorus it
children think 1/8 is bigger than 1/6 because 8 is bigger and the teacher just says 'galat'
no 'how do you know?' when a child says which fraction is bigger
modules.not_for: Teachers whose lesson is not on fractions, or Grade 1-2 teachers whose children are only starting halves and quarters.

segments.title_en: A fraction as equal parts of a roti; numerator and denominator
segments.title_ur: روٹی کے برابر حصے، شمار کنندہ اور نسب نما
segments.summary_en: Objective stated; a roti cut into 2 and 4 equal parts, drawn on the board, shows what 1/2 and 1/4 mean; numerator and denominator named with 3/4.

segments.title_en: Compare like fractions with shaded paper strips
segments.title_ur: کاغذ کی رنگی پٹیوں سے یکساں کسروں کا موازنہ
segments.summary_en: With the same denominator the larger numerator wins (5/7 > 2/7); children shade 2 and 5 parts of 7-part strips to see it, then answer a pizza-slices question.

segments.title_en: Compare unit fractions with folded strips
segments.title_ur: موڑی ہوئی پٹیوں سے مختلف نسب نما والی کسروں کا موازنہ
segments.summary_en: Children fold one strip into 6 and one into 8, shade one part each and see 1/6 > 1/8, then a roti-sharing question; note the board example is misspoken as 1/7 vs 1/8.

segments.title_en: Close with 'How do you prove it?' and a like/unlike sort
segments.title_ur: آخر میں: آپ کیسے ثابت کریں گے؟ اور کسروں کی چھانٹی
segments.summary_en: Closing questions (which pair is like? which is bigger, 1/2 or 1/3, and how do you prove it?), then children write like and unlike examples in two board columns and look for fractions around them.

modules.title: Case study on Estimation and Rounding up
modules.teacher_line_en: Teaching rounding? Two place-value rules, a rhyme and bazaar examples
modules.teacher_line_ur: رائونڈنگ پڑھا رہے ہیں؟ مقامی قدر کے دو اصول، ایک نظم اور بازار کی مثالیں
modules.summary_en: A trainer opens with market and school examples (98 rupees is about 100, 49 children about 50), gives the two rounding rules by place value (5 or more round up, 4 or less stay, then zeros) with a rhyme for children, and works through 2,612 and 27,268 rounded at different places. The teacher then sees estimation as quick rounding of totals (97 + 46 is about 150, 278 m about 300 m) and is told to use local, real-life examples in class.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ مقامی مثالوں اور ایک نظم کے ذریعے بچوں کو مقامی قدر کے حساب سے رائونڈنگ اور تخمینہ کیسے سکھائیں۔
symptoms: children round 47 to 40 or 62 to 70 and the teacher just says 'galat' without the rule
rounding taught as a rule on the board with no prices, distances or class numbers
teacher does not say which place value is being rounded to
estimation questions are answered by exact calculation
modules.not_for: Teachers outside Grades 3-5 maths or whose lesson is not about rounding or estimation; it is content, not a general teaching move.

segments.title_en: Why round? Prices and class sizes
segments.title_ur: رائونڈنگ کیوں؟ قیمتیں اور بچوں کی تعداد
segments.summary_en: Opens with everyday rounding (98 rupees for tomatoes is about 100, 49 students about 50) and defines rounding as replacing a number with a nearby easier one.

segments.title_en: Rounding rules, a rhyme and worked examples
segments.title_ur: رائونڈنگ کے اصول، نظم اور حل شدہ مثالیں
segments.summary_en: Check the place value, then 5 or more round up and 4 or less stay (47 to 50, 62 to 60), a rhyme to remember it, and 2,612 and 27,268 rounded at each place. Caution: at 163-183 s the trainer says 'tens place' but rounds 27,268 to 30,000 (ten-thousands).

segments.title_en: Estimation with real-life numbers
segments.title_ur: روزمرہ اعداد کے ساتھ تخمینہ
segments.summary_en: Estimation as quick rounding (97 + 46 is about 150, 278 m about 300 m, 2,578 children about 3,000) and the advice to give children local examples like bazaar rates and distances; ends with a short recap.

modules.title: Measurements Units
modules.teacher_line_en: Teach km/m, kg/g, L/ml and hours/minutes with real examples and 'which unit, why?'
modules.teacher_line_ur: کلومیٹر، کلوگرام، لیٹر اور گھنٹے کی تبدیلی روزمرہ مثالوں اور 'کون سی اکائی، کیوں؟' سے
modules.summary_en: A presenter walks through length, mass, volume, time and temperature units for Grades 4-5: what each unit is for (mm for a pencil tip, km from village to city), the conversion rule to write on the board (1 km = 1000 m, 1 kg = 1000 g, 1 hour = 60 minutes) and a worked real-life conversion (2 km = 2000 m; 350 g = 0.35 kg; 120 minutes = 2 hours). After each unit the teacher asks a 'which unit and why?' question (Lahore to Karachi in cm or km? flour in kg but spices in g?) and explains the reason.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ لمبائی، وزن، مقدار، وقت اور درجہ حرارت کی اکائیاں روزمرہ مثالوں سے کیسے سمجھائیں، تبدیلی کے اصول بورڈ پر کیسے لکھیں اور 'کون سی اکائی اور کیوں؟' جیسا سوال کیسے پوچھیں۔
symptoms: measurement lesson where conversion rules (1 km = 1000 m) are only read out and copied, with no real-life example
children multiply or divide by the wrong number when converting units (e.g. 350 g = 3.5 kg)
teacher never asks why a unit is used for a quantity, only 'kitne meter hain?'
units and their abbreviations (mm, cm, kg, ml) are used without being explained
modules.not_for: Teachers of Grades 1-3 (the video itself says conversions suit Grades 4-5) and of non-maths lessons; it is content refresh, not a classroom-management or general questioning clip.

segments.title_en: Intro: five kinds of measurement units
segments.title_ur: تعارف: پیمائش کی پانچ اکائیاں
segments.summary_en: Greeting; length, mass, volume, time and temperature, and where they appear in daily life (distance, vegetables, milk, fever).

segments.title_en: Length: mm, cm, m, km and converting
segments.title_ur: لمبائی: ملی میٹر سے کلومیٹر تک اور تبدیلی
segments.summary_en: Each length unit with an everyday object, the rules 1 km = 1000 m, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 cm = 10 mm on the board, 2 km = 2000 m worked out, then 'Lahore to Karachi: cm or km? Why?'.

segments.title_en: Mass: grams, kilograms and converting both ways
segments.title_ur: وزن: گرام، کلوگرام اور دونوں طرف تبدیلی
segments.summary_en: Grams for a biscuit, kilograms for people; 3 kg = 3000 g and 350 g ÷ 1000 = 0.35 kg; a note that conversions suit Grades 4-5; then 'why is flour in kg but spices in g?'.

segments.title_en: Volume: litres and millilitres
segments.title_ur: مقدار: لیٹر اور ملی لیٹر
segments.summary_en: Volume for milk, water, oil; 2 L = 2000 ml; ml to L by dividing by 1000; 'a milk tanker: litres or millilitres?'. The board rule is spoken as '1000 mm = 1 L' (should be ml).

segments.title_en: Time: hours, minutes, seconds
segments.title_ur: وقت: گھنٹے، منٹ اور سیکنڈ
segments.summary_en: A 1-hour period, a 30-minute break, a blink of about 1 second; 2 hours = 120 minutes and 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours; 'why is a break in minutes but an exam in hours?'.

segments.title_en: Temperature: Celsius and Fahrenheit
segments.title_ur: درجہ حرارت: سیلسیس اور فارن ہائیٹ
segments.summary_en: Celsius for weather and fever in Pakistan, Fahrenheit described as mostly medical use in the USA; 'why are weather and fever both shown in Celsius?'; closing.

modules.title: Area and Perimeter
modules.teacher_line_en: Children mix up area and perimeter? Carpet vs fence: a 3-minute story that fixes it
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے ایریا اور پیرامیٹر میں الجھتے ہیں؟ قالین اور باڑ کی کہانی سے فرق واضح کریں
modules.summary_en: A narrated story: the school caretaker must order a carpet for the hall and fencing for the boundary and cannot tell whether to measure inside or around. The maths teacher counts 1-unit floor tiles (12 square units), moves to Area = length x width on a 4 cm x 3 cm board diagram, then lays a rope round a 10 m square ground and asks what to do with four sides (10+10+10+10 = 40 m). The teacher learns to anchor the area/perimeter difference in a real job: carpet = inside (area), fence = outside (perimeter).
modules.summary_ur: آپ دیکھیں گے کہ قالین اور باڑ کی ایک کہانی، ٹائلیں گننے اور رسی سے ناپنے کے ذریعے بچوں کو ایریا اور پیرامیٹر کا فرق کیسے سمجھایا جائے۔
symptoms: teacher writes 'Area = L x W' and drills it with no tiles, grid or real object
students add the sides when asked for area (or multiply for perimeter) and the teacher just gives the right answer
area/perimeter lesson with no example from school or home (floor, carpet, boundary wall)
answers for area given without 'square units' / 'square cm'
modules.not_for: Teachers not teaching area and perimeter, or Grade 6+ teachers who need composite shapes and unit conversion; it is a narrated story, not classroom footage.

segments.title_en: Carpet or fence? Area by counting tiles, then L x W
segments.title_ur: قالین یا باڑ؟ ٹائلیں گن کر ایریا، پھر لمبائی × چوڑائی
segments.summary_en: The caretaker's confusion (measure inside or around?) is named as area vs perimeter; the teacher counts 12 one-unit tiles on a classroom floor, says area always measures the inside, then gives Area = length x width with a 4 cm x 3 cm = 12 sq cm diagram.

segments.title_en: Perimeter with a rope round the ground; carpet = area, fence = perimeter
segments.title_ur: میدان کے گرد رسی سے پیرامیٹر؛ قالین = ایریا، باڑ = پیرامیٹر
segments.summary_en: A rope is laid round a 10 m square ground; the teacher asks what to do with four sides and the caretaker works out 40 m. The story closes on the rule (carpet needs the inside area, fencing the outside perimeter) and a tip to tell this story in class.

modules.title: Integrating graphs
modules.teacher_line_en: Teach bar graphs and pictographs from your own class survey
modules.teacher_line_ur: اپنی کلاس کے سروے سے بار گراف اور پکٹوگراف سکھائیں
modules.summary_en: Children run class surveys (best school start time, favourite playground spot, lunch vegetable) in groups, choose which questions to ask and which graph to use. The presenter models a bar graph on the board step by step (axes, marking counts, plotting) and a pictograph with a scale (1 star = 2 students, half a star for 1), then asks which bar or symbol row is longest and shortest so children read the data, not just plot it.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں بچے گروپس میں سروے کرتے ہیں اور بورڈ پر ماڈلنگ کے بعد بار گراف اور پکٹوگراف (پیمانے اور آدھے نشان سمیت) بنا کر ڈیٹا کا تجزیہ کرتے ہیں۔
symptoms: teacher draws a bar graph from book data with no data collected by the children
children copy a graph but are never asked which bar is longest or what it means
pictograph scale (1 symbol = 2) not explained; children unsure what half a symbol means
graph lesson with no link to anything in the children's own school life
modules.not_for: Non-maths teachers and early-grade (1-2) teachers who do not teach graphs; it does not cover line graphs or pie charts.

segments.title_en: A class survey becomes a bar chart
segments.title_ur: کلاس کا سروے بار چارٹ میں
segments.summary_en: Graphs build observation and decision-making; children survey the best school start time and turn the votes into a bar chart to see which option won.

segments.title_en: Groups pick survey questions and graph types
segments.title_ur: گروپ سروے کے سوال اور گراف کی قسم چنیں
segments.summary_en: More survey questions (playground spot, lunch vegetable); divide children into groups who decide which questions to ask first and which type of graph to use.

segments.title_en: Model a bar graph, then read it
segments.title_ur: بار گراف بنا کر دکھائیں، پھر پڑھوائیں
segments.summary_en: Explains bar graph vs pictograph, then models on the board: draw the axes, mark each count (swings 10, slides 7) while saying it aloud, children plot their own data, then ask which bar is longest and shortest and what that means.

segments.title_en: Pictograph with a scale and half symbols
segments.title_ur: پیمانے اور آدھے نشان کے ساتھ پکٹوگراف
segments.summary_en: 1 star = 2 students: 12 likes for potato = 6 stars, 8 for okra = 4, 5 for cauliflower = 2 and a half stars; ask which vegetable has most and fewest symbols and explain why half symbols are needed. Short wrap-up.

modules.title: Patterns
modules.teacher_line_en: Teach patterns as 'find the rule, then extend', plus the 1-to-100 pairing trick
modules.teacher_line_ur: پیٹرن سکھائیں: پہلے اصول پہچانیں، پھر آگے بڑھائیں؛ ساتھ 1 سے 100 جوڑنے کا طریقہ
modules.summary_en: Two different recordings joined together. In the first (Urdu, 0–190 s) a trainer works through repeating, growing and +1/-1 patterns (red-yellow blocks, 1-2-3 squares, 9 down to 5 with 4 missing) and shows how to have children name the rule, then extend the pattern or fill the gap, how to make the rules harder and where to find patterns in real life. The second (English, 198 s to the end) is a session for parents and teachers: the presenter sets 'add 1 to 100 in one minute', gives think time, and solves it by starting small and pairing first and last numbers (5 pairs × 11 = 55 … 50 × 101 = 5050), then talks about adults' attitudes to maths.
modules.summary_ur: آپ دیکھیں گے کہ بچوں سے پیٹرن کا اصول کیسے پہچانوایا جائے، پیٹرن کیسے آگے بڑھایا جائے، اور مشکل سوال کو چھوٹے سے شروع کر کے کیسے حل کیا جائے۔
symptoms: teacher reads a number or shape sequence aloud and children repeat it, but no one is asked 'what is the rule?'
no 'what comes next?' or 'which one is missing?' question during pattern or counting work
teacher sets a hard sum and shows the method straight away, with no think time or 'try a smaller case first'
children's answers are never followed by 'how did you work it out?'
modules.not_for: Teachers of non-maths subjects or Grade 6+ classes; the Urdu pattern chapters are early-primary, and the English part is a parents' session.

segments.title_en: Find the rule, then extend the pattern
segments.title_ur: اصول پہچانیں، پھر پیٹرن آگے بڑھائیں
segments.summary_en: Four worked patterns, each named by its rule: red-yellow A-B blocks, +1 numbers, a growing pattern of 1, 2, 3 blue squares (so the next line has 4), and 9, 8, 7, 6, 5 counting down to the missing 4. The teacher is told to have children name the rule first and then extend the pattern or fill the gap.

segments.title_en: Make patterns harder step by step
segments.title_ur: پیٹرنز کو قدم بہ قدم مشکل بنائیں
segments.summary_en: Ways to raise the difficulty beyond alternating or +1/-1: three repeating shapes, an AAB shape rule, steps of +2, +5, -2, -5, mixed steps (-2, -5) and a constant pattern (2, 2, 2) for spotting rules.

segments.title_en: Patterns in tiles, claps and street lights
segments.title_ur: ٹائلز، تالیوں اور اسٹریٹ لائٹس میں پیٹرن
segments.summary_en: Real-life patterns (tile designs, hand-clap rhythms, street lights that alternate on and off), then children are asked to find patterns at home or nearby and share them in class. Ends with the sign-off of the first recording.

segments.title_en: A hard task: add 1 to 100 in one minute
segments.title_ur: مشکل سوال: 1 سے 100 تک کا مجموعہ ایک منٹ میں
segments.summary_en: A second, English recording begins. The presenter sets a non-routine task (the sum of the first 100 natural numbers), says a 10-year-old did it in one minute, and asks viewers to talk about different strategies for a minute before any help is given.
segments.recommendable_reason: panel_veto: spliced_foreign_recording: English parent/teacher webinar from a different event, adult audience; not a standalone classroom move for a teacher who tapped "Patterns" (ped-panel ruling 18:4xZ, replaces the 18:30Z module veto)

segments.title_en: Strategies people try, and noticing a pattern
segments.title_ur: مختلف طریقے اور پیٹرن کو پہچاننا
segments.summary_en: Goes through the usual strategies: add the numbers one by one, or use a calculator or Excel in blocks of ten (55, 155, 255…) until a pattern shows and gives 5050. It also covers the 'too hard, I give up' response.
segments.recommendable_reason: panel_veto: spliced_foreign_recording: English parent/teacher webinar from a different event, adult audience; not a standalone classroom move for a teacher who tapped "Patterns" (ped-panel ruling 18:4xZ, replaces the 18:30Z module veto)

segments.title_en: Start small: pair first and last numbers
segments.title_ur: چھوٹے سے شروع کریں: پہلا اور آخری نمبر جوڑیں
segments.summary_en: The 'start small' heuristic: work with 1 to 10, ask what the first and last numbers add to (11), check 2+9, 3+8, 4+7 and 5+6, and conclude 5 pairs × 11 = 55, explaining why the shortcut works.

segments.title_en: Generalise: 20, 40, then 100 numbers
segments.title_ur: عام اصول: 20، 40 اور پھر 100 نمبر
segments.summary_en: The same pairing idea is applied to 1 to 20 (10 pairs × 21 = 210) and 1 to 40 (20 × 41 = 820), and finally to the original task: 50 pairs × 101 = 5050.
segments.recommendable_reason: panel_veto: spliced_foreign_recording: English parent/teacher webinar from a different event, adult audience; not a standalone classroom move for a teacher who tapped "Patterns" (ped-panel ruling 18:4xZ, replaces the 18:30Z module veto)

segments.title_en: Session aims recap; ask 'how did you do it?'
segments.title_ur: سیشن کا خلاصہ؛ بچے سے پوچھیں 'آپ نے کیسے کیا؟'
segments.summary_en: Recap of the session aims (adults' role in a positive attitude to maths; relationships and patterns in every topic), with one practical point: after any activity, give the child time to explain 'how did you do this?'.
segments.recommendable_reason: panel_veto: spliced_foreign_recording: English parent/teacher webinar from a different event, adult audience; not a standalone classroom move for a teacher who tapped "Patterns" (ped-panel ruling 18:4xZ, replaces the 18:30Z module veto)

segments.title_en: Parents' attitude to maths; sign-off
segments.title_ur: ریاضی کے بارے میں والدین کا رویہ؛ اختتام
segments.summary_en: Principles for parents: children copy adults' attitude to maths, every child has maths potential, avoid gender stereotypes, and play maths games. Ends with thanks and contact details.
segments.recommendable_reason: panel_veto: spliced_foreign_recording: English parent/teacher webinar from a different event, adult audience; not a standalone classroom move for a teacher who tapped "Patterns" (ped-panel ruling 18:4xZ, replaces the 18:30Z module veto)

modules.title: Building phonic foundations
modules.teacher_line_en: Children mix up short and long vowels? Try actions, word sorting and CVC blending
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے چھوٹی اور لمبی آواز میں الجھتے ہیں؟ اشارے، الفاظ کی چھانٹی اور آوازیں ملانا آزمائیں
modules.summary_en: The trainer explains the five English vowels and the difference between short sounds (a as in apple) and long sounds that say the letter name (a as in cake), taught with a chant children repeat. Four practice activities follow: an action for each vowel sound (eat an apple, elephant trunk), sorting words like cat, bed, fish, dog, sun into five vowel boxes on the board, group vowel hunts in the textbook, and blending CVC words (c-a-t) by tapping or finger-stretching.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ انگریزی حروفِ علت کی چھوٹی اور لمبی آواز نظم، اشاروں، الفاظ کی چھانٹی اور تین حرفی الفاظ ملا کر پڑھنے سے کیسے سکھائیں۔
symptoms: children recite the alphabet or vowel names but cannot give the short sound
teacher reads the word and children repeat it whole, with no sounding out c-a-t
no actions, sorting or game in a phonics lesson; only chorus repetition
children guess words from the picture instead of blending
modules.not_for: Teachers of Urdu reading or of children who already read CVC words fluently (Grade 4+).

segments.title_en: Short and long vowel sounds, taught with a chant
segments.title_ur: چھوٹی اور لمبی آواز والے حروفِ علت، نظم کے ساتھ
segments.summary_en: The five vowels, short sounds (apple, egg) vs long sounds that say the letter name (cake, bee), and a chant the teacher says and children repeat to tell them apart.

segments.title_en: An action for every vowel sound
segments.title_ur: ہر آواز کے ساتھ ایک اشارہ
segments.summary_en: Each vowel is linked to a word and an action (eat an apple, elephant trunk, igloo roof, octopus fingers, umbrella); children copy and repeat.

segments.title_en: Sort words into vowel boxes
segments.title_ur: الفاظ کو حروفِ علت کے خانوں میں رکھیں
segments.summary_en: Five boxes on the board (or five notebook columns); children write cat, bed, fish, dog, sun in the right vowel box, no flash cards needed.

segments.title_en: Vowel hunt in groups
segments.title_ur: گروپ میں حروفِ علت کی تلاش
segments.summary_en: Groups each hunt and circle words with one vowel in the textbook or a chart.

segments.title_en: Blend CVC words by tapping or finger-stretching
segments.title_ur: تین حرفی الفاظ کی آوازیں ملا کر پڑھنا
segments.summary_en: Consonant-vowel-consonant words: the teacher models c-a-t, then children blend by tapping or finger-stretching.

segments.title_en: Recap of the four strategies
segments.title_ur: چاروں طریقوں کا خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Recap of actions, sorting, vowel hunt and CVC building; goodbye.

modules.title: Multi-Literacy Skills
modules.teacher_line_en: Reading lesson ends at the book? Plan read → talk in pairs → write a summary
modules.teacher_line_ur: سبق صرف پڑھنے پر ختم ہو جاتا ہے؟ پڑھیں، جوڑیوں میں بات کریں، پھر خلاصہ لکھیں
modules.summary_en: An English-language podcast conversation on planning one literacy lesson (or a short unit) that joins reading, oral discussion and writing. The guest models three measurable objectives for a Grade 4 story (read the story, discuss the main idea in pairs, write a 5-sentence summary with sentence starters) tied to the curriculum outcome 'identify the main idea', then a pre-reading routine (new words on the board, a 'Have you ever been to a bazaar?' prior-knowledge question) and the sequence read → talk → write spread over three days. The teacher learns to plan the writing task from the text, give struggling learners sentence starters ('I think… because…') and strong–struggling pairs, and keep a short reflection log after the lesson.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ سیکھیں گے کہ ایک ہی سبق میں پڑھنا، بات چیت اور لکھنا کیسے جوڑیں: قابلِ پیمائش مقاصد، پڑھنے سے پہلے نئے الفاظ، پھر جوڑیوں میں گفتگو اور جملوں کے آغاز کے ساتھ خلاصہ لکھنا۔
symptoms: students read the text aloud or the teacher reads it, and the lesson ends with no pair discussion and no writing about it
no objective stated, or only 'today we will read lesson 5' with nothing students will say or write
teacher starts reading straight away: no new words introduced and no 'have you ever…?' question before the text
a writing task is set ('write about it') with no sentence starters or model, and weaker children write nothing
modules.not_for: Maths or science teachers, and early-grade teachers whose children cannot yet decode a short text; it is an English talk with no classroom footage.

segments.title_en: Podcast intro: planning multi-skill literacy lessons
segments.title_ur: تعارف: کئی مہارتوں والے خواندگی کے اسباق کی منصوبہ بندی
segments.summary_en: The host introduces the episode on integrating reading, writing and oral language in one lesson, introduces the guest, and says integration feels hard to start.

segments.title_en: Three measurable objectives and choosing the text
segments.title_ur: تین قابلِ پیمائش مقاصد اور متن کا انتخاب
segments.summary_en: For a Grade 4 story the guest writes one objective per skill (read the story, discuss the main idea in pairs, write a 5-sentence summary with sentence starters), checks each is measurable and tied to the outcome 'identify the main idea', then picks grade-appropriate texts that invite talk and writing.

segments.title_en: Pre-reading: new words and a prior-knowledge question
segments.title_ur: پڑھنے سے پہلے: نئے الفاظ اور پہلے سے معلوم باتوں پر سوال
segments.summary_en: Before reading, the teacher writes new words on the board and explains them, then asks 'Have you ever been to a bazaar? What did you see there?' to activate prior knowledge; struggling learners get visuals, Urdu-English word lists and a partner.

segments.title_en: Read → talk → write, with sentence starters for weaker learners
segments.title_ur: پڑھنا، بولنا، لکھنا: کمزور بچوں کے لیے جملوں کے آغاز
segments.summary_en: The lesson runs reading, then oral discussion, then writing, spread over a unit (Day 1 reading plus discussion, Day 2 vocabulary plus guided writing, Day 3 extended writing with peer feedback); struggling learners get 'I think… because…' starters, a stronger partner and visuals.

segments.title_en: Reflecting after the lesson: four questions and a log
segments.title_ur: سبق کے بعد غور: چار سوال اور ایک ڈائری
segments.summary_en: After the lesson the teacher asks: did students use all three skills, were objectives aligned, did weaker learners get scaffolds, did the flow connect to the next day; and writes a log line such as 'discussion went well, writing was weak, plan more guided writing'.

segments.title_en: Wrap-up and task: plan your own integrated lesson
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ اور کام: اپنا مربوط سبق بنائیں
segments.summary_en: The host recaps that reading, writing and oral language should be planned together and asks teachers to choose a text and plan how students will read, discuss and write about it.

modules.title: Degrees of Adjectives, Adverbs, and more complex grammar
modules.teacher_line_en: Teach 'long, longer, longest' with real pencils, a comparison race and an acting game
modules.teacher_line_ur: کلاس کی پنسلوں، مقابلے کے کھیل اور اداکاری سے 'long, longer, longest' سکھائیں
modules.summary_en: A presenter teaches adjectives vs adverbs side by side ('Ali is careful' / 'Ali works carefully'), then positive, comparative and superlative forms with short rules (tall-taller-tallest; more/most for longer words) and asks why we say 'more beautiful' not 'beautiful-er'. Teachers see four classroom activities: comparing real pencils and books ('long, longer, longest'), a 'comparison race' in groups with 'Why faster, not more fast?', an acting game ('Walk slowly', 'Walk carefully'), and adding adjectives and adverbs to a short story.
modules.summary_ur: آپ دیکھیں گے کہ انگریزی میں adjectives اور adverbs کے درجے کلاس کی چیزوں، مقابلے کے کھیل، اداکاری اور کہانی کے ذریعے کیسے سکھائیں۔
symptoms: grammar lesson where the teacher reads the rule and students copy 'tall, taller, tallest' tables from the board
students mix up adjectives and adverbs ('he runs quick', 'she is carefully')
no object, action or game is used; only textbook sentences
students never asked why a form is used ('why more beautiful?')
modules.not_for: Teachers of Grades 1-2 or of Urdu-only classes; it is English grammar content for upper-primary teachers, spoken in English.

segments.title_en: Intro: why teach grammar in context
segments.title_ur: تعارف: گرامر سیاق و سباق میں کیوں
segments.summary_en: Greeting; 'This is a mango' vs 'This is a very sweet mango' to show why adjectives and adverbs make speech and writing richer.

segments.title_en: Adjective vs adverb, side by side
segments.title_ur: صفت اور متعلق فعل کا فرق، ساتھ ساتھ
segments.summary_en: Adjective describes a noun ('small book'), adverb describes a verb ('reading clearly'); compare 'Ali is careful' with 'Ali works carefully'.

segments.title_en: Degrees of comparison and why 'more beautiful'
segments.title_ur: موازنے کے درجے اور قاعدے کی وجہ
segments.summary_en: Positive, comparative, superlative; -er/-est for short words, more/most for longer words and adverbs, irregular forms; discuss why it is 'more beautiful' not 'beautiful-er'. Note: the irregular list is spoken as 'bad, worst, worst' (should be bad, worse, worst).

segments.title_en: Compare real pencils, books and classroom actions
segments.title_ur: اصلی پنسلوں، کتابوں اور کاموں کا موازنہ
segments.summary_en: Board sentences on 'beautiful / more beautiful / most beautiful' with 'How has the meaning changed?', then 'This pencil is long, that one is longer, this marker is the longest' and 'reads clearly / more clearly / most clearly' with classroom examples.

segments.title_en: Comparison race and an acting game
segments.title_ur: مقابلے کی دوڑ اور اداکاری کا کھیل
segments.summary_en: Groups play 'Comparison race' ('Ali is fast. Who is faster? Who is the fastest?'), the teacher asks 'Why faster, not more fast?', then children act out 'Walk slowly / quickly / carefully'.

segments.title_en: Story with added adjectives, and recap
segments.title_ur: کہانی میں نئے الفاظ اور خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: 'Once there was a very brave boy...' read aloud, then students add their own adjectives and adverbs; recap of the strategies and two leftover lines on highlighting describing words in a read-aloud.

modules.title: Writing Paragraphs
modules.teacher_line_en: Students can't write a paragraph? Model one, outline together, then let them try
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے پیراگراف نہیں لکھ پاتے؟ پہلے ماڈل دکھائیں، خاکہ بنوائیں، پھر خود لکھوائیں
modules.summary_en: A presenter, reading slide-style headings, breaks a paragraph into topic sentence, supporting details and concluding sentence and models one on grasshoppers ('Grasshoppers eat many different types of food...'). Students then outline their own paragraph on a playground by asking 'What do I know? What details? How do I conclude?' before writing it neatly. A second part contrasts narrative paragraphs (first, next, finally) with descriptive ones (sensory details, adjectives), same three-part structure.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ ایک ماڈل پیراگراف دکھا کر بچوں کو ٹاپک سینٹینس، تفصیلات اور اختتامی جملے والا پیراگراف خود لکھنا کیسے سکھائیں۔
symptoms: students told 'write a paragraph on X' with no model paragraph or outline shown first
teacher dictates a paragraph for copying; students never draft their own
no mention of topic sentence, main idea or concluding sentence in a writing lesson
story or description task given with no sequence words or describing words modelled
modules.not_for: Teachers of Grade 1-3 still on sentence writing, or Urdu-only teachers; it is an English talk with no classroom footage.

segments.title_en: Intro: what a paragraph is and today's goals
segments.title_ur: تعارف: پیراگراف کیا ہے اور آج کے مقاصد
segments.summary_en: Greeting, a paragraph as a small story around one main idea, and the list of what the video will cover.

segments.title_en: Three parts modelled (grasshoppers), then students outline and write
segments.title_ur: تین حصے ماڈل کے ساتھ، پھر بچے خاکہ بنا کر لکھیں
segments.summary_en: Make a rough outline with students; the three parts are named and modelled on a grasshopper paragraph, then students outline a paragraph about a playground with three self-questions and write it neatly.

segments.title_en: Narrative vs descriptive paragraphs, same structure
segments.title_ur: بیانیہ اور توضیحی پیراگراف، ایک ہی ڈھانچہ
segments.summary_en: Narrative paragraphs tell a sequence with first/next/finally; descriptive ones paint a picture with sensory details and adjectives (park examples); both keep topic sentence, details, conclusion, and teachers should model both.

modules.title: Develop narrative fluency
modules.teacher_line_en: Get children talking in sequence: first, next, finally, with a partner
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچوں کو first, next, finally سے جوڑی میں بولنا سکھائیں
modules.summary_en: The presenter models three speaking-and-listening activities in English with Urdu explanation: describing a park picture with first / next / finally and sentence starters, retelling a short story ('Ali went to the market…') in pairs with sequence cards while the partner checks the order, and narrating a personal event that the partner summarises and gives feedback on. It ends with a 6-week progression and an end-of-class checklist (sequence words? in order? clear?).
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں تصویر بیان کرنے، کہانی دوبارہ سنانے اور اپنے واقعات سنانے کی سرگرمیوں سے بچوں کی انگریزی بولنے اور سننے کی روانی بڑھانا دکھایا گیا ہے۔
symptoms: in an English lesson children only repeat words or sentences after the teacher in chorus
children never speak more than one word or one sentence of their own
no pair talk; only the teacher speaks English
children retell or describe without any order words (first, then, finally)
modules.not_for: Maths or science teachers, and English teachers looking for reading or grammar; it covers oral narration only.

segments.title_en: What narrative fluency is (intro)
segments.title_ur: بیانیہ روانی کیا ہے (تعارف)
segments.summary_en: Greeting; narrative fluency means expressing ideas in sequence, with detail and clear language; the curriculum asks for short sentences, retelling and narrating experiences.

segments.title_en: Picture description with sentence starters
segments.title_ur: جملوں کے آغاز کے ساتھ تصویر بیان کرنا
