segments.summary_en: The teacher models describing a park picture ('First, I see two children on the swing… Next… Finally…'), gives starters (I see, next, I notice, finally) and children narrate; 2-3 sentences in lower grades, 3-5 lines in higher ones.

segments.title_en: Pair retell with sequence cards
segments.title_ur: سیکوئنس کارڈ کے ساتھ جوڑی میں کہانی دوبارہ سنانا
segments.summary_en: The teacher tells a 4-sentence story ('Ali went to the market…'); in pairs children retell it in their own words with first / then / finally cards while the listener checks the order.

segments.title_en: Personal narratives with partner summary and feedback
segments.title_ur: اپنا واقعہ سنائیں، ساتھی خلاصہ اور رائے دے
segments.summary_en: The teacher models a personal event ('Last Sunday I visited my grandmother…'); children narrate their own event to a partner, who summarises it and says whether they used first / next / finally and whether it made sense.

segments.title_en: Six-week progression and an end-of-class checklist
segments.title_ur: چھ ہفتوں کی ترتیب اور کلاس کے آخر میں چیک لسٹ
segments.summary_en: Build up from single-sentence picture description (week 1) to multi-paragraph personal narratives (weeks 4-6); end each class with a quick checklist or peer feedback to see who needs more support.

segments.title_en: Recap of the three strategies and planning task
segments.title_ur: تینوں طریقوں کا خلاصہ اور منصوبہ بندی
segments.summary_en: Recaps picture prompts, sequence-card retells and personal narratives with peer feedback, then asks the teacher to design one listening-speaking activity.

modules.title: Continuous and perfect tenses
modules.teacher_line_en: Use a board timeline so children see 'is playing' vs 'has played' at a glance
modules.teacher_line_ur: بورڈ پر ٹائم لائن سے بچوں کو 'is playing' اور 'has played' کا فرق دکھائیں
modules.summary_en: A trainer teaches present continuous vs present perfect with a timeline on the board ('I'm studying now' vs 'I have studied'), a transformation drill ('Ali plays cricket' to 'Ali is playing' and 'Ali has played'), and examples from the children's own day. In a group task children decide which tense a sentence is and where it sits on the timeline, using a clue chart (is/am/are + -ing = continuous; has/have + third form = perfect), with weaker students paired with stronger ones.
modules.summary_ur: آپ ٹائم لائن، جملوں کی تبدیلی اور روزمرہ مثالوں سے بچوں کو کنٹینیوس اور پرفیکٹ ٹینس کا فرق سکھانا سیکھیں گے۔
symptoms: teacher reads tense rules or formulas aloud with no example of when the action happens
children mix up 'is eating' and 'has eaten' and the teacher only repeats the rule
tense practice is copying sentences from the book; children never change one sentence across tenses
no example sentence comes from the children's own day
modules.not_for: Teachers of Urdu, maths or lower-primary English who are not yet teaching verb tenses.

segments.title_en: Why tenses matter: eating vs has eaten
segments.title_ur: ٹینس کیوں ضروری ہیں: کھا رہی ہے اور کھا چکی ہے
segments.summary_en: Introduces the module and contrasts 'She's eating' (happening now) with 'She has eaten' (completed) to show that tenses express time.

segments.title_en: Board timeline and sentence transformation drill
segments.title_ur: بورڈ پر ٹائم لائن اور جملوں کی تبدیلی کی مشق
segments.summary_en: Draws a timeline to place 'I'm studying now' and 'I have studied', then has children turn 'Ali plays cricket' into continuous and perfect forms.

segments.title_en: Real-life sentences and a group tense task with clue chart
segments.title_ur: روزمرہ جملے اور کلو چارٹ کے ساتھ گروپ کام
segments.summary_en: Uses the children's own day ('you're sitting in class', 'you've done your homework'), then groups label sentences by tense and place them on the timeline, with a clue chart and mixed-ability pairs.

segments.title_en: Recap of the four strategies
segments.title_ur: چاروں طریقوں کا خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Lists the four methods again (timelines, transformations, real-life examples, group activities) and signs off.

modules.title: Diagnosing and Correcting Errors in Sentence Construction, Spelling, and Punctuation
modules.teacher_line_en: Correcting every copy yourself? Teach pupils a 3-question checklist to edit each other
modules.teacher_line_ur: ہر کاپی خود درست کرتے ہیں؟ بچوں کو تین سوالوں کی چیک لسٹ سے آپس میں کام جانچنا سکھائیں
modules.summary_en: The trainer walks through common writing errors with wrong and corrected English sentences: fragments ('Because Ali was late.'), run-ons and misplaced modifiers, spelling errors from sound-letter confusion (writing 'difrent'), and punctuation that changes meaning (missing comma, quotation marks). Teachers learn to put incorrect and correct sentences side by side on the board and ask what differs, set error-correction sentences, and run pair self- and peer-editing with a three-question checklist (complete sentence? spelling? punctuation?).
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ بچوں کی جملہ سازی، ہجے اور رموزِ اوقاف کی عام غلطیاں کیسے پہچانیں، غلط اور صحیح جملے ساتھ لکھ کر فرق پوچھیں، اور چیک لسٹ سے بچوں کو خود اور ایک دوسرے کا کام درست کرنا سکھائیں۔
symptoms: teacher marks writing errors with a cross or rewrites the sentence, with no explanation of the error
children write fragments or run-on sentences and no one asks what is missing
spelling corrected only by the teacher saying the right spelling; no breaking words into sounds
no self-check or peer-check step before work is handed in
modules.not_for: Teachers of early readers still learning letters, or of non-English lessons.

segments.title_en: Why diagnosing writing errors matters
segments.title_ur: تحریری غلطیوں کی تشخیص کیوں ضروری ہے
segments.summary_en: Intro: the skill is in the national English curriculum; diagnosing and correcting errors builds clarity and confidence.

segments.title_en: Fragments, run-ons and misplaced modifiers, wrong vs right
segments.title_ur: ادھورے جملے، جڑے ہوئے جملے اور غلط جگہ صفت: غلط اور صحیح
segments.summary_en: Each error with a wrong and corrected sentence; write both on the board and ask children what differs, have pairs read the correct and incorrect versions aloud; adjust example difficulty by grade.

segments.title_en: Spelling errors from sound-letter confusion
segments.title_ur: آواز اور حرف کی الجھن سے ہجے کی غلطیاں
segments.summary_en: Break hard words into syllables; most spelling errors come from writing what is heard ('difrent', 'cause' as 'kaas'), so work on phonemic awareness; spelling buddies check each other's work.

segments.title_en: Punctuation that changes meaning
segments.title_ur: رموزِ اوقاف جو مطلب بدل دیتے ہیں
segments.summary_en: Missing full stops, commas, question and quotation marks; a comma example that changes meaning; then give practice sentences with errors for children to correct.

segments.title_en: Self- and peer-editing with a three-question checklist
segments.title_ur: تین سوالوں کی چیک لسٹ سے خود اور ساتھی کا کام جانچنا
segments.summary_en: Instead of only teacher correction: a checklist (complete sentence? correct spelling? right punctuation?) and a pair activity where one writes and the other checks.

segments.title_en: Where this fits in the writing series; recap
segments.title_ur: تحریری سلسلے میں اس سبق کی جگہ اور خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Overview of the writing series (ideas, sentences, paragraphs, extended writing) and a recap; no new technique.

modules.title: Scaffolding Oral Language through Structured Speaking Activities
modules.teacher_line_en: Children answer in one word? Give sentence starters, then fade them
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے ایک لفظ میں جواب دیتے ہیں؟ جملے کے آغاز دیں، پھر آہستہ آہستہ ہٹا دیں
modules.summary_en: A trainer shows three scaffolds that get children speaking in full sentences: sentence starters on the board or flash cards ('I think...', 'because...', 'The answer is 12 because I added 6 and 6'), retelling with a First/Then/After that/Finally sequence chart (a lemonade experiment), and structured pair dialogues the teacher models first ('What did you do yesterday?'). The teacher learns to fade the frames so children move to their own words.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ سیکھیں گے کہ جملے کے آغاز، ترتیب والے چارٹ اور جوڑیوں میں مکالمے سے بچوں کو مکمل جملوں میں بولنا کیسے سکھائیں۔
symptoms: children answer in single words or stay silent when asked to speak
teacher completes the children's half sentences for them
no 'because' in any student answer; teacher never asks for a reason
retelling or explaining a process is done by the teacher, not the children
modules.not_for: Teachers whose students already speak at length in full sentences, or whose need is reading or phonics rather than speaking.

segments.title_en: Why children stay silent without support
segments.title_ur: سہارے کے بغیر بچے کیوں چپ رہتے ہیں
segments.summary_en: Introduces structured speaking: with support children gain confidence and fluency, without it they stay silent or speak in incomplete sentences.

segments.title_en: Sentence starters
segments.title_ur: جملے کے آغاز (سینٹینس اسٹارٹرز)
segments.summary_en: Write starters like 'I think...', 'because...', 'First... Next... Finally...' on the board or flash cards and set a task where children use them, e.g. 'The answer is 12 because I added 6 and 6.'

segments.title_en: Retelling with a sequence chart
segments.title_ur: ترتیب والے چارٹ سے کہانی دوبارہ سنانا
segments.summary_en: Children retell a story, event or experiment using a First/Then/After that/Finally chart on the board, copied into their notebooks; modelled with a lemonade-making experiment.

segments.title_en: Structured pair dialogues, then fade the frames
segments.title_ur: جوڑیوں میں مکالمہ اور پھر سہارا کم کرنا
segments.summary_en: Pairs role-play a scenario ('What did you do yesterday?' 'I played football. What about you?'); the teacher models first, pairs practise, and sentence frames are slowly removed.

segments.title_en: Recap of the three strategies
segments.title_ur: تینوں حکمت عملیوں کا خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Recaps sentence starters, retelling and structured dialogues and the idea of fading scaffolds; sign-off.

modules.title: مرکب الفاظ
modules.teacher_line_en: Children join word cards in pairs to make compound words, then use them in sentences
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے جوڑیوں میں کارڈ ملا کر مرکب الفاظ بنائیں اور پھر جملوں میں استعمال کریں
modules.summary_en: A presenter defines compound words (مرکب الفاظ) with English (sun + flower = sunflower, tooth + brush = toothbrush) and Urdu examples (صبح و شام، آب و ہوا، کارخانہ). Teachers see a pair activity joining word cards (or paper slips, or words written on children's hands) into compound words, model sentences on the board, sentence starters with a word bank for children to complete, and a 'spot and sort' task where children underline the compound words in a mixed list, plus a short checklist and reflection question to check learning.
modules.summary_ur: آپ دیکھیں گے کہ مرکب الفاظ کو کارڈ جوڑنے کی سرگرمی، بورڈ پر نمونے کے جملوں، جملے شروع کرنے والے الفاظ اور 'ڈھونڈو اور چھانٹو' سرگرمی سے کیسے سکھائیں۔
symptoms: vocabulary lesson where the teacher only reads word meanings and children copy them
no card, slip or game; children never build or sort words themselves
children are given new words but never asked to use them in a sentence
teacher never checks which children can pick out the new words
modules.not_for: Teachers of Grade 4+ or of maths and science lessons; it is early-grade Urdu/English word-building content.

segments.title_en: What compound words are: English and Urdu examples
segments.title_ur: مرکب الفاظ کیا ہیں: انگریزی اور اردو مثالیں
segments.summary_en: Greeting, then the definition: two words join to make a new word with a new meaning; sunflower, rainbow, classroom, toothbrush; صبح و شام، عجیب و غریب، آب و ہوا، روزمرہ، کارخانہ.

segments.title_en: Joining activity with cards in pairs
segments.title_ur: جوڑیوں میں کارڈ جوڑنے کی سرگرمی
segments.summary_en: Use word cards, paper slips, or words written on children's hands; pairs join 'sun' + 'flower' or 'آب' + 'ہوا' into a compound word and tell the class its meaning.

segments.title_en: Model sentences and sentence starters
segments.title_ur: نمونے کے جملے اور جملے کی شروعات
segments.summary_en: Model sentences on the board ('اس شہر کی آب و ہوا خوشگوار ہے', 'I put my toothbrush in the cup'), then sentence starters with a word bank so children choose the right compound word to finish each one.

segments.title_en: Spot and sort
segments.title_ur: ڈھونڈو اور چھانٹو
segments.summary_en: Children copy a mixed word list and underline only the 6 compound words; the class discusses answers and children who erred revise the examples.

segments.title_en: Recap, success checklist and reflection
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ، کامیابی کی فہرست اور سوچ بچار
segments.summary_en: Recap of the four steps, what to look for in children's copies (correct joining, meaning, usage) and a closing question: which compound word was easiest or hardest today, and why?

modules.title: تشکیل، مذکر  اور مونث
modules.teacher_line_en: Children write 'larki gaya'? A quick routine to catch gender and tense slips in Urdu
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے 'لڑکی گیا' لکھتے ہیں؟ مذکر مونث اور زمانے کی غلطیاں پکڑنے کا آسان طریقہ
modules.summary_en: A presenter walks through Urdu sentence building on step slides: simple sentences (one is corrected for verb gender), joining two with اور/لیکن into compound sentences, complex sentences with جب/اگر/جو, harakat on look-alike words (علم knowledge vs flag), and gender and tense agreement errors ('وہ لڑکی گیا' -> 'گئی', 'کل وہ جاتا ہے' -> 'گیا تھا / جائے گا'). Classroom tips: a pair activity where one child says the sentence right and one wrong, a joining-word bank on the board used orally then in copies, and a check routine (is the subject masculine/feminine, singular/plural, then the tense).
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ سادہ جملوں سے مرکب اور پیچیدہ جملے کیسے بنوائیں، اعراب سے معنی کیسے واضح کریں، اور مذکر مونث و زمانے کی عام غلطیاں کیسے پکڑیں۔
symptoms: students say or write 'larki gaya' / mismatched gender and verb, and the teacher only says 'ghalat' without naming the rule
Urdu writing lesson where every sentence is copied from the book; nothing joined with اور / لیکن / جب / اگر
teacher never asks students to check whether the subject is masculine/feminine or singular/plural before the verb
look-alike words (علم) read wrongly and no harakat marked to fix the meaning
modules.not_for: Teachers of English, maths or science, or of Grade 1-2 children still learning letters; it is a talk with no classroom footage.

segments.title_en: Simple sentences and a gender correction, with a pair activity
segments.title_ur: سادہ جملے، مذکر مونث کی درستی اور جوڑی کی سرگرمی
segments.summary_en: After a short intro, the simple sentence pattern with three examples; 'علی کتاب پڑھتی ہے' is corrected because the subject is masculine, and pairs practise one child saying the sentence right and one wrong.

segments.title_en: Compound and complex sentences with joining words
segments.title_ur: مرکب اور پیچیدہ جملے، جوڑنے والے الفاظ کے ساتھ
segments.summary_en: Two sentences are joined with اور / لیکن into compound sentences, then جب / اگر / جو build complex ones; put a word bank of joining words on the board and have children use them orally, then in copies.

segments.title_en: Harakat that change meaning (علم: knowledge or flag)
segments.title_ur: اعراب جو معنی بدل دیتے ہیں (علم: علم یا جھنڈا)
segments.summary_en: Zabar, zer, pesh and shadd make meaning clear where words look alike (علم as knowledge vs flag); mark harakat wherever a sentence is hard or misread, using a board table of examples.

segments.title_en: Gender and tense errors and a check routine
segments.title_ur: مذکر مونث اور زمانے کی غلطیاں اور جانچ کا طریقہ
segments.summary_en: Common errors are named and fixed ('وہ لڑکی گیا', 'چھوٹی لڑکا', 'کل وہ جاتا ہے'), and children are taught to check the subject's gender and number, then the tense, before speaking.

segments.title_en: Recap and close
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ اور اختتام
segments.summary_en: Recap of the three skills and advice to model them; sign-off.

modules.title: بنیادی تحریری مہارتیں
modules.teacher_line_en: Model a paragraph: mind map, topic sentence, first-next-finally, close
modules.teacher_line_ur: مائنڈ میپ سے پیراگراف تک: لکھنا ماڈل کر کے سکھائیں
modules.summary_en: The presenter shows how to model writing in English and Urdu: a 'My School' mind map on the board, an outline (topic sentence, three details, concluding sentence), then a think-aloud paragraph ('My school is a happy place… First… Next… Finally… That is why I love my school') with starters children complete. It then gives informal and formal letter formats (a letter to a friend, a leave application to the principal) and daily-use sentence starters ('I want…', 'مجھے… چاہیے'), ending with model → guided → independent writing.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں مائنڈ میپ، خاکہ اور ماڈل پیراگراف کے ذریعے بچوں کو انگریزی اور اردو میں پیراگراف، خط اور روزمرہ جملے لکھنا سکھایا گیا ہے۔
symptoms: teacher says 'write a paragraph on My School' with no model, outline or mind map
children copy a paragraph from the board instead of writing their own
no sentence starters or topic/concluding sentence mentioned in a writing lesson
letter writing taught by dictation with no format shown
modules.not_for: Maths or science teachers, and early-grade teachers still teaching letter formation; it is about organising paragraphs, letters and sentences.

segments.title_en: Organise ideas first with a mind map
segments.title_ur: لکھنے سے پہلے مائنڈ میپ سے خیالات ترتیب دیں
segments.summary_en: After a short intro, draw a circle with 'My School' on the board and branches where children add ideas (classrooms, teachers, playground, friends) as supporting details.

segments.title_en: Outline, then think aloud a model paragraph
segments.title_ur: خاکہ بنائیں، پھر بول کر ماڈل پیراگراف لکھیں
segments.summary_en: An outline of topic sentence, three details and a concluding sentence, then the teacher thinks aloud 'My school is a happy place… First… Next… Finally… That is why I love my school' in English and Urdu and gives starters children complete themselves.

segments.title_en: Informal and formal letter formats
segments.title_ur: غیر رسمی اور رسمی خط کا فارمیٹ
segments.summary_en: Model letters as templates: 'Dear Ali, how are you?… Your friend Ahmad' and a leave application to the principal, each in English and Urdu. Note: the formal closing is modelled as "Your obediently" (should be "Yours obediently").

segments.title_en: Daily-use sentences with starters; model, guide, then let go
segments.title_ur: روزمرہ جملے؛ پہلے ماڈل، پھر رہنمائی، پھر خود
segments.summary_en: Practise everyday sentences ('I'm feeling hungry', 'May I drink water?') with starters such as 'I want…', 'مجھے… چاہیے' that children complete their own way; reminder to model, then scaffold guided practice, then independent writing.

modules.title: واحد/جمع, تذکیر/تانیث,اور  فاعل/مفعول
modules.teacher_line_en: Picture cards and sorting games for singular/plural, gender and subject/object in Urdu
modules.teacher_line_ur: تصویری کارڈز اور چھانٹنے کے کھیل سے واحد جمع، تذکیر تانیث اور فاعل مفعول سکھائیں
modules.summary_en: A trainer teaches three Urdu grammar ideas in order, each with an aid and a short activity: singular/plural with one-apple vs three-apple picture cards that groups sort into two boxes, then 'what is this, and what if there are more?'; masculine/feminine with a gender-swap ('لڑکا اسکول جاتا ہے' to 'لڑکی اسکول جاتی ہے') done orally and in writing; and subject/object with an arrow diagram and name cards children place into two columns to build a sentence. It ends with a quick oral quiz idea for the end of the lesson.
modules.summary_ur: آپ تصویری کارڈز، جنس بدلنے کی مشق اور تیر والے خاکے سے بچوں کو واحد جمع، تذکیر تانیث اور فاعل مفعول سکھانا سیکھیں گے۔
symptoms: teacher dictates singular-plural or masculine-feminine lists for children to copy
grammar terms (واحد، جمع، فاعل، مفعول) are defined but children never sort or change real words
no picture, card or board diagram is used for an Urdu grammar lesson
lesson ends with no question that checks whether children can find the plural or the فاعل
modules.not_for: Teachers of maths, science or English, or of older Urdu classes already working on advanced grammar.

segments.title_en: Introduction: three grammar ideas
segments.title_ur: تعارف: قواعد کے تین موضوعات
segments.summary_en: Greets teachers, names the three topics and says why grammar concepts strengthen reading, writing, speaking and listening.

segments.title_en: Singular and plural: picture cards and a sorting game
segments.title_ur: واحد اور جمع: تصویری کارڈز اور چھانٹنے کا کھیل
segments.summary_en: Examples (کتاب/کتابیں، لڑکا/لڑکے), one-apple vs three-apple cards, groups sort picture cards into واحد and جمع boxes, then oral questions 'what is this, what if there are more?'.

segments.title_en: Masculine and feminine: gender-swap sentences
segments.title_ur: تذکیر اور تانیث: جملے کی جنس بدلنا
segments.summary_en: Defines تذکیر and تانیث, shows noun and verb both change (کھیلتا/کھیلتی), then children turn 'لڑکا اسکول جاتا ہے' into 'لڑکی اسکول جاتی ہے' orally and in writing.

segments.title_en: Subject and object: arrow diagram and card columns
segments.title_ur: فاعل اور مفعول: تیر کا خاکہ اور کارڈز کے کالم
segments.summary_en: An arrow shows the doer (فاعل) and the one acted on (مفعول); children place name cards (علی، بلی، فٹبال، کتاب) in two columns and build a sentence; teachers design a similar activity.

segments.title_en: End-of-lesson oral quiz and sign-off
segments.title_ur: سبق کے آخر میں زبانی کوئز
segments.summary_en: Recaps the links between the three topics and suggests a quick oral quiz (what is the plural, masculine or feminine, find the فاعل and مفعول), then signs off.

modules.title: اسم، فعل، صفت، ضمیر، حرفِ جار، حرفِ عطف، ندا، استفہام
modules.teacher_line_en: Grammar taught as a list of definitions? Let children change a sentence and see why
modules.teacher_line_ur: گرامر صرف تعریفیں رٹوانا؟ بچوں سے جملہ بدلوا کر اجزائے کلام سکھائیں
modules.summary_en: The trainer defines the eight Urdu parts of speech (اسم، فعل، صفت، ضمیر، حرفِ جار، حرفِ عطف، ندا، استفہام) and shows three ways to teach them in context: write a familiar sentence ('سارا اسکول جا رہی ہے') and ask children which words are nouns and which is the verb; a sentence-change game where children add an adjective (گرم روٹی) or swap in a pronoun (اس نے); and a group role-play where each group performs a short dialogue using one exclamation and one question word.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ اجزائے کلام کو روزمرہ کے جملوں، جملہ بدلنے کے کھیل اور گروپ رول پلے کے ذریعے سیاق و سباق میں کیسے سکھائیں۔
symptoms: teacher dictates definitions of اسم، فعل، صفت and children copy or memorise them
children never identify parts of speech in a real sentence
no activity where children build or change a sentence themselves
grammar period is only teacher talk and chorus repetition
modules.not_for: Teachers of English or maths lessons, or of Grade 1-2 children still learning to read.

segments.title_en: Why children's sentences go wrong; teach grammar in context
segments.title_ur: بچوں کے جملے کیوں بگڑتے ہیں؛ گرامر سیاق میں سکھائیں
segments.summary_en: Intro: incomplete or confusing sentences come from not knowing what each word does; objective: recognise parts of speech and teach them through context.

segments.title_en: The eight Urdu parts of speech
segments.title_ur: اردو کے آٹھ اجزائے کلام
segments.summary_en: Short definitions of اسم، فعل، صفت، ضمیر، حرفِ جار، حرفِ عطف، ندا and استفہام.

segments.title_en: Everyday sentences and the sentence-change game
segments.title_ur: روزمرہ کے جملے اور جملہ بدلنے کا کھیل
segments.summary_en: Write a familiar sentence and ask which words are nouns and which is the verb; then children add an adjective (گرم روٹی) or replace the noun with a pronoun and see how meaning changes.

segments.title_en: Role-play with exclamations and questions
segments.title_ur: ندا اور استفہام کے ساتھ رول پلے
segments.summary_en: Groups get one exclamation and one question word and perform a short dialogue using both ('ارے واہ، آج تو ہماری کلاس جیت گئی!' / 'کون سی ٹیم سیکنڈ آئی تھی؟').

segments.title_en: Recap
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Recap of the eight parts of speech and the three activities; thanks.

modules.title: زمانہ ماضی، حال، مستقبل
modules.teacher_line_en: Teaching Urdu tenses? Three boxes on the board, a timeline game and a closing check
modules.teacher_line_ur: زمانے پڑھا رہے ہیں؟ بورڈ پر تین خانے، ٹائم لائن کا کھیل اور آخر میں جانچ
modules.summary_en: A trainer teaches Urdu past, present and future tense: three boxes on the board with one verb in each (علی نے کھانا کھایا / کھاتا ہے / کھائے گا), think-aloud on why the subject stays and the verb changes, and transforming 'میں اسکول گیا' into present and future. The teacher also gets common errors (time word and verb not matching), three practice games (transformation drill with peer checking, a yesterday-today-tomorrow timeline with flashcards, spot-the-mistake) and a closing check where students make all three forms of one sentence.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ بورڈ پر تین خانوں، ٹائم لائن اور غلطی پکڑو کھیل کے ذریعے بچوں کو ماضی، حال اور مستقبل کے جملے بدلنا کیسے سکھائیں۔
symptoms: children write 'وہ کل آیا ہے' or mix time words and verb forms and the teacher does not point out why
tense taught only as definitions read from the book, no transformation practice
teacher never names فاعل/فعل when correcting a sentence
the grammar lesson ends without students producing any sentence of their own
modules.not_for: Teachers outside Urdu grammar in upper primary; English-tense lessons need an English example set.

segments.title_en: What a tense is: three boxes on the board
segments.title_ur: زمانہ کیا ہے: بورڈ پر تین خانے
segments.summary_en: Short intro, then think-aloud: tense tells when an action happens; three boxes (past, present, future) with one verb in each; the subject stays and only the verb changes with time.

segments.title_en: Changing sentences across tenses and fixing common errors
segments.title_ur: جملوں کا زمانہ بدلنا اور عام غلطیاں درست کرنا
segments.summary_en: Transforms 'میں اسکول گیا' into present and future, then names the two common errors (verb form and sentence structure) and corrects sentences where the time word and verb do not match.

segments.title_en: Three practice games for tenses
segments.title_ur: زمانوں کی مشق کے تین کھیل
segments.summary_en: Transformation drill (one student changes the sentence, another checks it), a yesterday-today-tomorrow timeline where students stick sentence cards, and a spot-the-mistake game with a deliberately wrong sentence.

segments.title_en: Closing check: one sentence, three forms
segments.title_ur: اختتامی جانچ: ایک جملہ، تین زمانے
segments.summary_en: At the end of the lesson ask students short questions, give one sentence to turn into past, present and future, a group round where each child picks a tense, and a written task rewriting a present-tense story in the past; sign-off.

modules.title: Conceptual Understanding
modules.teacher_line_en: Add one 'unseen' question to every test so children apply the idea, not recite it
modules.teacher_line_ur: ہر ٹیسٹ میں ایک ان دیکھا سوال شامل کریں تاکہ بچے رٹا نہیں، سمجھ استعمال کریں
modules.summary_en: A presenter tells a story about a test where children knew the questions in advance, scored well, then went silent when the same concept was asked in a new way. The video defines 'seen' questions (the five end-of-chapter questions announced for the test) and 'unseen' questions that apply a known concept to a new problem, e.g. 'You have 3/4 of a naan and your friend has 2/3; who has more?'. Teachers are asked to put at least one unseen application question in every paper and class check, alongside seen practice questions.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ ٹیسٹ اور کلاس میں رٹے والے دیکھے ہوئے سوالوں کے ساتھ کم از کم ایک نیا، ان دیکھا سوال کیسے شامل کریں تاکہ بچے تصور کو استعمال کرنا سیکھیں۔
symptoms: teacher tells the class exactly which questions will come in the test ('yehi paanch sawal aayenge')
every question is a textbook question read word for word and answered from memory
children chant memorised answers but no question asks them to apply the idea to a new case
children say a question is 'out of syllabus' when it is reworded
modules.not_for: Teachers looking for a ready classroom routine; this is a short argument for unseen test questions with one example, not a full assessment-design or questioning lesson.

segments.title_en: Intro: seen and unseen questions
segments.title_ur: تعارف: دیکھے اور ان دیکھے سوال
segments.summary_en: Greeting and the topic: teachers undervalue seen vs unseen questions, which separates rote learning from understanding.

segments.title_en: Good marks, then silence on a new question
segments.title_ur: اچھے نمبر، پھر نئے سوال پر خاموشی
segments.summary_en: A class story: children knew the test questions, wrote memorised answers and scored well, then went silent and called it 'out of syllabus' when the same concept was asked differently.

segments.title_en: Seen vs unseen question, with a naan fraction example
segments.title_ur: دیکھا اور ان دیکھا سوال، نان کے حصوں کی مثال
segments.summary_en: Seen = the announced end-of-chapter questions; unseen = a new problem answered from the concept, e.g. '3/4 of a naan or 2/3: who has more?'.

segments.title_en: Why unseen questions build thinking
segments.title_ur: ان دیکھے سوال سوچ کیوں بڑھاتے ہیں
segments.summary_en: Seen questions reward memory; unseen questions give practice in problem solving and higher-order thinking and show real understanding.

segments.title_en: Put one unseen question in every paper
segments.title_ur: ہر پرچے میں ایک ان دیکھا سوال
segments.summary_en: When designing a paper, ask yourself: is there one question that makes children apply, not recall? Keep seen questions for basic practice and add unseen ones.

modules.title: Formative Assessment
modules.teacher_line_en: Not sure who understood? Three 1-minute checks: quick quiz, group share, exit note
modules.teacher_line_ur: پتا نہیں کس کو سمجھ آئی؟ تین مختصر جانچیں: کوئز، گروپ کا جواب، آخر میں ایک جملہ
modules.summary_en: A presenter, reading English slide headings, defines formative assessment as small checks during the lesson and then shows three tools in use: a 3-4 question quiz mid- or end-lesson (simplest form of 5/10, name the three stages of the water cycle), a small-group problem (4 items at 25 rupees) where one child per group shares the answer and reasoning, and a one-minute written reflection 'which step was not clear to me today?'. The teacher learns what to do with the results: re-teach when most are wrong, pull a small remedial group when only a few are, and plan one check for the next lesson.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ سبق کے دوران چھوٹا کوئز، گروپ ڈسکشن اور آخر میں ایک منٹ کی تحریری ریفلیکشن سے بچوں کی سمجھ کیسے جانچیں اور نتیجے کے مطابق کیا کریں۔
symptoms: teacher asks 'samajh aa gaya?' and moves on after a chorus 'jee'
no quiz, mini-question or written check anywhere mid-lesson
lesson ends with no student writing or saying what was unclear
after group work no group shares its answer or how it got it
modules.not_for: Teachers who already run quick checks and need to re-explain in a different way; it lists tools on slides and shows no classroom footage.

segments.title_en: Intro: what formative assessment is for
segments.title_ur: تعارف: فارمیٹو اسیسمنٹ کس لیے ہے
segments.summary_en: Greeting and definition: small checks during the lesson to see who is learning and who needs help, with a fractions-quiz example.

segments.title_en: Three quick checks in use: quiz, group share, exit reflection
segments.title_ur: تین فوری جانچیں: کوئز، گروپ کا جواب، آخر میں تحریری ریفلیکشن
segments.summary_en: Lists then enacts three tools: a 3-4 question quiz (5/10 in simplest form, water-cycle stages), a group problem (4 items at 25 rupees, find the verb) with one child per group sharing the answer, and a one-minute written note on which step was not clear.

segments.title_en: Act on the results: re-teach or a small remedial group
segments.title_ur: نتائج پر عمل: دوبارہ سمجھائیں یا چھوٹا ریمیڈیل گروپ
segments.summary_en: If most answers are wrong re-explain the topic, if only a few are confused pull a small remedial group, use reflections and exit notes to see each child's difficulty and adjust the next lesson; ends by asking teachers to design one check for tomorrow.

modules.title: diagnostic assessments
modules.teacher_line_en: Start a unit with 3 ungraded questions that show who needs what
modules.teacher_line_ur: یونٹ کے آغاز میں تین سوال، تاکہ پتا چلے کس بچے کو کیا چاہیے
modules.summary_en: A presenter explains diagnostic assessment as an ungraded check at the start of a unit to find each child's prior knowledge and gaps (example: a new Grade 4 class where not everyone has Grade 4 skills). The teacher learns three steps: write one diagnostic question per unit objective (objective 'add 2-digit numbers' → '27 + 35 = ?'), review results thinking aloud ('if most got question X wrong, I must teach it more deeply'), and add scaffolding and practice where gaps are largest.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں یونٹ کے آغاز پر بغیر نمبروں کا تشخیصی ٹیسٹ بنانے اور اس کے نتائج سے سبق کی منصوبہ بندی بدلنے کا طریقہ بتایا گیا ہے۔
symptoms: teacher starts a new unit straight from the book with no question about what children already know
teacher assumes the whole class is at grade level ('sab ko aata hai')
the same task and pace for every child although some clearly cannot do the basics
teacher announces a test 'for marks' at the start of a topic
modules.not_for: Teachers whose report is about an in-lesson move (questioning, feedback, closure); this is unit-planning work done before teaching, with no classroom footage.

segments.title_en: What a diagnostic assessment is for
segments.title_ur: تشخیصی جائزہ کس لیے ہوتا ہے
segments.summary_en: Diagnostic assessment at the start of a unit shows prior knowledge and gaps; in a new Grade 4 class not every child has Grade 4 skills; it is the starting point on a map.

segments.title_en: When to give it, no marks, and which tools
segments.title_ur: کب لیں، نمبر نہیں، اور کون سے طریقے
segments.summary_en: Give it only at the start of a unit or course, ungraded, and tell children there is no marks pressure; options are questionnaires, self-rating surveys and, best of all, teacher-made questions aligned to the unit objectives.

segments.title_en: Objective grid, think-aloud review, adjust teaching
segments.title_ur: مقاصد کی جدول، نتائج پر غور، تدریس میں تبدیلی
segments.summary_en: Write one diagnostic question per objective ('add 2-digit numbers' → '27 + 35 = ?'), review answers thinking aloud ('if most got X wrong I must teach it more deeply'), and add scaffolding and practice where the gaps are.

segments.title_en: Your task: write 3 diagnostic questions (recap)
segments.title_ur: آپ کا کام: تین تشخیصی سوال لکھیں (خلاصہ)
segments.summary_en: Make a small grid of unit goals with at least 3 diagnostic questions and try them at the start of the next class; recap that the diagnostic is the starting line.

modules.title: summative assessments
modules.teacher_line_en: What end-of-unit tests are for, their formats, and their limits
modules.teacher_line_ur: یونٹ کے آخر والے ٹیسٹ کس لیے ہیں، ان کی اقسام اور حدود
modules.summary_en: A talking-head explainer of summative assessment: how it differs from formative assessment, its three features (standardised, comprehensive, outcome-focused), its formats (written exams, oral tests, projects, board exams), and its benefits and limits (stress, teaching to the test). The only practical advice is to align tests with unit objectives, share rubrics with students, and use results to adjust the next lessons.
modules.summary_ur: یہ ویڈیو سمیٹو اسیسمنٹ کی تعریف، اقسام، فائدے اور حدود بیان کرتی ہے، لیکن کلاس میں کرنے کا کوئی عملی طریقہ نہیں دکھاتی۔
symptoms: teacher only tests at the end of a unit and never uses the results to plan
test questions do not match the unit objectives
modules.not_for: Any teacher looking for something to try in tomorrow's lesson; this is definitions and theory about exams.

segments.title_en: Summative vs formative assessment
segments.title_ur: سمیٹو اور فارمیٹو اسیسمنٹ کا فرق
segments.summary_en: Defines summative assessment as end-of-unit measurement (class tests, mid-terms, finals, board exams) and contrasts it with formative assessment during learning.

segments.title_en: Features and formats
segments.title_ur: خصوصیات اور اقسام
segments.summary_en: Lists three features (structured and standardised, comprehensive, outcome-focused) and four formats (written exams, oral tests, projects, standardised tests).

segments.title_en: Benefits, limits and balanced use
segments.title_ur: فائدے، حدود اور متوازن استعمال
segments.summary_en: Benefits (clear evidence, motivation) and limits (stress, teaching to the test); advises aligning with unit objectives, sharing rubrics, testing after each unit and adjusting teaching from results.

segments.title_en: Recap
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Summarises the definition, formats, benefits and limits, and signs off.

modules.title: Small Steps, Big Success
modules.teacher_line_en: Class lost at new terms? Re-teach in small steps with tea steam and a glass of water
modules.teacher_line_ur: نئے الفاظ پر کلاس الجھ گئی؟ چائے کی بھاپ اور پانی کے گلاس سے قدم بہ قدم سمجھائیں
modules.summary_en: A narrated story of a Grade 5 science teacher whose class switches off when 'evaporation, condensation, precipitation' go on the board, so she re-teaches in small steps: steam from a cup of tea, a glass of water left in the sun and checked the next day, drops on a cold glass, rain seen from the window. Then short board notes read aloud, pairs explaining one stage each and switching, an independent task to write a daily-life example, and finally linking all examples into the water cycle.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں ایک کہانی کے ذریعے دکھایا گیا ہے کہ مشکل سبق کو روزمرہ مثالوں، چھوٹے تجربوں اور جوڑی میں وضاحت کے ذریعے چھوٹے چھوٹے قدموں میں کیسے سکھائیں۔
symptoms: teacher writes several new terms on the board at once and defines them in one go
children go quiet, chat or close notebooks during the explanation and the teacher carries on
the same definition is repeated when children look confused, with no example from home
children never explain a stage in their own words or give their own example
modules.not_for: Urdu-medium teachers who cannot follow English narration, or teachers whose class already follows the explanation.

segments.title_en: Children lost? Re-teach with tea steam, a glass and the window
segments.title_ur: بچے الجھ گئے؟ چائے کی بھاپ، گلاس اور کھڑکی سے دوبارہ سمجھائیں
segments.summary_en: When the class switches off at three new terms, the teacher drops the plan and re-teaches one stage at a time: steam from tea (evaporation), a glass left in the sun and checked next day, drops on a cold glass (condensation), and rain seen from the window (precipitation).

segments.title_en: Short notes, pair explaining, then a home example
segments.title_ur: مختصر نوٹس، جوڑی میں وضاحت، پھر گھر کی مثال
segments.summary_en: Short board notes are read aloud; in pairs one child explains evaporation and the other condensation, then they switch; next class each child writes one example from daily life.

segments.title_en: Join the examples into the water cycle
segments.title_ur: مثالوں کو جوڑ کر آبی چکر بنائیں
segments.summary_en: The teacher links the children's examples to the ocean, clouds and rain as one cycle; weeks later children bring their own examples; scaffolding defined as small connected steps.

modules.title: differentiated assessments
modules.teacher_line_en: One test for all? Let children choose quiz, poster or speech for one objective
modules.teacher_line_ur: سب کے لیے ایک ہی ٹیسٹ؟ ایک مقصد کے لیے بچوں کو کوئز، پوسٹر یا تقریر چننے دیں
modules.summary_en: A presenter defines differentiated assessment as several formats (written quiz, oral presentation or storytelling, peer review) that measure the same objective, then gives three strategies: a choice board where each child picks a quiz, poster or short speech for the same objective; a mixed-format assessment for one unit (short written test plus group oral presentation); and peer review with a structured feedback form or rubric. It is a spoken list with no worked classroom example.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ سنیں گے کہ ایک ہی مقصد کے لیے چوائس بورڈ، ملے جلے طریقۂ جانچ اور روبرک کے ساتھ ہم جماعت جائزے سے جانچ کو سب بچوں کے لیے منصفانہ کیسے بنائیں۔
symptoms: every check in the lesson is the same written question for all children
children never give or receive feedback on each other's work
students are never offered any choice of how to show what they learned
modules.not_for: Teachers looking for a classroom demonstration or for in-lesson questioning; it is a short spoken list about test formats, framed partly in 'learning styles' terms.

segments.title_en: What differentiated assessment is
segments.title_ur: مختلف طریقوں سے جانچ کیا ہے
segments.summary_en: Intro and definition: one test does not suit every child, so use several formats (written, oral, peer review) for the same objective; then the benefits (fairness, more authentic results). Framed in 'learning styles' terms.

segments.title_en: Choice board, mixed formats and peer-review rubrics
segments.title_ur: چوائس بورڈ، ملے جلے طریقے اور روبرک کے ساتھ ہم جماعت جائزہ
segments.summary_en: Three strategies: a choice board (quiz, poster or short speech, same objective), two formats for one unit (short written test plus group oral presentation), and a structured peer-feedback form where students evaluate each other's work and write suggestions.
segments.recommendable_reason: panel_veto: not_enacted_voice_over (lists assessment formats, nothing enacted; v8 Z234 wrong; ped/vetoes.json module 80, COS 20261024T044233 §2)

segments.title_en: Recap
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Recaps the definition, the three formats, the benefits and the three strategies; sign-off.

modules.title: implement simple routines
modules.teacher_line_en: Big, noisy class? Fixed start and end routines, hand signals and praise
modules.teacher_line_ur: بڑی اور شور والی کلاس؟ شروع اور آخر کے معمول، ہاتھ کے اشارے اور تعریف
modules.summary_en: A presenter gives three sets of routines for large, multilingual, disruptive classes: a predictable starter (bell work or a visual prompt) and an exit routine (quick reflection, notebooks closed, line-up), routine posters in English plus the local language with pictures; visual cues and hand signals, a buddy system and bilingual key instructions; and a positive behaviour system of 3-4 rules on posters, non-verbal signals instead of shouting, and specific praise for correct behaviour.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ سیکھیں گے کہ بڑی اور کئی زبانوں والی کلاس میں روزانہ کے معمول، اشاروں اور مثبت رویے کے نظام سے شور اور خلل کیسے کم کریں۔
symptoms: teacher says 'chup' or 'khamosh' many times and raises their voice to restart the lesson
long noisy gaps when the lesson starts and between activities
lesson ends abruptly with no exit routine
teacher only names misbehaviour and never praises correct behaviour
modules.not_for: Teachers whose classes are already settled and orderly; it lists tips without showing a classroom.

segments.title_en: The challenge: large, multilingual, disruptive classes
segments.title_ur: چیلنج: بڑی، کئی زبانوں والی اور شور والی کلاس
segments.summary_en: Introduces the problem of many students, different home languages and hard-to-keep discipline, and the need for simple, predictable routines.

segments.title_en: Start and end routines
segments.title_ur: کلاس کے آغاز اور اختتام کے معمول
segments.summary_en: A predictable starter every day (bell work or a visual prompt), an exit routine (quick reflection, notebooks closed, line-up) and routine posters on the wall in English plus the local language with pictures.

segments.title_en: Visual cues, buddies and bilingual instructions
segments.title_ur: تصویری اشارے، ساتھی بچے اور دو زبانوں میں ہدایات
segments.summary_en: Hand signals for silence and picture instructions, a buddy system pairing a fluent with a less fluent speaker for group work, and key instructions written in two languages.

segments.title_en: Positive behaviour system
segments.title_ur: مثبت رویے کا نظام
segments.summary_en: Communicate 3-4 clear rules with visual posters, use eye contact and a silent hand raise instead of shouting, and praise correct behaviour specifically ('Thank you for sitting quietly').

segments.title_en: Recap of the three strategies
segments.title_ur: تینوں حکمت عملیوں کا خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Recaps routines, visual and multilingual support, and the positive behaviour system; sign-off.

modules.title: SMART goals for behavior and academic tasks
modules.teacher_line_en: Help children set one clear goal, like 'raise my hand before speaking', and track it
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچوں سے ایک واضح گول بنوائیں، جیسے 'بولنے سے پہلے ہاتھ اٹھانا'، اور چارٹ پر دیکھیں
modules.summary_en: A presenter explains SMART goals (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound) with two student goals: 'I will complete 5 math problems with 90% accuracy by Friday' and 'I will raise my hand before speaking for the next 3 days'. Teachers learn four ways to make children own such goals: goal cards or a goal wall, a goal buddy who asks 'did you achieve your goal?', a weekly name/goal/tick chart reviewed every Friday, and an end-of-week question 'if not, what will you do differently next time?'.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ بچے پڑھائی اور رویے کے لیے واضح، ناپے جا سکنے والے SMART گول کیسے بنائیں اور گول کارڈ، بڈی چیک اور ہفتہ وار چارٹ سے اپنی پیش رفت کیسے دیکھیں۔
symptoms: teacher repeats the same behaviour reminders ('haath utha kar bolo', 'homework kyun nahi laye') with no target the child agreed to
rules are announced but children never say or write what they themselves will do
no chart, tick list or weekly check of any child's progress is mentioned
children are never asked what they will do differently next time
modules.not_for: Teachers looking for a questioning or content-explanation clip; this is about student goal-setting and self-monitoring, and early-years children will need it much simplified.

segments.title_en: What a SMART goal is, with two examples
segments.title_ur: SMART گول کیا ہے، دو مثالوں کے ساتھ
segments.summary_en: Greeting, then Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound unpacked on an academic goal (5 math problems at 90% by Friday) and a behaviour goal (raise my hand before speaking for 3 days).

segments.title_en: Goal cards, goal buddies and a progress chart
segments.title_ur: گول کارڈ، گول بڈی اور پیش رفت کا چارٹ
segments.summary_en: Each child writes a goal on a card or the goal wall; goal buddies ask each other 'did you achieve your goal?' and swap roles; a weekly chart (name, goal, tick/cross) is reviewed with the class every Friday.

segments.title_en: End-of-week reflection and behaviour goals
segments.title_ur: ہفتے کے آخر میں سوچ بچار اور رویے کے گول
segments.summary_en: At the week's end ask 'did you achieve your SMART goal? If not, what will you do differently?', celebrate small wins, and turn class rules into personal goals like 'I will bring my homework 4 days this week'.

segments.title_en: Recap
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Recap of why SMART goals help and the strategies covered; encouragement to set goals at the start of the year.

modules.title: Individualized Behavior Charts for Positive Student Progress
modules.teacher_line_en: Same few children disrupt every day? A one-target weekly chart with stars and praise
modules.teacher_line_ur: روز وہی چند بچے شور کرتے ہیں؟ ایک ہدف، ہفتہ وار چارٹ، ستارے اور فوری تعریف
modules.summary_en: A host interviews a teacher about individual behaviour charts for overcrowded classes. The teacher picks one specific, measurable target per child (raise hand before speaking, hand in homework on time, speak politely), draws a weekly grid with a star, tick or smiley for each day the target is met (picture icons for young children), praises the named behaviour at once ('you raised your hand every time today'), gives a small individual reward when the week is complete, and sets a new target once the old habit sticks. Tip for 40+ classes: run charts for a few children or small groups.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ ہر بچے کے لیے ایک واضح رویے کا ہدف، ہفتہ وار چارٹ، فوری تعریف اور نیا ہدف رکھ کر بغیر ڈانٹے رویہ کیسے بہتر کریں۔
symptoms: teacher says 'chup' / 'shor mat karo' again and again to the same few children
praise is only 'shabash' or 'very good' with no behaviour named
the same child disrupts several times and is only scolded, never given a target or follow-up
rewards and warnings are addressed only to the whole class
modules.not_for: Teachers whose problem is whole-class noise or getting attention (send an attention-cue clip); a chart for every child is heavy in a 40+ class unless kept to a few children or small groups.

segments.title_en: Intro: why stickers alone fail; personalised charts
segments.title_ur: تعارف: صرف اسٹیکر کیوں کافی نہیں؛ ذاتی چارٹ
segments.summary_en: Opens on overcrowded classes and hoarse teachers, says generic stickers and rewards do not always work, introduces individual charts and the guest teacher.

segments.title_en: Pick one specific target per child and draw the chart
segments.title_ur: ہر بچے کا ایک واضح ہدف چنیں اور چارٹ بنائیں
segments.summary_en: Choose a specific, measurable target per child (raise hand before speaking, homework on time, speak politely), then a weekly grid with the target column and a star, tick or smiley each day it is met; picture icons for young children.

segments.title_en: Daily named praise and a small weekly reward
segments.title_ur: روزانہ نام لے کر تعریف اور ہفتہ وار چھوٹا انعام
segments.summary_en: Praise the target behaviour the moment it happens, naming it; when the week's chart is complete give a small individual reward (sticker, chance to be monitor, appreciation note, class cheer).

segments.title_en: Set a new target when the habit sticks
segments.title_ur: عادت پکی ہو جائے تو نیا ہدف رکھیں
segments.summary_en: Once a child meets a target consistently, replace it (e.g. stop pencil tapping, then speak politely in group discussion); children start tracking their own progress and gain confidence.

segments.title_en: Recap: four rules, use small groups in big classes
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ: چار اصول، بڑی کلاس میں چھوٹے گروپ
segments.summary_en: Recap of the four rules (specific target, visual chart, consistent timely reinforcement, update the target) and a tip to run charts by small groups in overcrowded rooms.

modules.title: Project based learning
modules.teacher_line_en: Run a pretend shop with paper money so children budget, buy and work as a team
modules.teacher_line_ur: کاغذی پیسوں سے کلاس میں دکان لگائیں تاکہ بچے بجٹ اور مل جل کر کام سیکھیں
modules.summary_en: English slide text lists what a project is and the core elements of project-based learning (inquiry, real-world relevance, collaboration, student role, a final product). The Urdu narration then gives one worked idea: while teaching money in maths, run a classroom market where some children are shopkeepers and some customers, each with limited paper money and a list of basic items to buy, so they learn budgeting, teamwork and respect. It ends with community projects such as a cleanliness drive, with the teacher guiding rather than giving answers.
modules.summary_ur: آپ دیکھیں گے کہ پیسوں کے سبق میں بچوں کو دکاندار اور گاہک بنا کر کاغذی پیسوں سے خریداری کا چھوٹا پروجیکٹ کیسے کروائیں تاکہ وہ بجٹ، ٹیم ورک اور احترام سیکھیں۔
symptoms: maths lesson on money taught only from textbook sums with no link to buying or budgeting
children never work together on a task; every activity is individual copying
no role, choice or product for the children; teacher talks for the whole period
modules.not_for: Teachers looking for a quick within-period routine; it is a short overview of project-based learning with one shop role-play example and no step-by-step plan.

segments.title_en: What project-based learning is (slides)
segments.title_ur: پروجیکٹ پر مبنی تدریس کیا ہے
segments.summary_en: English slide text: a project as a long-term real-life task; core elements inquiry, real-world relevance, collaboration, student role, evidence of learning; purpose.

segments.title_en: PBL for character building
segments.title_ur: کردار سازی کے لیے پروجیکٹ
segments.summary_en: Do classroom activities teach real life? PBL introduced in Urdu, and turning everyday classroom questions toward projects and character education.

segments.title_en: A classroom market with paper money
segments.title_ur: کاغذی پیسوں سے کلاس کا بازار
segments.summary_en: While teaching money, children become shopkeepers and customers with limited paper money and buy basic items; each child has a role (leader, shopkeeper, customer) and learns budgeting, teamwork and respect.

segments.title_en: Community projects and the teacher as guide
segments.title_ur: معاشرتی پروجیکٹ اور رہنما کے طور پر ٹیچر
segments.summary_en: Environment or cleanliness projects for social responsibility; the teacher shows the way instead of giving answers in a safe classroom where mistakes are allowed; closing.

modules.title: inquiry-based learning
modules.teacher_line_en: Start science with a question, not the answer: 'Why does rain water collect here?'
modules.teacher_line_ur: سائنس کا سبق جواب سے نہیں، سوال سے شروع کریں: بارش کا پانی یہاں کیوں جمع ہوتا ہے؟
modules.summary_en: A presenter contrasts open questions (why, how, what do you think) with closed yes/no questions, then a narrated story shows a Grade 5 science teacher running an inquiry lesson. She writes 'Why does water collect in our streets after it rains?' on the board, asks 'What do you think causes this?' and takes students' ideas (blocked drains, uneven road), sends groups to observe the school's drains and report next day, writes their findings on the board and asks 'What can be done to solve this problem?', then has each group share what they learned. The teacher learns to open with a real-life question and hold back the answer while students investigate.
modules.summary_ur: آپ دیکھیں گے کہ سبق کو روزمرہ زندگی کے ایک سوال سے کیسے شروع کریں، بچوں کے خیالات کیسے لیں، اور انہیں خود مشاہدہ اور تجزیہ کر کے جواب تک کیسے پہنچنے دیں۔
symptoms: lesson opens with 'aaj hum chapter X parhenge' and a definition, never a question
teacher asks 'why?' and answers it herself or himself within seconds
no 'what do you think?' question put to students before the explanation
students never observe, investigate or report anything; they only read and memorise
modules.not_for: Teachers who first need basic open questions (the Level 1 questioning module), or maths-drill lessons; it is an English narrated story with no real classroom footage.

segments.title_en: Background: Socratic questioning, open vs closed questions
segments.title_ur: پس منظر: سقراطی سوال، کھلے اور بند سوال
segments.summary_en: Where inquiry comes from (Socrates asking instead of lecturing) and the difference between closed yes/no questions and open why/how/what-do-you-think questions; points back to the Level 1 questioning module.

segments.title_en: Open the lesson with a real-life question and take students' ideas
segments.title_ur: سبق روزمرہ کے سوال سے شروع کریں اور بچوں کے خیالات لیں
segments.summary_en: A Grade 5 science teacher whose students only memorise writes 'Why does water collect in our streets after it rains?', asks 'What do you think causes this?' and students reason (blocked drains, uneven road); the teacher guides instead of giving answers.

segments.title_en: Groups investigate, analyse findings, propose solutions and share
segments.title_ur: گروپ تحقیق کریں، نتائج پر غور کریں، حل تجویز کریں اور بتائیں
segments.summary_en: Groups observe the school's drains and report next day (garbage, low land); the teacher lists findings on the board and asks what can be done, students propose a clean-up or a request letter, and each group shares what it learned and would improve.

segments.title_en: Teacher's reflection and the five steps recapped
segments.title_ur: ٹیچر کی سوچ اور پانچ مراحل کا خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: The teacher reflects that students found the answers themselves; recap of the steps (real-life question, students' ideas, group observation, guided analysis, reflection and sharing) and a closing call to start lessons with a question.

modules.title: Use Socratic Questioning
modules.teacher_line_en: Ask 'why might this happen?' instead of giving the answer
modules.teacher_line_ur: جواب بتانے کے بجائے پوچھیں: یہ کیوں ہو رہا ہے؟
modules.summary_en: A narrated story shows a Grade 4 science teacher opening with 'Have you noticed summers are getting hotter? Why do you think this is happening, and how might it affect plants and animals?' and children answering with their own observations (dry school garden, fewer butterflies). The video then explains inquiry-based learning and gives question stems to use tomorrow: 'What do you think?', 'Why might this happen?', 'How can we find out?', small-group discussion, and follow-ups 'Can you explain more?' / 'What makes you think that?'.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں سقراطی سوالات کے ذریعے بچوں کو جواب بتانے کے بجائے سوالوں سے سوچنے اور خود جواب ڈھونڈنے پر لگانا ایک سائنس سبق کی مثال سے دکھایا گیا ہے۔
symptoms: teacher asks only yes/no or one-word questions ('theek hai?', 'kitne hain?')
teacher gives the answer immediately after asking
a student's answer is accepted with 'good' and never followed by 'why do you think that?'
science lesson read from the book with no question about what children have noticed around them
modules.not_for: Teachers who need a phonics or maths-procedure clip, or whose report shows they already ask open questions with follow-ups; it is in English only.

segments.title_en: Socratic questioning in a Grade 4 science lesson
segments.title_ur: گریڈ 4 سائنس میں سقراطی سوالات
segments.summary_en: Defines Socratic questioning (guide thinking through questions, not answers), then a teacher asks why summers are getting hotter and how that affects plants and animals; children answer from their own observations.

segments.title_en: What an inquiry classroom looks like
segments.title_ur: تحقیقی کلاس روم کیسا ہوتا ہے
segments.summary_en: Inquiry learning means asking why and how and finding answers together, with the teacher as guide; example questions on water pollution: 'How does dirty water affect fish?', 'What can our community do to keep water clean?'.
segments.recommendable_reason: panel_veto: ladder only, not a next-step pick (a definition chapter; 0/8 in the R7 panel, ped/REVIEW_r7_scale.md §6.2)

segments.title_en: Open question stems, group talk and follow-up probes
segments.title_ur: کھلے سوال، گروپ گفتگو اور مزید پوچھنا
segments.summary_en: Start from real life, avoid yes/no questions ('What do you think?', 'Why might this happen?', 'How can we find out?'), let small groups discuss, value every answer, and follow up with 'Can you explain more?' / 'What makes you think that?'.

modules.title: Group Projects
modules.teacher_line_en: Group work where every child has a job: leader, writer, presenter, time-keeper
modules.teacher_line_ur: ایسا گروپ ورک جس میں ہر بچے کا کام ہو: لیڈر، رائٹر، پریزنٹر، ٹائم کیپر
modules.summary_en: For an overcrowded class, a trainer shows how to run group work in which every child has a job: write the project objective on the board, make groups of 5-6, and let each group decide in a short discussion who is leader, writer, presenter, time-keeper and materials manager, with guiding questions such as 'who can take everyone along?'. It covers keeping noise productive (talking stick, a 5-minute limit, rotating roles, praising calm groups), what to watch for while circulating, an end-of-activity reflection ('which role helped most? what will we do better?'), and low-cost role cards and a role chart.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ بڑی کلاس میں گروپ ورک کیسے کروائیں جہاں ہر بچہ خود اپنا کردار چنے، اور شور کو قابو میں رکھتے ہوئے آخر میں گروپ سے غور و فکر کروائیں۔
symptoms: children sit in groups but the teacher hears from one or two of them; others are silent
group task given with no roles and no stated goal
teacher stops group work because of noise: 'chup', 'shor mat karo' many times
group work ends with no reflection on how the group worked
modules.not_for: Teachers who never use group work and first need a basic seating or attention routine; this assumes groups already happen.

segments.title_en: Why groups need roles
segments.title_ur: گروپ میں کردار کیوں ضروری ہیں
segments.summary_en: Introduces group work with roles for overcrowded classes: without clear roles a few children work and the rest sit silently.

segments.title_en: Objective on the board, children choose their roles
segments.title_ur: بورڈ پر مقصد، بچے خود کردار چنیں
segments.summary_en: Write the project objective on the board, form groups of 5-6, and let each group discuss and decide leader, writer, presenter, time-keeper and materials manager, with guiding questions from the teacher.

segments.title_en: Facilitate and keep the noise productive
segments.title_ur: رہنمائی کریں اور شور کو قابو میں رکھیں
segments.summary_en: The teacher circulates as a facilitator; to keep discussion from turning chaotic: set rules, a talking stick, a 5-minute time limit, turn-taking when two want the same role, and instant praise for calm groups.

segments.title_en: Watch the roles, then group reflection
segments.title_ur: کرداروں پر نظر، پھر گروپ کا جائزہ
segments.summary_en: What to watch for (fair roles, everyone taking part, an inclusive leader), giving hints but not decisions, then reflection questions for each group and a note for the teacher's own reflection.

segments.title_en: Low-cost tools: role cards, rotation, role chart
segments.title_ur: کم خرچ طریقے: رول کارڈز، باری، چارٹ
segments.summary_en: For overcrowded rooms: role cards handed out at random, rotating roles after every activity, a role chart on the board or wall, and a short oral summary from each group.

segments.title_en: Recap of the five steps
segments.title_ur: پانچ مراحل کا خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Lists the steps again (objective, student-chosen roles, managing discussion, monitoring, reflection) and signs off.

modules.title: Peer Problem-Solving
modules.teacher_line_en: Group work where everyone works: roles, one shared product, and a peer tick-rubric
modules.teacher_line_ur: ایسا گروپ ورک جس میں سب کام کریں: کردار، ایک مشترک نتیجہ اور ساتھیوں کی جانچ
modules.summary_en: Small-group problem-solving with peer accountability: pick a problem one child cannot solve alone (divide 120 students into 6 equal teams; design a solution to the village water shortage), give each group roles (leader, writer, presenter, timekeeper) feeding ONE shared product, break it into steps (brainstorm, choose, prepare presentation) and hand out a paper rubric (Participation, Respect, Accuracy) members tick for each other. The teacher learns to facilitate (circulate, stop one child dominating, ask 'Where has your group reached? Who will share an idea?', 5-minute time calls) and to assess collaboration, not just the answer, through group-to-group peer review and a short checklist.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ سیکھیں گے کہ چھوٹے گروپوں کو ایسا مسئلہ کیسے دیں جو مل کر حل ہو، ہر بچے کو کردار اور ایک مشترک نتیجہ دیں، اور جانچ میں صرف جواب نہیں بلکہ سب کی شرکت بھی کیسے دیکھیں۔
symptoms: 'groups mein kaam karo' with no roles; one or two students do the work
group task is a worksheet each child could do alone
teacher marks only the group's final answer, never who took part
one student talks for the whole group while others are silent
modules.not_for: Teachers who have not yet tried basic pair work or whose class has no space or routine for groups; start with a pair-talk clip.

segments.title_en: From pair teaching to group problem-solving
segments.title_ur: جوڑیوں سے گروپ میں مسئلہ حل کرنے تک
segments.summary_en: Intro: groups solve one problem together, produce and present a shared outcome; the teacher only designs the task and makes sure everyone takes part.

segments.title_en: Choose a problem that needs the whole group
segments.title_ur: ایسا مسئلہ چنیں جس میں پورا گروپ لگے
segments.summary_en: The problem must be too big for one child: share 120 students into 6 equal teams (Grade 4 maths) or design a group solution to the village water shortage (social studies).

segments.title_en: Roles, one shared product and a peer rubric
segments.title_ur: کردار، ایک مشترک نتیجہ اور ساتھیوں کا روبرک
segments.summary_en: Assign leader, writer, presenter, timekeeper working toward one poster/worksheet/skit; a paper rubric (Participation, Respect, Accuracy) members tick for each other; split the task into brainstorm, choose, prepare.

segments.title_en: Facilitating groups: circulate, prompt, time calls
segments.title_ur: گروپوں کی رہنمائی: گھومیں، سوال کریں، وقت یاد دلائیں
segments.summary_en: The teacher circulates, stops one child dominating, asks 'Where has your group reached? Who will share an idea?', calls time every 5 minutes, and uses old notebook pages instead of chart paper.

segments.title_en: Assess the collaboration, not just the answer
segments.title_ur: صرف جواب نہیں، شرکت کو بھی جانچیں
segments.summary_en: Check whether everyone took part, roles were done and the product was shared, using group-to-group peer feedback and a teacher checklist (Participation, Accuracy, Teamwork).

segments.title_en: Reflection and recap
segments.title_ur: سوچ بچار اور خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Reflective questions on designing a task where every member takes ownership, then a recap of the steps.

modules.title: Encouraging Multiple Solutions in the Classroom
modules.teacher_line_en: Only one 'right method' in class? Ask groups for 3 solutions, then compare
modules.teacher_line_ur: کلاس میں صرف ایک ہی طریقہ؟ گروپوں سے تین حل لیں، پھر ان کا موازنہ کروائیں
modules.summary_en: A podcast-style conversation with a pedagogy specialist on getting students to produce and compare several solutions to one problem: choose problems that allow many routes (120 students into 6 teams by repeated subtraction or long division, saving water for plants, a village with no library), set multi-path group tasks, then compare solutions with guiding questions (feasible? cost-effective? sustainable?). The teacher also hears how to answer an unrealistic idea without discouraging the child, and to close with a written reflection: which methods we tried, which was best and why.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ سنیں گے کہ ایک ہی مسئلے کے کئی حل بچوں سے کیسے نکلوائیں، رہنما سوالوں سے ان کا موازنہ کیسے کروائیں اور آخر میں ان سے مختصر تحریری جائزہ کیسے لکھوائیں۔
symptoms: teacher shows one method and every child copies the same working
teacher accepts only the textbook method and marks a different correct method wrong
students are never asked which answer or method is better and why
an unusual student idea is dismissed with 'nahi, galat' and no reason
modules.not_for: Teachers who still need basic questioning or classroom-control routines first; it is a conversation, with no children shown.

segments.title_en: Podcast intro: multiple solutions
segments.title_ur: تعارف: ایک مسئلے کے کئی حل
segments.summary_en: The host introduces the topic, links it to earlier episodes on peer teaching and group work, and welcomes the guest.

segments.title_en: Pick problems with many routes and set multi-path tasks
segments.title_ur: ایسے مسئلے چنیں جن کے کئی حل ہوں
segments.summary_en: Examples of problems that naturally have several solutions (120 students into 6 teams by repeated subtraction or long division; saving water for plants; book access in a village without a library), then three task designs: groups solve one maths problem in different ways and present, a design-thinking challenge to brainstorm at least 3 solutions, and writing one idea in different genres.

segments.title_en: Compare solutions with guiding questions
segments.title_ur: رہنما سوالوں سے حل کا موازنہ
segments.summary_en: The teacher asks which solution was feasible, cost-effective and sustainable, and answers an unrealistic idea ('take everyone by helicopter') with 'great imagination, now is it practical for cost and safety?' so the child thinks critically without being discouraged.

segments.title_en: Reflection note and a Grade 5 school-trip example
segments.title_ur: تحریری جائزہ اور جماعت پنجم کی مثال
segments.summary_en: Students end by writing which methods they tried, which was best and why, and what they would improve; then a Grade 5 example where groups plan a school trip (bus, parents' cars, walking) and learn to balance safety and cost by comparing.

segments.title_en: Recap
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Recaps the four steps (choose, design, compare with criteria, reflect) and the teacher's role as facilitator; sign-off.

modules.title: Using Varied Strategies to Build Connected Lessons
modules.teacher_line_en: Plan 3 linked lessons (recognise, compare, add) and check readiness before moving on
modules.teacher_line_ur: تین جڑے ہوئے اسباق کی منصوبہ بندی کریں اور آگے بڑھنے سے پہلے تیاری جانچیں
modules.summary_en: A presenter shows how to plan 2-3 connected lessons with objectives that build step by step: Grade 4 fractions (identify in everyday objects, then compare and order, then add like denominators), Grade 5 plants (parts, then functions, then a simple experiment) and Grade 3-4 Urdu stories (read, then characters/setting/main idea, then write a paragraph). Teachers learn to change the strategy at each stage (real-life visuals, group discussion, guided then independent practice, reflection) and to end each lesson with a readiness checklist: most students struggling means a short review, a few means small-group support, all strong means a harder next lesson.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ دو تین جڑے ہوئے اسباق کے مقاصد قدم بہ قدم کیسے بنائیں اور ہر سبق کے آخر میں ایک چھوٹی فہرست سے کیسے دیکھیں کہ بچے اگلے قدم کے لیے تیار ہیں یا نہیں۔
symptoms: teacher announces only the topic or page ('aaj chapter 4') and never says what students will be able to do
today's lesson does not mention or build on what the class learned last time
the whole period is one kind of activity (teacher explains, students copy)
the teacher moves to the next exercise without checking whether most children got today's one
modules.not_for: Teachers whose report is about a single in-lesson move such as questioning or feedback; this is about planning a short sequence of lessons.

segments.title_en: Intro: why lessons should connect
segments.title_ur: تعارف: اسباق جڑے ہوئے کیوں ہوں
segments.summary_en: Greeting; foundation, then practice, then application; randomly planned lessons confuse students; the national curriculum asks for gradual building of skills.

segments.title_en: Three-lesson sequences: fractions, plants, stories
segments.title_ur: تین اسباق کا سلسلہ: کسر، پودے، کہانیاں
segments.summary_en: Progressive objectives for Grade 4 fractions (identify, compare and order, add like denominators), Grade 5 plants (parts, functions, experiment) and Grade 3-4 Urdu stories (read, find characters and main idea, write a paragraph).
segments.recommendable_reason: panel_veto: not_a_move: a three-lesson objectives sequence, 2/2 (ped-review live review, board 20261020T194756_ped-review_spec.md; appended by eng-engine on lead-review 19:56Z item 4)

segments.title_en: A different strategy at each stage
segments.title_ur: ہر مرحلے پر الگ طریقہ
segments.summary_en: Lesson 1: visuals and familiar objects; lesson 2: group work and discussion; then guided practice with misconceptions corrected, independent practice, and a reflection on what was learned and what was easy.
segments.recommendable_reason: panel_veto: not_a_move: a planning list, R3 = 2 in 6/6 (ped-review live review, board 20261020T194756_ped-review_spec.md; appended by eng-engine on lead-review 19:56Z item 4)

segments.title_en: Readiness checklist at the end of each lesson
segments.title_ur: ہر سبق کے آخر میں تیاری کی فہرست
segments.summary_en: Ask: did most students reach today's objective and explain their answers? Many struggling = short review first; a few = small-group support or extra practice; all strong = make the next lesson harder.

segments.title_en: Recap
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Progressive objectives, varied strategies, readiness checklist; closing.

modules.title: Bloom’s Taxonomy
modules.teacher_line_en: Class can do 4+3 but freezes on word problems? Ask recall, then apply, then analyse
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے ۴+۳ تو کر لیتے ہیں مگر سوالیہ مسئلے پر رک جاتے ہیں؟ یاد، اطلاق، پھر تجزیہ کے سوال
modules.summary_en: After a recap of Bloom's first three levels (recall, application, analysis), a narrated story follows a Grade 3 addition lesson: the class shouts '7!' to 4 + 3 but goes silent on a mango word problem. The teacher then asks recall questions ('What does addition mean? Which sign?'), an application question (6 pencils and 3 more) with buttons for small groups to add, and an analysis question ('If 8 + 2 = 10, what happens if I make one number smaller and the other bigger?'), waiting while students test numbers until one finds 7 + 3 = 10. The teacher learns to plan one question at each level for the same objective.
modules.summary_ur: آپ دیکھیں گے کہ جمع کے ایک ہی سبق میں یاد، اطلاق اور تجزیے کی سطح کے سوال کیسے بنائیں تاکہ بچے صرف رٹیں نہیں بلکہ سوچیں۔
symptoms: every maths question is 'what is 4 plus 3?' answered in chorus
class goes quiet on a word problem and the teacher gives the answer
no question that asks students to compare, predict or find a pattern
addition taught with numbers on the board only, no objects or real-life example
modules.not_for: Teachers whose transcript already shows why/how questions with follow-ups (C1 is not their gap), or Grade 6+ maths teachers; it is an English narrated story, not footage.

segments.title_en: Recap: Bloom's first three levels
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ: بلوم کی پہلی تین سطحیں
segments.summary_en: Points back to the earlier Bloom's training, recaps recall, application and analysis, and says today's example is a maths lesson on addition.

segments.title_en: Students can recall sums but freeze on a word problem; start with recall questions
segments.title_ur: بچے جمع یاد رکھتے ہیں مگر سوالیہ مسئلے پر رک جاتے ہیں؛ پہلے یاد کے سوال
segments.summary_en: The class shouts '7!' to 4 + 3 but goes silent on 'Ali has 5 mangoes, buys 3 more'; the teacher decides to question across three Bloom's levels and begins with recall questions (What does addition mean? Which sign? 5 + 2?).

segments.title_en: Application: a real-life question and buttons to add in groups
segments.title_ur: اطلاق: روزمرہ کا سوال اور گروپ میں بٹن گن کر جمع
segments.summary_en: An application question (6 pencils and 3 more) gets students counting and writing; small groups then add handfuls of buttons and say the total.

segments.title_en: Analysis: 'one number smaller, the other bigger: same total?'
segments.title_ur: تجزیہ: ایک عدد چھوٹا، دوسرا بڑا، کیا جواب وہی رہے گا؟
segments.summary_en: The teacher asks what happens to 8 + 2 = 10 if one number gets smaller and the other bigger, writes it on the board, waits through the silence while students test numbers, and one finds 7 + 3 = 10: students look for a pattern instead of just solving.

segments.title_en: Recap: recall to application to analysis in every lesson
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ: ہر سبق میں یاد، اطلاق اور تجزیہ
segments.summary_en: End of the lesson and recap: include questions from all three levels in every maths lesson so children think, not just memorise.

modules.title: Decimals
modules.teacher_line_en: Teach decimals from shaded grids, place value and rupees-paisa
modules.teacher_line_ur: اعشاریہ سکھائیں: رنگے خانے، مقامی قدر اور روپے پیسے
modules.summary_en: A Grade 4 demo lesson builds decimals from fractions: children recall that fractions are parts, see shaded grids (4/10, 15/100, 32/1000) and learn 'decimal fraction'. Two conversion methods follow (place-value columns and long division: 4 ÷ 10 = 0.4, 'fractions are division in disguise'), then whole part, decimal point and decimal places with children counting places in 49.35 and 0.859, and money/length links (50 paisa = 0.50 rupee, 25 cm = 0.25 m).
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں گریڈ 4 کے ڈیمو سبق کے ذریعے کسور سے اعشاریہ تک پہنچنا، دو طریقوں سے تبدیلی، اعشاری مقامات اور پیسوں و پیمائش سے تعلق دکھایا گیا ہے۔
symptoms: Grade 4-5 decimals lesson that starts with the rule 'put a point' and never links to fractions
children read 0.15 as 'zero point fifteen' and the teacher does not correct it
teacher never uses the words tenths, hundredths, decimal point or decimal places
decimals taught with no money or measurement example
modules.not_for: Teachers not teaching decimals or fractions in Grades 4-5; it is content knowledge for that topic, not a general engagement clip.

segments.title_en: From fractions to decimal fractions with shaded grids
segments.title_ur: رنگے خانوں سے کسور سے اعشاری کسور تک
segments.summary_en: After a short host intro, the teacher asks what fractions are (a child: 'parts'), shows shaded grids 4/10, 5/10, 15/100, 32/1000 and names fractions over 10, 100, 1000 'decimal fractions'.

segments.title_en: Method 1: place value to write 4/10 as 0.4
segments.title_ur: پہلا طریقہ: مقامی قدر سے 4/10 کو 0.4 لکھنا
segments.summary_en: Look at the denominator, place the numerator in the right decimal place (4/10 = 0.4, 15/100 = 0.15, 32/1000 = 0.032) and read it in words. The audio says 'hundreds/thousands' where hundredths/thousandths are meant.

segments.title_en: Method 2: long division, and read digits separately
segments.title_ur: دوسرا طریقہ: لمبی تقسیم، اور ہندسے الگ پڑھیں
segments.summary_en: 4 ÷ 10 worked as long division to show 'fractions are division in disguise', then the results are named decimal numbers and children are warned to read 0.15 digit by digit, not as fifteen.

segments.title_en: Whole part, decimal point and decimal places
segments.title_ur: مکمل حصہ، اعشاری نقطہ اور اعشاری مقامات
segments.summary_en: Using 24.31, 49.35 and 0.859 the teacher names the whole part, decimal part and decimal point, then asks children how many decimal places there are ('two, teacher!', 'three').

segments.title_en: Decimals with rupees, paisa and metres
segments.title_ur: روپے، پیسے اور میٹر سے اعشاریہ
segments.summary_en: Link decimals to real life with coins and play notes (100 paisa = 1 rupee, so 50 paisa = 0.50 rupee) and length (25 cm = 25/100 = 0.25 m).

segments.title_en: Recap of the steps and a planning task
segments.title_ur: مراحل کا خلاصہ اور منصوبہ بندی
segments.summary_en: Recaps the sequence (fractions link, grid shading, place-value game, both sides of the point, money and measurement) and asks the teacher to plan one small activity.

modules.title: Percentages
modules.teacher_line_en: Show 'percent = out of 100' with a 100-square grid, then link it to fractions and decimals
