modules.teacher_line_ur: 100 خانوں کے گرڈ سے فیصد کا مطلب دکھائیں اور اسے کسر اور اعشاریہ سے جوڑیں
modules.summary_en: A short demo lesson: a 100-square grid with 30 red, 16 green and 24 yellow boxes shows that percent means 'out of 100' (30% = 30/100), then children write examples such as 99 out of 100 marks. The trainer then shows how to convert 1/2 to 0.5 by division and to 50% by moving the decimal point two places ('because 100 has two zeros'), a fraction-decimal-percent ladder (1/4, 3/4), real-life questions about exam marks and '50% off', a shopping-sale game, and a modelled word problem solved in pairs.
modules.summary_ur: آپ 100 خانوں والے گرڈ، کسر سے اعشاریہ اور فیصد میں تبدیلی اور دکان کی سیل جیسی روزمرہ مثالوں سے فیصد سکھانا سیکھیں گے۔
symptoms: percent taught only as the rule 'divide and multiply by 100' with no picture of 100 parts
teacher does not link percentages to fractions or decimals children already know
children move the decimal point with no reason given
no example from marks, prices or sales outside the textbook
modules.not_for: Teachers of early grades, or maths teachers whose class has not yet learnt fractions and decimals.

segments.title_en: Percent means out of 100: the 100-square grid
segments.title_ur: فیصد یعنی 100 میں سے: 100 خانوں کا گرڈ
segments.summary_en: Defines percent as 'per hundred' with the % sign, then uses a square split into 100 boxes (30 red, 16 green, 24 yellow) to write 30% = 30/100 and has children repeat it.

segments.title_en: Writing percentages, then children try
segments.title_ur: فیصد لکھنا، پھر بچوں کی باری
segments.summary_en: Writes examples symbolically (99 out of 100 marks = 99%, 52 red boxes = 52%) and hands over: children open notebooks and find the percent for examples on the board.

segments.title_en: From prior knowledge: fraction to decimal (1/2 = 0.5)
segments.title_ur: پچھلے علم سے: کسر سے اعشاریہ
segments.summary_en: Suggests opening from fractions and decimals children already know, and works 1 / 2 by division (2 does not go into 1, add a decimal point and a zero) to get 0.5.

segments.title_en: Decimal to percent, and why two places
segments.title_ur: اعشاریہ سے فیصد، اور دو جگہ کیوں
segments.summary_en: Moves the decimal point two places right to turn 0.5 into 50%, and explains why: 100 has two zeros and percent means out of 100; gives a one-line tip for children.

segments.title_en: Fraction-decimal-percent ladder and wall poster
segments.title_ur: کسر، اعشاریہ اور فیصد کی سیڑھی
segments.summary_en: Writes one value three ways (1/2, 0.5, 50%; 1/4, 0.25, 25%; 3/4, 0.75, 75%) and suggests a class poster where children add a new example each day.

segments.title_en: Real life: marks, '50% off' and a shopping-sale game
segments.title_ur: روزمرہ زندگی: نمبر، سیل اور دکان کا کھیل
segments.summary_en: Asks what 80 out of 100 marks is and what '50% off' means, waiting for replies, then sets up a sale game with price tags (25% off, 10% off) for mental calculation.

segments.title_en: Model a word problem, then pairs solve
segments.title_ur: سوال حل کر کے دکھائیں، پھر جوڑیوں میں
segments.summary_en: Models 'a student scored 45 out of 60, find the percentage' on the board and then puts children in pairs to solve each other's questions. The spoken working says '40 / 60 x 100 = 75%' (should be 45).

segments.title_en: Recap of strategies
segments.title_ur: طریقوں کا خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Lists the strategies again (100-square grid, conversion ladder, real-life context, word problems in pairs) and signs off.

modules.title: Factor and Multiple
modules.teacher_line_en: Factors vs multiples: share 12 mangoes, hop on multiples, fix the common mix-up
modules.teacher_line_ur: عاد اور اضعاف: بارہ آم بانٹیں، اضعاف پر چھلانگ لگائیں، عام الجھن دور کریں
modules.summary_en: For Grade 4-5, factors are defined as numbers that divide exactly (6: 1, 2, 3, 6) and multiples as what you get by multiplying (3: 3, 6, 9, 12), then made real: share 12 mangoes equally among how many friends; baskets of 5 mangoes. Activities: a group race to list all factors of a number card, a chalk 'multiples hop' on the floor, and colouring multiples of 2 and 3 on a number chart to spot common multiples. It names the common mix-up of factors and multiples and gives a board rule to fix it.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ چوتھی پانچویں جماعت کو عاد اور اضعاف آموں کی تقسیم کی مثال، فرش پر چھلانگ والے کھیل اور نمبر چارٹ سے کیسے سکھائیں اور ان دونوں کے فرق کی عام غلطی کیسے دور کریں۔
symptoms: students call 12 a factor of 3 or list factors when asked for multiples, and the teacher only says 'galat'
factors and multiples defined only by rote, no sharing or grouping example
whole lesson is board work with no game or group task
teacher gives the answer list without asking why a number is or is not a factor
modules.not_for: Teachers whose lesson is not on factors/multiples, Grade 1-3 teachers, and teachers who cannot follow English narration.

segments.title_en: What this video covers
segments.title_ur: اس ویڈیو میں کیا ہے
segments.summary_en: Greeting and the objectives: explain factors and multiples, use real-life examples and fun activities.

segments.title_en: What factors and multiples are
segments.title_ur: عاد اور اضعاف کیا ہیں
segments.summary_en: A factor divides a number exactly with no remainder (6: 1, 2, 3, 6); a multiple is what you get by multiplying (3: 3, 6, 9, 12); 'factors divide, multiples multiply'.

segments.title_en: Mangoes: sharing for factors, baskets for multiples
segments.title_ur: آم بانٹنا اور ٹوکریاں: عاد اور اضعاف کی مثال
segments.summary_en: Ask 'How many friends can share 12 mangoes equally?' and guide children to 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12 = factors of 12; baskets of 5 mangoes give multiples of 5.

segments.title_en: Factor race in groups and the multiples hop game
segments.title_ur: گروپ میں عاد کا مقابلہ اور اضعاف پر چھلانگ
segments.summary_en: Groups get a number card (12, 15, 20) and race to list all its factors; numbers chalked on the floor, the teacher calls 3 and children hop only on multiples of 3.

segments.title_en: Number chart colouring for common multiples
segments.title_ur: نمبر چارٹ پر مشترک اضعاف
segments.summary_en: Children circle multiples of 2 in blue and 3 in red and answer 'Which numbers have both colours?'; a pencils-and-erasers pack question applies common multiples.

segments.title_en: Fixing the factor/multiple mix-up
segments.title_ur: عاد اور اضعاف کی الجھن دور کریں
segments.summary_en: Students often confuse the two; the rule 'factors are smaller than or equal to the number, multiples are equal or bigger' with 6 as an example is written on the board.

segments.title_en: Recap: three steps
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ: تین قدم
segments.summary_en: Recap: real-life examples, hands-on or group activities, keep checking understanding; thanks.

modules.title: HCF and LCM
modules.teacher_line_en: Teaching HCF/LCM to a big class? Board columns, pair checks and a race game
modules.teacher_line_ur: بڑی کلاس میں HCF/LCM؟ بورڈ پر کالم، جوڑیوں میں جانچ اور ایک تیز کھیل
modules.summary_en: An English narration explains HCF and LCM with 6 and 8 (list factors, circle common ones, HCF 2; list multiples, LCM 24), gives a balloon story for HCF (15 red and 20 blue balloons into equal groups, HCF 5), and then four classroom strategies: factor and multiple columns on the board with colour coding, pairs finding HCF of 4 and 10 and checking each other, groups each solving a different pair of numbers and presenting, and a 'common friend' race game. Caution: the LCM apple story (6 and 8 apples a day, 'after 4 days both have 24') is mathematically wrong.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ عاد اعظم اور ذو اضعاف اقل کو بورڈ کے کالموں، جوڑیوں، گروپ کام اور 'مشترک دوست' کھیل سے کیسے پڑھائیں۔
symptoms: children list factors and multiples but mix up which one HCF and LCM use
teacher works every HCF/LCM example on the board while the class copies
no pair or group practice in a maths lesson of 40+ children
teacher never says 'factor', 'multiple' or 'common' when explaining
modules.not_for: Teachers outside upper-primary maths or not teaching factors, multiples, HCF or LCM; avoid the apple-story chapter.

segments.title_en: Intro and what you will learn
segments.title_ur: تعارف اور اس ویڈیو کے مقاصد
segments.summary_en: Greeting and the video's aims for the teacher: explain HCF and LCM simply, use real-life examples, use pair and group strategies in large classes.

segments.title_en: HCF and LCM with 6 and 8
segments.title_ur: چھ اور آٹھ کی مثال سے HCF اور LCM
segments.summary_en: Defines HCF and LCM, then lists factors of 6 and 8 (common 1, 2; HCF 2) and multiples of 6 and 8 (smallest common 24; LCM 24).

segments.title_en: Real-life stories for LCM and HCF (contains an error)
segments.title_ur: روزمرہ کہانیاں (اس حصے میں غلطی ہے)
segments.summary_en: An apple story for LCM that is mathematically wrong (6 and 8 apples a day do not both give 24 after 4 days) and a correct balloon story for HCF (15 and 20 into equal groups, HCF 5), plus everyday uses of HCF. Not recommended because of the LCM error.

segments.title_en: Board columns and pair practice with peer checking
segments.title_ur: بورڈ پر کالم اور جوڑیوں میں مشق
segments.summary_en: Factor and multiple columns on the board in colour, children call out factors aloud; pairs get 4 and 10, find and circle common factors and the HCF, other pairs do LCM, then pairs check each other's work.

segments.title_en: Group task and the 'common friend' game
segments.title_ur: گروپ کام اور 'مشترک دوست' کھیل
segments.summary_en: 4-5 groups each get two numbers (HCF of 12 and 16, LCM of 3 and 5, HCF of 15 and 20), present after 5 minutes, and the teacher praises and corrects; then a race to find the 'common friend' of 9 and 12.

segments.title_en: Tips and closing
segments.title_ur: مشورے اور اختتام
segments.summary_en: Tips (start with small numbers, visuals, real examples, guiding questions like 'What numbers divide both?', end-of-class oral quiz) and a closing recap.

modules.title: Transformation of sentences
modules.teacher_line_en: Teach active/passive and reported speech with a sorting race and an error hunt
modules.teacher_line_ur: active/passive اور direct/indirect جملے چھانٹنے کے مقابلے اور غلطی ڈھونڈنے سے سکھائیں
modules.summary_en: A presenter teaches active/passive voice ('Ali eats an apple' / 'An apple is eaten by Ali') and direct/indirect speech ('Ali said, "I am tired"' / 'Ali said that he was tired'), explaining why pronouns change, tenses shift back and questions become statements. Teachers see classroom activities: a group sorting race of active vs passive sentences, error correction of deliberately wrong sentences, pairs turning a dialogue into reported speech, changing quoted newspaper headlines, and an integrated task rewriting a short text in indirect and passive form. Common mix-ups (subject/object in passive, pronoun changes) are named up front.
modules.summary_ur: آپ دیکھیں گے کہ انگریزی میں active/passive اور direct/indirect جملے گروپ میں چھانٹنے، غلطی درست کرنے اور مکالمے کی مشق سے کیسے سکھائیں۔
symptoms: grammar lesson where the teacher dictates the active-passive rule and students copy converted sentences from the board
students keep the same pronoun and tense in reported speech ('He said that I am tired')
no wrong example is ever shown or corrected; only right answers are read out
students never transform a sentence themselves in pairs or groups
modules.not_for: Teachers of Grades 1-5 or of Urdu, maths or science lessons; it is upper-grade English grammar content.

segments.title_en: Intro: what sentence transformation is
segments.title_ur: تعارف: جملوں کی تبدیلی کیا ہے
segments.summary_en: Greeting; transformation means changing a sentence from one form to another, e.g. active to passive, direct to indirect.

segments.title_en: Common mix-ups to expect
segments.title_ur: عام غلطیاں جن کی توقع رکھیں
segments.summary_en: Students mix up subject and object in passive and struggle with pronoun changes in indirect speech; passive suits an unknown doer; check whether meaning stays clear.

segments.title_en: Active vs passive: where the focus goes
segments.title_ur: فاعلی اور مفعولی جملہ: توجہ کہاں ہے
segments.summary_en: Active focuses on the doer, passive on what is acted on: 'Ali eats an apple' / 'An apple is eaten by Ali'; 'The teacher explains the lesson' / 'The lesson is explained by the teacher'.

segments.title_en: Sorting race and error correction
segments.title_ur: چھانٹنے کا مقابلہ اور غلطی کی درستی
segments.summary_en: Groups sort mixed sentences ('The boy kicked the ball' / 'The ball was kicked by the boy') into active and passive columns as a race, then correct a deliberately wrong sentence. The worked correction ('Ali was eats an apple' to 'Ali ate an apple') is muddled.

segments.title_en: Direct vs indirect and why words change
segments.title_ur: direct اور indirect، اور الفاظ کیوں بدلتے ہیں
segments.summary_en: 'Ali said, "I am tired"' becomes 'Ali said that he was tired'; why: pronouns change, tense shifts back (am/is to was, will to would), questions become statements, negative commands use 'not to'.

segments.title_en: Dialogue pairs, headlines and error hunt
segments.title_ur: مکالمے کی جوڑیاں، سرخیاں اور غلطی کی تلاش
segments.summary_en: One student reads direct speech and a partner reports it; quoted newspaper headlines are changed to reported speech; students fix 'He said that he is tired'.

segments.title_en: One task using both transformations
segments.title_ur: دونوں تبدیلیاں ایک سرگرمی میں
segments.summary_en: Rewrite 'Ali said, "I cleaned the room." The teacher praised him.' first into indirect, then passive: 'Ali said that he had cleaned the room. He was praised by the teacher.'

segments.title_en: Recap
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Summary of both transformations, their examples and the six strategies.

modules.title: Comprehension Strategies
modules.teacher_line_en: Children read fluently but can't say what it meant? Predict, infer, 5W, draw
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے روانی سے پڑھتے ہیں مگر مطلب نہیں بتا پاتے؟ اندازہ، چھپا مطلب، 5W خلاصہ، تصویر
modules.summary_en: A trainer, switching between English and Urdu, teaches four reading strategies each with a classroom routine: stop and predict after every paragraph ('What do you think will happen next? Why did you guess that?'), an inference clue T-chart filled in pairs ('red eyes, yawning' -> 'Ali is tired'), a 5W summary told on the fingers then written, and visualising a sentence then drawing it. It closes with how to put them together: think aloud while reading a short text, a comprehension journal (one prediction, inference, summary, sketch) and pairs who read and question each other.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ پڑھائی کے دوران اندازہ لگانا، چھپا مطلب سمجھنا، 5W سے خلاصہ بنانا اور ذہنی تصویر بنانا بچوں کو کیسے سکھائیں اور خود بول کر سوچ کیسے دکھائیں۔
symptoms: students read the passage aloud in turns and the only questions are literal recall ('who went to the market?')
teacher never pauses mid-text to ask 'what will happen next?' or 'how do you know?'
students copy lines from the text as answers instead of saying it in their own words
teacher never models their own thinking while reading
modules.not_for: Teachers whose pupils cannot yet decode words (send a phonics clip) or maths/science teachers; it is a talk with no classroom footage.

segments.title_en: Intro: reading is not comprehending; four strategies
segments.title_ur: تعارف: پڑھنا سمجھنا نہیں؛ چار حکمت عملیاں
segments.summary_en: Children read well but stall at 'what did you understand?'; the four strategies (predicting, inferring, summarising, visualising) are listed.

segments.title_en: Stop and predict after every paragraph
segments.title_ur: ہر پیراگراف کے بعد رک کر اندازہ
segments.summary_en: Predicting is explained with 'Dark clouds covered the sky'; while reading aloud pause after each paragraph, ask 'What do you think will happen next?' and make students justify the guess.

segments.title_en: Inference clue chart in pairs
segments.title_ur: جوڑیوں میں قرائن کا چارٹ
segments.summary_en: Inferring is reading between the lines ('red eyes and kept yawning' -> did not sleep well); a T-chart of text clues and 'I think...' is filled in pairs to join text evidence with their own thinking.

segments.title_en: 5W summary on the fingers, then in notebooks
segments.title_ur: انگلیوں پر 5W خلاصہ، پھر کاپی میں
segments.summary_en: Summarising as retelling the main idea in fewer words; write Who, What, Where, When, Why on the board, students say them orally on their fingers and then write the summary, so they stop copying lines.

segments.title_en: Visualise and draw the scene
segments.title_ur: ذہن میں تصویر بنائیں اور بنا کر دکھائیں
segments.summary_en: Students close their eyes on 'The garden was full of colourful butterflies' and then draw what they imagined in their notebooks, making comprehension visible.

segments.title_en: Think aloud, comprehension journals and peer monitoring
segments.title_ur: بول کر سوچنا، فہم کی ڈائری اور ساتھی کی جانچ
segments.summary_en: The teacher reads a short text aloud modelling prediction and inference out loud; students keep a journal with one prediction, inference, summary and sketch per story, and pairs read, use two strategies, question and check each other.

segments.title_en: Recap
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Recap of the four strategies and the classroom routines; comprehension improves with repeated use.

modules.title: Vocabulary Instructions to Reading and Writing
modules.teacher_line_en: Teach new English words with word webs, semantic maps and context clues
modules.teacher_line_ur: ورڈ ویب اور سیاق و سباق سے انگریزی کے نئے الفاظ سکھائیں
modules.summary_en: An English-narrated part shows three vocabulary tools: a word web ('happy' → joyful, smile, excited; opposite: sad) built after reading with synonym/antonym questions, a semantic map ('animal' → pets, farm, wild) used during reading and as a word bank for writing ('A lion is a wild animal'), and guessing a word from context ('a thick sweater because it was very cold'). A classroom clip in Urdu/English then shows a teacher pre-teaching words from a story paragraph (neighbour, some, yummy), reading it with the class and asking children to guess each meaning from the sentence and use it in a sentence.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں ورڈ ویب، سیمینٹک میپ اور سیاق و سباق کے ذریعے انگریزی کے نئے الفاظ سکھا کر انہیں پڑھنے اور لکھنے سے جوڑنا دکھایا گیا ہے۔
symptoms: teacher translates each new English word into Urdu and moves on
children read a passage aloud in chorus but are never asked what a word means
new words written on the board with no synonym, opposite or example sentence
writing task with no word bank or reference to words from the reading
modules.not_for: Maths or science teachers and teachers of early phonics; it is about word meaning in English reading and writing.

segments.title_en: Why vocabulary must be used, not just read (intro)
segments.title_ur: الفاظ صرف پڑھنا کافی نہیں (تعارف)
segments.summary_en: Greeting and objectives; children understand and write better when they know word meanings, but new words must be used in reading, speaking and writing.

segments.title_en: Word web: synonyms, opposites, a sentence
segments.title_ur: ورڈ ویب: ہم معنی، متضاد اور جملہ
segments.summary_en: Write 'happy' in the middle and link joyful, smile, excited and the opposite sad; after a story pick 2-3 new words, build a web together and ask for synonyms, antonyms and a sentence.

segments.title_en: Semantic map for reading and as a writing word bank
segments.title_ur: سیمینٹک میپ: پڑھنے میں اور لکھنے کے لیے الفاظ
segments.summary_en: Group 'animal' into pets, farm and wild animals; during a story ask which animals live on a farm or are wild, then show the same map when children write ('A lion is a wild animal. It lives in the jungle.').

segments.title_en: Guess the meaning from context
segments.title_ur: سیاق و سباق سے معنی کا اندازہ
segments.summary_en: Context means the words around a new word: 'a thick sweater because it was very cold' lets children guess 'thick'. While reading, stop and ask 'What does this word mean? Can we guess from the story?' and let children explain in their own words.

segments.title_en: Classroom clip: pre-teach words, then read the paragraph
segments.title_ur: کلاس کی جھلک: پہلے الفاظ، پھر پیراگراف
segments.summary_en: A teacher introduces target words from a story paragraph, the class reads the paragraph line by line after the teacher and stops each time a target word appears. Audio and transcript are rough.

segments.title_en: Classroom clip: children guess meanings from the sentence
segments.title_ur: کلاس کی جھلک: بچے جملے سے معنی بوجھتے ہیں
segments.summary_en: The teacher asks what 'neighbour', 'some' and 'yummy' mean from the sentence, links neighbour to the child sitting next to them, confirms 'yummy means tasty' and moves to using the words in sentences.

segments.title_en: Review and sign-off
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ اور اختتام
segments.summary_en: Recaps word webs, semantic maps and context clues and suggests starting with one new word a day.

modules.title: Integrating listening texts and oral narratives into literacy lessons to build auditory comprehension
modules.teacher_line_en: Read a story 3 times: listen, answer, retell; then draw it and predict what happens next
modules.teacher_line_ur: کہانی تین بار سنائیں: سنیں، جواب دیں، دہرائیں؛ پھر تصویر بنائیں اور اندازہ لگائیں
modules.summary_en: A trainer shows three no-cost listening routines built on a storybook or newspaper story: read it three times (first just listen, then pause for questions like 'what happened first?', then children retell it in pairs or act it out); listen and draw ('the boy was walking in the rain with a red umbrella', sketched in notebooks or even in sand); and listen and infer ('Zara saw dark clouds and heard thunder. What will happen next?'). It then links each listening task to speaking, drawing or a two-sentence written summary.
modules.summary_ur: آپ کہانی بار بار سنا کر، سن کر تصویر بنوا کر اور آگے کیا ہوگا کا اندازہ لگوا کر بچوں کی سن کر سمجھنے کی مہارت بڑھانا سیکھیں گے۔
symptoms: teacher reads a story aloud once and moves straight to the exercise
children are never asked to retell a story in their own words
no 'what do you think will happen next?' question during a read-aloud
listening activity is followed by no speaking, drawing or writing task
modules.not_for: Teachers of maths or science, or of older classes whose literacy lessons are already built on discussion and writing from texts.

segments.title_en: Why listening comprehension matters
segments.title_ur: سن کر سمجھنا کیوں ضروری ہے
segments.summary_en: Introduces listening as the base of reading and writing and promises low-cost strategies using listening texts and oral stories.

segments.title_en: Three levels of listening (theory)
segments.title_ur: سننے کی تین سطحیں
segments.summary_en: Explains three levels of listening (words and grammar, joining sentences, a deeper level of inferring and connecting to life) with a rain-in-my-street example.

segments.title_en: Repeated listening: listen, answer, retell
segments.title_ur: بار بار سننا: سنیں، جواب دیں، دہرائیں
segments.summary_en: Read the same storybook or newspaper story three times: once straight through, once with pauses for guiding questions, and once with children retelling in pairs or groups, or acting it out.

segments.title_en: Listen and draw: picture what you hear
segments.title_ur: سنیں اور تصویر بنائیں
segments.summary_en: Children make a picture in their head and sketch it ('a boy walking in the rain with a red umbrella'), using rough notebooks, chalk or even sand.

segments.title_en: Listen and infer: what happens next?
segments.title_ur: سنیں اور اندازہ لگائیں: آگے کیا ہوگا؟
segments.summary_en: Reads 'Zara saw dark clouds and heard thunder' and asks what will happen next; stop any story or radio clip halfway to ask for a prediction or a missing detail.

segments.title_en: From listening to speaking, drawing and writing
segments.title_ur: سننے سے بولنے، تصویر اور لکھنے تک
segments.summary_en: Links each listening task to a literacy output: retell orally, draw a quick picture, or write a two-sentence summary.

segments.title_en: Recap: retell, draw, infer
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ: دہرانا، تصویر، اندازہ
segments.summary_en: Summarises the three strategies (repeated narratives, listen and draw, listen and infer) and signs off.

modules.title: استعجابیہ، تمنائی، شرطیہ اور امر و نہی جملوں کی پہچان اور تدریس
modules.teacher_line_en: Urdu sentence types made active: fix-the-error, role-play and sorting slips
modules.teacher_line_ur: جملوں کی اقسام مزے سے: غلطی ڈھونڈیں، رول پلے کریں، پرچیاں چھانٹیں
modules.summary_en: Four Urdu sentence types are explained with signal words and examples: tamannai (wish, 'کاش'), istejabiya (surprise, 'واہ'), sharti (condition, 'اگر... تو'), and amr-o-nahi (command/prohibition, 'کتاب کھولو', 'شور مت کرو'), linked to instructions children hear daily. Then six activities: write one of each, identify types on the board, correct a wrong conditional ('اگر تم آئے تو ہم خوش ہیں' → 'اگر تم آؤ گے تو ہم خوش ہوں گے'), role-play one type each, sort sentence slips into four categories, and pair practice where one says a sentence and the partner names its type.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ تمنائی، استعجابیہ، شرطیہ اور امر و نہی جملے مثالوں سے کیسے سکھائیں اور غلطی ڈھونڈنے، رول پلے، پرچیوں کی چھانٹی اور جوڑی میں مشق سے بچوں کو کیسے استعمال کروائیں۔
symptoms: sentence types defined and copied from the book with no student-made sentences
children only memorise definitions; never asked to identify or correct a sentence
no game, sorting or pair task in an Urdu grammar lesson
students mix tense in 'اگر... تو' sentences and the teacher only says 'galat'
modules.not_for: Teachers of non-Urdu lessons or of Grades 1-3; it is grammar content for middle grades.

segments.title_en: Why teach these sentence types
segments.title_ur: جملوں کی یہ اقسام کیوں سکھائیں
segments.summary_en: Intro: sentences we use daily for surprise, wishes, conditions and commands make speech and writing expressive; four types.

segments.title_en: Wish, surprise and condition sentences
segments.title_ur: تمنائی، استعجابیہ اور شرطیہ جملے
segments.summary_en: Signal words and examples: 'کاش' for wishes, 'واہ' for surprise, 'اگر... تو' for conditions; children are asked to make their own wish and 'اگر' sentences.

segments.title_en: Command and prohibition sentences from classroom instructions
segments.title_ur: امر و نہی: کلاس کی ہدایات سے مثالیں
segments.summary_en: 'کتاب کھولو', 'شور مت کرو', 'لائن میں کھڑے ہو جاؤ' show that everyday classroom instructions are amr-o-nahi sentences.

segments.title_en: Write, identify, and fix the wrong sentence
segments.title_ur: لکھیں، پہچانیں اور غلط جملہ درست کریں
segments.summary_en: Children write one sentence of two types and discuss the feeling each shows, identify types on the board, then correct 'اگر تم آئے تو ہم خوش ہیں' to 'اگر تم آؤ گے تو ہم خوش ہوں گے'.

segments.title_en: Role-play, sorting slips and pair practice
segments.title_ur: رول پلے، پرچیوں کی چھانٹی اور جوڑی میں مشق
segments.summary_en: Four children each speak one sentence type; groups sort sentence slips into four categories; in pairs one says a sentence and the partner names its type.

segments.title_en: Reflection questions and recap
segments.title_ur: سوچنے کے سوال اور خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: The teacher is asked which types they use in daily instructions and which type students find hardest; recap of the four types and six strategies.

modules.title: لغت کا استعمال سیکھنا
modules.teacher_line_en: Children lost in the dictionary? Synonym sentences, an antonym race, a word chain
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے لغت میں الجھ جاتے ہیں؟ مترادف سے جملے، متضاد کی دوڑ اور لفظی زنجیر
modules.summary_en: Two teachers talk through teaching dictionary use (لغت) in Urdu for Grades 4-5: first what a dictionary tells us (meaning, synonyms, antonyms, e.g. خوبصورت: حسین، دلکش، جمیل / بدصورت), then three activities: each child picks a synonym from the dictionary and writes their own sentence, a group race to find five antonyms of اندھیرا, and a word chain (کتاب، علم، دانائی، جہالت) built link by link on the board, extended into a story for Grade 5.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ مترادف سے جملے، متضاد ڈھونڈنے کی دوڑ اور لفظی زنجیر کے ذریعے بچوں کو لغت کا استعمال دلچسپ انداز میں کیسے سکھائیں۔
symptoms: teacher reads out word meanings and children copy them; no child looks a word up
children are asked for a word's meaning and answer only with one memorised synonym
new words are never used by the children in a sentence of their own
vocabulary practice is only copying from the board
modules.not_for: Teachers of early grades still learning letters, or non-Urdu lessons; it is Urdu vocabulary and dictionary work for upper primary.

segments.title_en: What a dictionary tells us: meaning, synonym, antonym
segments.title_ur: لغت ہمیں کیا بتاتی ہے: معنی، مترادف، متضاد
segments.summary_en: A teacher's Grade 5 class gets confused by the dictionary; the colleague first teaches what a dictionary gives (meaning, synonyms, antonyms) with خوبصورت as the example before children open one.

segments.title_en: Synonym activity: choose one and write your own sentence
segments.title_ur: مترادف کی سرگرمی: ایک لفظ چن کر اپنا جملہ
segments.summary_en: The teacher shows synonyms of خوبصورت in the dictionary, each child picks one and writes their own sentence ('باغ دلکش ہے'), showing that a word has many shades.

segments.title_en: Antonym race and word chain
segments.title_ur: متضاد کی دوڑ اور لفظی زنجیر
segments.summary_en: Groups race to find five antonyms of اندھیرا in the dictionary; then a word chain where each child adds a link (کتاب، علم، دانائی، جہالت) on the board, made harder for Grade 5 and turned into a story.

segments.title_en: Recap of the three activities
segments.title_ur: تینوں سرگرمیوں کا خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Recaps synonym sentences, the antonym race and the word chain, and that the objective is met when children open the dictionary themselves.

modules.title: پیراگراف کی تنظیم اور ساخت
modules.teacher_line_en: Model a paragraph on the board, then groups order jumbled sentences into one
modules.teacher_line_ur: بورڈ پر نمونے کا پیراگراف لکھیں، پھر گروپ الٹے پلٹے جملے ترتیب دیں
modules.summary_en: A podcast conversation with a Grade 4-5 Urdu teacher on teaching paragraph structure (title, beginning, middle, ending). Teachers hear a short story about a sparrow followed by 'where did it start, what happened in the middle, how did it end?', then see three steps: writing a model paragraph 'میرا اسکول' on the board sentence by sentence, a group game putting jumbled sentences about 'میرا دوست' into order, and sentence-starter prompts for 'میری زندگی کا سب سے خوش دن' that children complete from their own experience.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سنیں گے کہ کہانی، بورڈ پر نمونے کے پیراگراف، الٹے پلٹے جملوں کے کھیل اور رہنما اشاروں سے بچوں کو پیراگراف کا آغاز، درمیان اور اختتام لکھنا کیسے سکھائیں۔
symptoms: writing task is set as 'write a paragraph on my school' with no model on the board
children's paragraphs are lists of unrelated sentences with no beginning or ending
teacher dictates a paragraph for children to copy word for word
no starter phrases or prompts are given to children who cannot begin
modules.not_for: Teachers of Grades 1-2 or of maths and science lessons; it is upper-primary Urdu writing.

segments.title_en: Intro: four parts of a paragraph
segments.title_ur: تعارف: پیراگراف کے چار حصے
segments.summary_en: Greeting; the four elements (beginning, sequence, title, ending); the guest Grade 4-5 Urdu teacher is welcomed.

segments.title_en: A story to show beginning, middle and end
segments.title_ur: کہانی سے آغاز، درمیان اور اختتام
segments.summary_en: A short sparrow story, then 'Where did the story start? What happened in the middle? How did it end?' so children see that every paragraph has three parts under a topic.

segments.title_en: Model paragraph on the board: 'میرا اسکول'
segments.title_ur: بورڈ پر نمونے کا پیراگراف: 'میرا اسکول'
segments.summary_en: The teacher writes the title, an opening sentence, detail sentences (10 rooms, a library, hardworking teachers) and a closing line, naming each part so children see the whole structure.

segments.title_en: Jumbled sentences game in groups
segments.title_ur: گروپ میں الٹے پلٹے جملوں کا کھیل
segments.summary_en: Jumbled sentences about 'میرا دوست' on the board; groups decide the beginning, middle and ending, put them in order and present their paragraph.

segments.title_en: Sentence-starter prompts for Grade 5
segments.title_ur: گریڈ 5 کے لیے جملوں کے رہنما اشارے
segments.summary_en: For 'میری زندگی کا سب سے خوش دن', starters on the board ('…تھا جب', 'سب سے پہلے میں نے', 'یہ دن میرے لیے خاص تھا کیونکہ') that children complete from their own experience.

segments.title_en: Recap
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Recap of the three strategies and the four parts of a paragraph; closing.

modules.title: مربوط اور غیر مربوط گفتگو
modules.teacher_line_en: Children answer in single words? Three Urdu speaking games for linked sentences
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے ایک لفظ میں جواب دیتے ہیں؟ جڑے جملوں میں بولنے کی تین آسان سرگرمیاں
modules.summary_en: A trainer contrasts connected (مربوط) and disconnected speech and gives three Urdu speaking activities: guided dialogue in pairs on 'my summer holidays' with prompt questions (where did you go, what did you see, what did you learn) where one child answers and the partner repeats it as connected sentences (Grade 3-4); a story chain from one opening line where each child adds a linked sentence and off-topic lines are corrected (Grade 5); and picture talk where Grade 2-3 children make short sentences about a market or school picture and the teacher has them put the sentences in sequence. It ends with a four-question observation checklist and a gentle next-step comment ('your sentences are good; joined together they will be even clearer').
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ رہنما مکالمہ، کہانی کی زنجیر اور تصویر سے گفتگو کے ذریعے بچوں کو جڑے ہوئے جملوں میں بولنا کیسے سکھائیں اور شفقت سے رائے کیسے دیں۔
symptoms: students answer in one word or one disconnected sentence and the teacher accepts it
Urdu lesson where only the teacher speaks at length; no pair or chain speaking task
teacher responds to a muddled answer with 'ghalat' or 'theek se bolo' without saying how to join the ideas
younger children are asked to 'speak about' a topic with no picture or prompt questions
modules.not_for: Teachers of maths or science, or teachers whose class already speaks at length; it is a talk with no classroom footage.

segments.title_en: Intro: connected vs disconnected speech
segments.title_ur: تعارف: مربوط اور غیر مربوط گفتگو
segments.summary_en: Children speak naturally, but are their sentences linked? Definition of connected speech (sentences joined logically and fluently) versus scattered, unrelated sentences.

segments.title_en: Guided dialogue in pairs: answer, then retell as connected sentences
segments.title_ur: جوڑیوں میں رہنما مکالمہ: جواب، پھر جڑے جملوں میں دہرانا
segments.summary_en: Topic 'my summer holidays' for Grade 3-4: the teacher writes prompt questions, pairs are formed, one child answers and the partner repeats the answers as connected sentences.

segments.title_en: Story chain: each child adds a linked line
segments.title_ur: کہانی کی زنجیر: ہر بچہ ایک جڑا ہوا جملہ جوڑے
segments.summary_en: For Grade 5 the teacher starts a story with one line, each child adds a sentence that continues it, and an unrelated sentence is corrected by the class or teacher; builds listening and coherence.

segments.title_en: Picture talk: short sentences put in sequence
segments.title_ur: تصویر سے گفتگو: چھوٹے جملے ترتیب سے
segments.summary_en: Grade 2-3 children look at a market or school picture, answer 'what is happening first? then what?', make short sentences, and the teacher has them arrange the sentences in order.

segments.title_en: Observation checklist and a gentle next-step comment
segments.title_ur: مشاہدے کی فہرست اور شفقت بھری رہنمائی
segments.summary_en: Four checklist questions (are sentences linked, on topic, fluent, responding to others?) and feedback that praises the sentences and says to join them so they are clearer.

segments.title_en: Recap
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Recap of the difference, the three activities and the checklist; connected speaking also improves writing.

modules.title: ارکان سازی
modules.teacher_line_en: Three Urdu word games: break into letters, word chains, prefixes
modules.teacher_line_ur: اردو لفظ سازی کے تین کھیل: حروف، لفظوں کی زنجیر، سابقے لاحقے
modules.summary_en: The presenter teaches three Urdu word-building activities: break a word into letters (کتاب → ک، ت، ا، ب) and say each one, with magnetic letters or picture cards for children who struggle to write; a word chain where each new word starts with the last letter of the previous one, played in mixed-level groups; and prefixes and suffixes (خوش → ناخوش، خوشی) where each group makes as many new words as it can from دوست، علم، کھیل. It ends with quick checks and ideas for giving struggling learners more time and fast finishers a create-a-word task.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں لفظ کو حروف میں توڑنے، لفظوں کی زنجیر بنانے اور سابقے لاحقے لگا کر نئے لفظ بنانے کی سرگرمیاں کمزور اور تیز بچوں کے لیے مدد سمیت دکھائی گئی ہیں۔
symptoms: Urdu lesson where children only copy words from the board and never break or build words
spelling taught by repetition of whole words with no letter-by-letter work
no game or group task in an Urdu language period
every child gets the same task; no extra support or extension
modules.not_for: English, maths or science teachers; it is about Urdu letters, prefixes and suffixes in primary grades.

segments.title_en: Why word-building matters (intro)
segments.title_ur: لفظ سازی کیوں ضروری ہے (تعارف)
segments.summary_en: Greeting; children should understand how words are made from letters, prefixes and suffixes; three methods are announced, each with support for slower learners.

segments.title_en: Break a word into letters and say each one
segments.title_ur: لفظ کو حروف میں توڑ کر ہر حرف بولیں
segments.summary_en: Children write a word such as کتاب as separate letters and say each one; give magnetic letters or picture cards to those who find writing hard. A short classroom clip shows children spelling words out and copying them in notebooks.

segments.title_en: Word chain from the last letter
segments.title_ur: آخری حرف سے لفظوں کی زنجیر
segments.summary_en: Say کتاب and children give words starting with ب, building a chain; picture cards help shy children, and groups mix levels so all can join. Suited to Grades 3-4.

segments.title_en: Prefixes and suffixes: which group makes most words?
segments.title_ur: سابقے اور لاحقے: کون سا گروپ زیادہ لفظ بنائے گا؟
segments.summary_en: Explain that a prefix changes meaning at the start and a suffix comes at the end (خوش → ناخوش، خوشی); give each group a root word (دوست، علم، کھیل) to build new words; children who find writing hard say theirs at the board.

segments.title_en: Quick checks, support and extension
segments.title_ur: فوری جانچ، مدد اور اضافی کام
segments.summary_en: After a short recap: checks (split a word into letters, play the chain game, make 3-4 words from a root word), more time for struggling learners and a create-a-word-and-sentence task for fast finishers.

segments.title_en: Closing message
segments.title_ur: اختتامی پیغام
segments.summary_en: Words are the bricks of language; breaking and joining words builds confidence in reading and writing; include every child.

modules.title: جملے کی ساخت، فاعل و مفعول، اسم نکرہ و معرفہ
modules.teacher_line_en: Children find the doer, the object and proper vs common nouns in their own Urdu sentences
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے اپنے جملوں میں فاعل، مفعول اور اسم نکرہ و معرفہ خود پہچانیں
modules.summary_en: A trainer teaches Urdu sentence structure through meaning: in 'علی کتاب پڑھتا ہے' children say who does the action (فاعل), what it is done to (مفعول) and the action (فعل), and what is lost if one is removed. Children then fill blanks in sentences with the missing فاعل or مفعول (with a picture if they are stuck), sort a list of nouns into common (نکرہ) and proper (معرفہ), and write three sentences of their own, label every part, and present them for other groups to comment on.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ بچے جملے میں فاعل، مفعول اور فعل اور اسم نکرہ و معرفہ کو مطلب کی بنیاد پر کیسے پہچانیں اور اپنے جملے بنا کر ان کا تجزیہ کیسے کریں۔
symptoms: teacher dictates definitions of فاعل and مفعول and children copy them
children are never asked 'who is doing the work? what is it done to?' about a real sentence
grammar practice is only underlining in the textbook; children never write their own sentences
when a child cannot find the فاعل the teacher repeats the definition louder
modules.not_for: Teachers of English, maths or science, or of Grade 1-2 Urdu classes still learning letters and harakat.

segments.title_en: Teach structure and meaning together
segments.title_ur: جملے کی بناوٹ اور مطلب ساتھ سکھائیں
segments.summary_en: Introduces the aim: teach how a sentence is built and the role of each word, not grammar rules alone.

segments.title_en: Doer, object, action: 'علی کتاب پڑھتا ہے'
segments.title_ur: فاعل، مفعول، فعل: علی کتاب پڑھتا ہے
segments.summary_en: Gives an example, then asks who is doing the work and what it is done to; labels علی as فاعل, کتاب as مفعول and پڑھتا ہے as فعل, and asks what is lost if one is removed.

segments.title_en: Fill the blank with the doer or the object
segments.title_ur: خالی جگہ میں فاعل یا مفعول لکھیں
segments.summary_en: Children complete sentences with a missing فاعل or مفعول by asking 'who is doing it? what is it done to?'; a child who is stuck is shown a picture of the action.

segments.title_en: Common vs proper nouns: underline and sort
segments.title_ur: اسم نکرہ اور معرفہ: نشان لگائیں اور الگ کریں
segments.summary_en: Explains معرفہ (a particular person, place or thing) vs نکرہ (general) with 'تعلیم و تربیت' as a book title, then children underline one of each in their own sentences and sort a list (احمد، مسجد، لاہور، کتاب…).

segments.title_en: Analyse your own sentences, groups give feedback
segments.title_ur: اپنے جملوں کا تجزیہ، گروپ رائے دیں
segments.summary_en: Children write three new sentences and label فاعل, مفعول and نکرہ or معرفہ in each; each group presents and other groups comment.

segments.title_en: Recap
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Lists what was covered (sentence parts, فاعل and مفعول, نکرہ and معرفہ, sentence analysis) and signs off.

modules.title: Learning from Student Data
modules.teacher_line_en: Quiz marked, many wrong? Count the common mistakes and reteach to a small group
modules.teacher_line_ur: کوئز میں بہت غلطیاں؟ عام غلطیاں گنیں اور چھوٹے گروپ کو دوبارہ پڑھائیں
modules.summary_en: An English-narrated slide story: a Grade 5 maths teacher marks a short fractions quiz, tallies the errors (12 confused numerator and denominator, 8 added fractions without equal denominators, 5 all correct), reteaches the next day with pizza and chocolate-bar drawings, puts the children who need help in a small group with bottle caps and paper plates while the strong ones get harder problems, and re-quizzes a few days later. The teacher learns to use quiz results, oral questions or classwork to decide what to reteach and to whom.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ چھوٹے کوئز کی عام غلطیاں گن کر اگلے دن دوبارہ کیسے پڑھائیں اور بچوں کو ضرورت کے مطابق گروپوں میں کیسے بانٹیں۔
symptoms: teacher moves to the next topic after a quiz without mentioning the mistakes children made
the same explanation is repeated louder when children get it wrong
whole class gets the same task although many children failed the last check
teacher never refers to what last lesson's classwork or test showed
modules.not_for: Teachers who already reteach from quiz results; and Urdu-only viewers, since the narration and slides are in English.

segments.title_en: Read the quiz: tally the common mistakes
segments.title_ur: کوئز دیکھیں: عام غلطیاں گنیں
segments.summary_en: After two weeks of fractions a Grade 5 teacher gives a short quiz, sees the same mistakes (numerator/denominator mix-up, adding without equal denominators) and notes counts: 12, 8, and 5 all correct.

segments.title_en: Reteach the next day with pictures
segments.title_ur: اگلے دن تصویروں کی مدد سے دوبارہ سمجھانا
segments.summary_en: 'Let's become fraction detectives': the teacher says the quiz showed tricky parts, draws pizzas and chocolate bars ('half a pizza and another half?') to explain again; then defines data-driven instruction.

segments.title_en: Group by need, then re-quiz
segments.title_ur: ضرورت کے مطابق گروپ اور دوبارہ کوئز
segments.summary_en: A small group that needs help practises with bottle caps and paper plates, those who understood get harder problems; a second short quiz a few days later shows the gap closing.

segments.title_en: Takeaway: tests are tools, not just marks
segments.title_ur: نتیجہ: ٹیسٹ صرف نمبروں کے لیے نہیں
segments.summary_en: Closing message that quiz results, oral questions and classwork should guide reteaching; the narration ends at about 182 s and the rest is non-speech.

modules.title: Design and Assign differentiated Instructional Activities
modules.teacher_line_en: Some finish in 2 minutes, others never start? One goal, three levels of practice
modules.teacher_line_ur: کچھ بچے فوراً ختم، کچھ شروع بھی نہیں کرتے؟ ایک مقصد، تین لیول کی مشق
modules.summary_en: A narrated story of a primary teacher whose class works at very different speeds. She keeps one objective for all (add two-digit numbers with carrying), models 47 + 36 with a place-value chart, then seats children in three level groups: strugglers solve 24 + 18 in pairs with sticks and counters while she stays with them, the middle group solves two sums in notebooks writing every step, and fast finishers do real-life word problems. Homework is differentiated the same way (two-digit sums, totalling household items, adding up an electricity bill).
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں ایک کہانی کے ذریعے دکھایا گیا ہے کہ ایک ہی مقصد رکھتے ہوئے کمزور، درمیانے اور تیز بچوں کو ان کے لیول کے مطابق الگ الگ مشق اور ہوم ورک کیسے دیں۔
symptoms: every child gets the same exercise from the book at the same time
fast finishers sit idle or chat while others are stuck
struggling children get no objects or extra help, only the same sum again
homework is identical for the whole class
modules.not_for: Teachers whose class is at a similar level, or whose next step is explanation or questioning rather than practice tasks.

segments.title_en: The problem: one lesson, very different speeds
segments.title_ur: مسئلہ: ایک سبق، سیکھنے کی رفتار مختلف
segments.summary_en: Story setup: copies show some children far behind and some far ahead; a senior colleague advises one learning goal for all with practice matched to each child's level.

segments.title_en: One goal, three level groups: counters, steps, word problems
segments.title_ur: ایک مقصد، تین گروپ: کاؤنٹر، مرحلہ وار حل، لفظی سوال
segments.summary_en: The teacher models 47 + 36 with a place-value chart, then groups by level: pairs with sticks and counters (24 + 18) with the teacher beside them, a middle group solving two sums writing each step, and a fast group on real-life word problems; she circulates to every group.

segments.title_en: Differentiated homework with the same goal
segments.title_ur: ایک ہی مقصد کے ساتھ لیول کے مطابق ہوم ورک
segments.summary_en: Homework at three levels (two-digit sums; totalling household items; adding up an electricity bill and three ways to save power); next day every group succeeds, and the lesson: same goal, practice matched to level.

modules.title: Creating Learning Stations: Helping Students Learn at Their Own Pace
modules.teacher_line_en: 40+ children, one task? Set up 3 low-cost stations and rotate groups every 10 minutes
modules.teacher_line_ur: چالیس سے زیادہ بچے اور ایک ہی کام؟ تین سستے اسٹیشن بنائیں، گروپ ہر دس منٹ بعد بدلیں
modules.summary_en: A trainer shows how to run 3-4 low-cost learning stations in a crowded class: a reading corner with storybooks and chart-paper questions ('Who was the main character? What happened at the end?'), a maths station where children solve 5 caps + 3 caps, 10 - 8 and 6 x 8 with stones, bottle caps and ice-cream sticks, and a creative-writing station with picture prompts. Groups of 3-4 spend 10 minutes per station and rotate while the teacher circulates, notes who needs help, and uses the notes to plan the next day.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ سیکھیں گے کہ بڑی کلاس میں پڑھائی، ریاضی اور تخلیقی تحریر کے سستے اسٹیشن بنا کر گروپوں کو دس دس منٹ بعد کیسے گھمائیں تاکہ ہر بچہ اپنی رفتار سے سیکھے۔
symptoms: the whole class does one task from the board while early finishers sit idle or make noise
teacher works with the whole class at once and never with a small group
no materials or objects used for counting practice
teacher says nothing to children who finish early except 'wait' or 'chup'
modules.not_for: Teachers of secondary grades or who already run group rotations; it is about organising stations, not about questioning or explanation.

segments.title_en: Intro: learning at their own pace
segments.title_ur: تعارف: اپنی رفتار سے سیکھنا
segments.summary_en: Introduces learning stations as a strategy for crowded, low-resource classrooms and links it to the curriculum's active-learning goals.

segments.title_en: What stations are, and the reading station
segments.title_ur: اسٹیشن کیا ہیں اور پڑھائی کا اسٹیشن
segments.summary_en: 3-4 simple corners with different tasks made from chalk, old chart paper and storybooks; the reading corner has books and chart-paper questions that children answer orally or in notebooks, individually or in pairs, while another group does classwork.

segments.title_en: Maths station with bottle caps and a writing station
segments.title_ur: ریاضی کا اسٹیشن (ڈھکنوں سے) اور تحریر کا اسٹیشن
segments.summary_en: Counting with stones, bottle caps, matchboxes and ice-cream sticks to solve 5 caps + 3 caps, 10 - 8, 6 x 8 in copies; then a creative-writing station with papers and prompts where groups discuss and write.

segments.title_en: Rotate groups and observe as facilitator
segments.title_ur: گروپوں کی گردش اور ٹیچر بطور سہولت کار
segments.summary_en: Divide the class into groups, 10 minutes per station then rotate; the teacher circulates, observes who is engaged or needs help, writes short notes for next day's planning; fast learners do more tasks, struggling ones work at their pace.

segments.title_en: Recap and plan your own stations
segments.title_ur: خلاصہ اور اپنے اسٹیشن کی منصوبہ بندی
segments.summary_en: Recaps the three stations and asks the teacher to think which stations would help their own class and to try one in the next English or maths period.

route_gate.reason: context_gated_move: a three-corner classroom redesign with its own catalogue caveat ('needs a changed lesson plan… not a quick next move'). v9 sent 122-s3 for a C1 'how did you work it out' card (Z238, full run) and 122-s2 for a D3 student-to-student talk card (Z477, card mode): wrong by both experts, R1/R2 = 2, as a competing system rather than the card's move. Right only for a differentiation card that itself asks for stations or levelled corners.

modules.title: گوگل ڈرائیو کے ذریعے کلاس میٹریلز کو منظم کرنا
modules.teacher_line_en: Worksheets keep getting lost? Store and share them with colleagues on Google Drive
modules.teacher_line_ur: ورک شیٹس گم ہو جاتی ہیں؟ گوگل ڈرائیو پر محفوظ کریں اور ساتھیوں سے شیئر کریں
modules.summary_en: A presenter walks through the Google Drive phone app: install and sign in with Gmail, tap plus to create a folder (e.g. 'Grade 5 English lessons'), upload a worksheet photo or lesson-plan PDF from the gallery, and share it with a colleague as viewer or editor. A worked example has two teachers co-plan a Grade 5 story-writing lesson in a shared file, and the practice task is to upload one worksheet and share it with a colleague as editor.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ موبائل پر گوگل ڈرائیو میں فولڈر بنا کر ورک شیٹس اور سبق کے منصوبے کیسے محفوظ کریں اور ساتھی اساتذہ کے ساتھ کیسے شیئر کریں۔
symptoms: teacher mentions lost worksheets or rewriting the same reading passage again
teacher says they plan alone and never share materials with colleagues
modules.not_for: Any teacher whose report is about classroom teaching; it is a Google Drive app how-to that needs a Gmail account and mobile data.

segments.title_en: Intro: why Google Drive on a phone
segments.title_ur: تعارف: موبائل پر گوگل ڈرائیو کیوں
segments.summary_en: Google Drive as a tool to organise class materials and co-plan with colleagues, taught on the mobile app because most teachers use phones.

segments.title_en: Install, create a folder, upload, share as viewer or editor
segments.title_ur: انسٹال، فولڈر، اپلوڈ اور ویوور یا ایڈیٹر کے طور پر شیئر
segments.summary_en: Install the app and sign in with Gmail, create a folder with the plus button, upload a worksheet photo or lesson plan PDF, and share it with a colleague's Gmail as viewer or editor.

segments.title_en: Co-plan a lesson in a shared file; practice task
segments.title_ur: مشترکہ فائل میں مل کر سبق کی منصوبہ بندی؛ مشق
segments.summary_en: Two teachers co-plan a Grade 5 English story-writing lesson: one uploads a story outline, the colleague as editor adds an activity; practice task: upload one worksheet and share it as editor.

modules.title: کے ذریعے آسان پوسٹر اور گرافکس بنانا (Canva)
modules.teacher_line_en: Make a picture-word chart for your class on your phone with Canva
modules.teacher_line_ur: اپنے فون پر Canva سے کلاس کے لیے تصویری چارٹ بنائیں
modules.summary_en: A presenter shows how to use the free Canva phone app to make classroom posters, charts, flashcards and worksheets: install and log in with Gmail, pick a template, add text and free images, then download as image or PDF to share on WhatsApp or print. The one classroom example is an Urdu vocabulary chart with a picture above each word; the task is to make a '5 new Urdu words with pictures' poster and share it with colleagues.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں موبائل پر Canva ایپ سے کلاس کے لیے پوسٹر، چارٹ اور فلیش کارڈ بنانے کے مراحل بتائے گئے ہیں۔
symptoms: teacher explains new words only verbally with no chart or picture
teacher mentions having no printed material or posters for the topic
modules.not_for: Any teacher whose report is about what happens in the lesson itself; this is an app how-to that needs a smartphone, data and a Gmail login, and shows no classroom teaching.

segments.title_en: What Canva is and why the phone app
segments.title_ur: Canva کیا ہے اور موبائل ایپ کیوں
segments.summary_en: Canva is a free design app; most teachers only have a phone, so the training uses the mobile app to make charts, vocabulary posters, worksheets and visuals (the website works the same on a computer).

segments.title_en: Four steps: install, template, add text and images, save
segments.title_ur: چار مراحل: انسٹال، ٹیمپلیٹ، متن و تصویر، محفوظ
segments.summary_en: Install from the Play Store and log in with Gmail or Facebook, pick a poster/flashcard/worksheet template, add text and free images, then download as image or PDF to share on WhatsApp or print.

segments.title_en: Example: an Urdu picture-word chart, and a practice task
segments.title_ur: مثال: اردو تصویری الفاظ کا چارٹ اور مشق
segments.summary_en: A simple chart template with pictures and the words written below for an Urdu vocabulary chart; the practice task is a '5 new Urdu words with pictures' or 'steps of addition' poster shared with colleagues.

modules.title: Using Google Meet and Zoom for Effective Teaching
modules.teacher_line_en: Teaching online from your phone: start a Meet or Zoom class, share your screen
modules.teacher_line_ur: فون سے آن لائن کلاس: گوگل میٹ یا زوم شروع کریں اور اسکرین شیئر کریں
modules.summary_en: A step-by-step phone how-to for online classes: download Google Meet or Zoom, start or schedule a meeting, share the link on WhatsApp, screen-share slides or worksheets, mute all, enable 'raise hand', use Zoom breakout rooms, and share recordings. A short section adds online-session habits (attendance and objective checklist, 'Can you find the main idea?' on a shared passage, a 'what did you like most?' feedback round) and fixes for cameras off, weak internet and an overloaded host.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ موبائل فون پر گوگل میٹ اور زوم سے آن لائن کلاس شروع کرنا، لنک بھیجنا، اسکرین شیئر کرنا اور کلاس سنبھالنے کے فیچر استعمال کرنا سیکھیں گے۔
symptoms: teacher says they run or plan online/remote classes and struggle with the app
remote session where students speak over each other with no mute or raise-hand control
modules.not_for: Teachers whose report is about their in-person classroom lesson; this is an app how-to for online classes and needs a smartphone and data.

segments.title_en: Why Meet and Zoom on a phone
segments.title_ur: فون پر میٹ اور زوم کیوں
segments.summary_en: Intro: these tools became a lifeline in the pandemic; most teachers have phones not laptops, so the steps use mobile apps.

segments.title_en: Download, start a meeting, invite students
segments.title_ur: ایپ ڈاؤن لوڈ، میٹنگ شروع اور طلبہ کو دعوت
segments.summary_en: Install from Play Store, log in, create an instant or scheduled meeting, and send the link or ID on WhatsApp or email.

segments.title_en: Screen share, mute all, raise hand, breakout rooms
segments.title_ur: اسکرین شیئر، سب کو خاموش، ہاتھ اٹھانا، گروپ روم
segments.summary_en: Share slides/PDFs/worksheets, send materials in chat, mute/unmute all, enable raise hand, Zoom breakout rooms, and share recordings afterwards.

segments.title_en: Online session habits: checklist, main-idea question, feedback
segments.title_ur: آن لائن سیشن کی عادتیں: چیک لسٹ، سوال، فیڈبیک
segments.summary_en: Start each session with attendance and objectives, highlight a passage and ask 'Can you find the main idea?', solve a sum step by step on screen, and end asking what students liked most.

segments.title_en: Common problems and fixes; closing
segments.title_ur: عام مسائل اور ان کا حل؛ اختتام
segments.summary_en: Cameras off: confirm participation via chat; weak internet: send the recording; overload: assign a co-host; plan a short session with one slide, a group discussion and feedback.

modules.title: Restorative Practices
modules.teacher_line_en: Tired of scolding over fights? Try a circle, I-statements and praise
modules.teacher_line_ur: جھگڑوں پر ڈانٹ ڈانٹ کر تھک گئے؟ دائرہ نشست، 'مجھے محسوس ہوتا ہے' جملے اور تعریف
modules.summary_en: A scripted conversation between a new teacher worn out by daily fights and scolding and an experienced colleague who explains four restorative practices: a weekly circle where each child shares feelings in turn while others only listen (used the day after two pupils fought, ending in mutual apology); I-statements ('I feel ... when ... because ...') taught with a poster and role-play scenarios; reflection questions after a conflict ('How did it feel to be heard? What will you do differently next time?'); and specific public praise for respectful behaviour.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ سنیں گے کہ ڈانٹ اور سزا کے بجائے دائرہ نشست، 'مجھے محسوس ہوتا ہے' والے جملوں، سوچنے والے سوالوں اور تعریف سے بچوں کے جھگڑے کیسے کم کریں۔
symptoms: teacher scolds or threatens punishment repeatedly over quarrels between children
children blame each other ('isne meri pencil li') and the teacher settles it by deciding who is wrong
no child is asked how they feel or what they will do differently
teacher never praises a child for respectful behaviour
modules.not_for: Teachers whose need is instructional (questioning, explanation, content); this is about conflict and class climate and raises no FICO indicator.

segments.title_en: Daily fights and what restorative practice means
segments.title_ur: روز کے جھگڑے اور بحالی والا طریقہ کیا ہے
segments.summary_en: A new teacher is tired of scolding over pencil and playground fights; a colleague explains restorative practice: instead of punishment, children reflect on mistakes and understand others' feelings.

segments.title_en: Restorative circles
segments.title_ur: دائرہ نشست (ریسٹوریٹو سرکل)
segments.summary_en: Children sit in a circle; the teacher facilitates, not judges, opens with a simple question ('What made you happy today?'), every child gets a turn and others only listen; used the day after two pupils fought, who then apologised to each other.

segments.title_en: I-statements with a poster and role-play
segments.title_ur: 'مجھے محسوس ہوتا ہے' جملے: پوسٹر اور کردار نگاری
segments.summary_en: Children replace blame ('You stole my pencil') with 'I feel ... when ... because ...'; the frame is on a wall poster, the teacher points to it during fights and runs role-play scenarios ('Your friend won't let you play, what will you say?').

segments.title_en: Reflection questions after a conflict
segments.title_ur: جھگڑے کے بعد سوچنے والے سوال
segments.summary_en: After a problem is solved the teacher asks 'How did it feel when you were heard?' and 'What will you do differently next time?' so children think about their own actions.

segments.title_en: Celebrate respectful behaviour
segments.title_ur: احترام والے رویے کی تعریف
segments.summary_en: Whenever a child uses an I-statement or listens respectfully, the teacher praises it specifically in front of the class, so others copy it and fights decrease.

segments.title_en: Start tomorrow with one small circle
segments.title_ur: کل سے ایک چھوٹی دائرہ نشست سے شروع کریں
segments.summary_en: Wrap-up: no extra resources needed, only a change of approach; start with one short circle session, then introduce I-statements; sign-off.
