modules.title: Positive Reinforcement Strategies
modules.teacher_line_en: Swap 'shabash' for praise that names the behaviour, plus free rewards and class jobs
modules.teacher_line_ur: 'شاباش' کی جگہ رویے کا نام لے کر تعریف، مفت انعام اور کلاس کی ذمہ داریاں
modules.summary_en: A podcast-style conversation with a Grade 4 teacher from crowded government and low-cost schools on three positive-reinforcement strategies. Teachers hear specific praise that names the behaviour ('I liked how you patiently explained to your partner in the group discussion') instead of just 'shabash', zero-cost rewards (stickers, a smiley, 'Superstar of the day', 5 extra minutes of game time), and class roles such as homework checker, line leader, board cleaner or class librarian, plus how to tell from tracking charts and notes whether it is working.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سنیں گے کہ صرف 'شاباش' کے بجائے رویے کا نام لے کر تعریف، بغیر خرچ کے انعامات اور کلاس کی ذمہ داریاں دے کر بڑی کلاس میں اچھا رویہ کیسے بڑھائیں۔
symptoms: the only praise in the lesson is 'shabash', 'very good' or 'good boy/girl' with nothing named
teacher repeatedly scolds or threatens ('maar khao ge', 'bahar nikal do') to control behaviour
the same few children do everything; no child has a class job or role
good behaviour is never noticed out loud, only misbehaviour
modules.not_for: Teachers whose report is about questioning, explanation or subject content; this is behaviour management and gives no academic-feedback model.

segments.title_en: Intro: reinforcement beyond 'shabash'
segments.title_ur: تعارف: 'شاباش' سے آگے حوصلہ افزائی
segments.summary_en: Host and guest introductions; positive reinforcement as a structured system, not just 'shabash', and why praise, small rewards and roles help in crowded classes.

segments.title_en: Specific praise that names the behaviour
segments.title_ur: رویے کا نام لے کر مخصوص تعریف
segments.summary_en: Instead of 'shabash', name exactly what was good ('I liked how you patiently explained to your partner'), and align praise with class rules such as respect and cooperation.

segments.title_en: Zero-cost rewards
segments.title_ur: بغیر خرچ کے انعامات
segments.summary_en: Stickers, a smiley, a 'Superstar of the day' note, a clap, 5 extra minutes of game time, or 'Captain for a day' for reaching a weekly target.

segments.title_en: Class jobs as reinforcement
segments.title_ur: کلاس کی ذمہ داریاں بطور حوصلہ افزائی
segments.summary_en: Give responsibility as a reward: 'Homework checker of the week', line leader, board cleaner, class librarian; roles build trust and accountability at no cost.

segments.title_en: Is it working? Then recap
segments.title_ur: کیا یہ کام کر رہا ہے؟ پھر خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Check with behaviour charts, quick reflection questions and observation notes; rotate rewards when interest drops; recap of the three strategies.

modules.title: کہانی کا عنوان: نور سکول میں پڑھنے کا انقلاب
modules.teacher_line_en: How one school built a love of reading together: reading corners and story sessions
modules.teacher_line_ur: ایک اسکول نے مل کر پڑھنے کا شوق کیسے پیدا کیا: ریڈنگ کارنر اور کہانی سیشن
modules.summary_en: A narrated story on illustrated slides: a facilitator tells a staff meeting how a nearby school gathered evidence that children found textbooks boring, set up a reading corner in every class and 10 minutes of free reading a week, and saw interest rise. It lists school-wide ideas (reading corners, a weekly storytelling session run as I do / we do / you do, pair reading, reading competitions, daily diaries), tracking with checklists, surveys and teacher logs, and ends with teachers writing a one-month action plan.
modules.summary_ur: یہ ایک کہانی ہے کہ پورا اسکول ریڈنگ کارنر، کہانی سنانے اور نگرانی جیسی مشترکہ حکمت عملی سے بچوں میں پڑھنے کا شوق کیسے پیدا کر سکتا ہے۔
symptoms: children read only the textbook; no story or picture books appear in the lesson
no time is given for children to choose and read on their own
modules.not_for: Classroom teachers looking for a move for tomorrow's period; this is a school-wide reading programme told as a story.

segments.title_en: Staff meeting: a school-wide reading goal
segments.title_ur: اسٹاف میٹنگ: پورے اسکول کا پڑھنے کا ہدف
segments.summary_en: Sets the scene: a facilitator tells teachers they will design and implement a school-wide strategy tied to literacy outcomes.

segments.title_en: The story: evidence, need, reading corners
segments.title_ur: کہانی: شواہد، ضرورت، ریڈنگ کارنر
segments.summary_en: A nearby school gathers evidence that children are bored by textbooks, decides with the principal on a reading corner in every class and 10 minutes of free reading a week, and sees interest rise.

segments.title_en: Reading corners, storytelling, pair reading, diaries
segments.title_ur: ریڈنگ کارنر، کہانی سنانا، جوڑیوں میں پڑھنا، ڈائری
segments.summary_en: Lists strategies: an Urdu/English reading corner with picture labels, a weekly dramatic story session run as I do / we do / you do, pair reading, reading competitions and wall displays, and a daily diary.

segments.title_en: Monitor with checklists, surveys and logs
segments.title_ur: چیک لسٹ، سروے اور لاگ سے نگرانی
segments.summary_en: Tracks the strategy with checklists, student surveys and teacher logs (e.g. participation up from 40% to 65%) and changes it if results are slow.

segments.title_en: Reflection sheets and a one-month action plan
segments.title_ur: غور و فکر اور ایک ماہ کا منصوبہ
segments.summary_en: Teachers discuss with a partner what interests their students and which strategy is easiest to start, then each writes an action plan for next month.

segments.title_en: Closing message
segments.title_ur: اختتامی پیغام
segments.summary_en: The facilitator's closing words on whole-school unity and the narrator's moral of the story.

modules.title: Project Based Learning
modules.teacher_line_en: Want children to research, not just copy? Start a small project from a real question
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے صرف نقل نہیں، خود تحقیق کریں؟ ایک حقیقی سوال سے چھوٹا پراجیکٹ شروع کریں
modules.summary_en: Two teachers talk through project-based learning: students ask questions, research and share findings while the teacher facilitates. Examples are a Grade 4 science project ('Where does our water come from, and is it safe?': small-group interviews, a filter model, presentations) and a maths classroom shop with paper money; five steps follow (start with a real question, plan steps with students, group work, collect information from home and community, end with 'What did you learn? What was hard? What would you do better?'). The last part is about mentoring colleagues: start small, a staff sharing circle and an idea wall.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں دو اساتذہ کی گفتگو سے آپ دیکھیں گے کہ حقیقی سوال سے پراجیکٹ شروع کر کے بچوں سے گروپ میں تحقیق، پیشکش اور آخر میں غور و فکر کیسے کروائیں۔
symptoms: every task is a textbook exercise; nothing links to children's own area or life
children never collect information, interview or observe outside the book
teacher decides all steps; children never plan or choose how to present
no 'what did you learn / what was hard' reflection at the end of an activity
modules.not_for: Teachers who first need basic lesson structure or classroom control; the last third is about mentoring colleagues, not classroom practice.

segments.title_en: What project-based learning is
segments.title_ur: پراجیکٹ پر مبنی تدریس کیا ہے
segments.summary_en: Two teachers discuss a PBL training: students ask questions, research and share findings, the teacher becomes a facilitator; framed around mentoring peer teachers.

segments.title_en: Two projects: safe water (Grade 4 science) and a classroom shop
segments.title_ur: دو پراجیکٹ: صاف پانی اور کلاس کی دکان
segments.summary_en: Children check where their area's water comes from and whether it is safe, interview people, build a filter model in small groups and present; in maths they run a pretend shop with paper money to practise adding, subtracting and money values.

segments.title_en: Five steps: real question, plan together, groups, research, reflect
segments.title_ur: پانچ قدم: حقیقی سوال، مل کر منصوبہ، گروپ، تحقیق، غور و فکر
segments.summary_en: Start with a real question ('How can we keep our classroom clean?'), plan the steps with students, work in small groups, collect pictures, notes or interviews from home and community, and end by asking what they learned, what was hard and what to improve.
segments.recommendable_reason: panel_veto: teacher_cant_act: a five-step project over days, not a single-period move (ped-review live review, board 20261020T194756_ped-review_spec.md; appended by eng-engine on lead-review 19:56Z item 4)

segments.title_en: Mentoring colleagues: start small, sharing circle, idea wall
segments.title_ur: ساتھی اساتذہ کی رہنمائی: چھوٹا آغاز، شیئرنگ سرکل، آئیڈیا وال
segments.summary_en: Handling colleagues' worries (time, discipline): a staff-meeting sharing circle, starting with a classroom garden project, and a PBL idea wall in the staff room.

modules.title: Designing Interdisciplinary Lessons through Project-Based Learning
modules.teacher_line_en: Plan one 'Healthy lunch' project that joins science, maths and language, with group roles
modules.teacher_line_ur: 'صحت مند لنچ' جیسا ایک پروجیکٹ جو سائنس، ریاضی اور زبان کو جوڑے، گروپ کرداروں کے ساتھ
modules.summary_en: A presenter explains interdisciplinary project-based learning for Grades 4-5 with a classroom garden project (science: how plants grow; maths: measure height and temperature; language: write observations; art: labels and posters). Teachers get five planning steps (pick a real-life theme such as 'Healthy lunch' or 'Saving water at home', map each subject's learning, plan hands-on tasks, act as a guide, end with reflection and presentations) and six classroom tools: a question wall, group roles (leader, recorder, researcher, presenter), a plan-do-create-present-reflect board, low-cost materials, quick group check-ins and a reflection journal.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ 'صحت مند لنچ' جیسے ایک حقیقی موضوع پر سائنس، ریاضی اور زبان کو جوڑ کر پروجیکٹ کیسے بنائیں اور گروپ کے کردار، سوالوں کی دیوار اور سوچ بچار کی ڈائری کیسے استعمال کریں۔
symptoms: every subject is taught separately from the textbook with no link to the children's daily life
group work has no roles, so one child does the task while others watch
children never write or post their own questions
no reflection at the end of a project or unit ('what did you learn, what was hard?')
modules.not_for: Teachers whose report is about a single in-period move, or early-years teachers; this is about planning a multi-day, multi-subject project.

segments.title_en: What interdisciplinary PBL is: a classroom garden
segments.title_ur: بین المضامین پروجیکٹ کیا ہے: کلاس کا باغ
segments.summary_en: Link to the earlier PBL session; one project joins subjects, e.g. a classroom garden (plant growth, measuring height and temperature, writing observations, posters); why real problems are not subject-wise.

segments.title_en: Five steps to plan a cross-subject project
segments.title_ur: مختلف مضامین کا پروجیکٹ بنانے کے پانچ قدم
segments.summary_en: Choose a real-life theme ('Clean school, green school', 'Healthy lunch'); map science, maths and language learning; plan hands-on tasks; guide rather than tell; end with 'What did you learn? What was hard? What will you do better?' and presentations.

segments.title_en: Question wall, group roles, planning board
segments.title_ur: سوالوں کی دیوار، گروپ کے کردار، منصوبہ بورڈ
segments.summary_en: A chart corner where students post their own project questions; clear roles (leader, recorder, researcher, presenter); a plan-do-create-present-reflect timeline on the board.

segments.title_en: Low-cost materials, check-ins, reflection journal
segments.title_ur: سستا سامان، گروپ سے مختصر بات، سوچ بچار ڈائری
segments.summary_en: Recycled bottles and cardboard; short check-ins where each group shares progress and gets feedback; a journal entry 'What did I learn today? How is it useful to me?'.

segments.title_en: Plan with colleagues; closing
segments.title_ur: ساتھی اساتذہ کے ساتھ منصوبہ بندی؛ اختتام
segments.summary_en: Science and English teachers can co-design a project; reminder to pick 2-3 subjects that connect in the next lesson plan; closing.

modules.title: Peer Classroom Observations
modules.teacher_line_en: Set up peer observation with a colleague: focus, facts, kind feedback
modules.teacher_line_ur: ساتھی ٹیچر کے ساتھ کلاس کا مشاہدہ: فوکس، حقائق اور مثبت رائے
modules.summary_en: A presenter explains how to design and lead peer classroom observation in a school: set a focus (questioning, group work, visuals), plan together, note facts not judgements ('asked 5 open-ended questions'), give feedback that starts with strengths and uses 'you could try…', then reflect together. Practical aids are an observation checklist, a pre-observation meeting, reciprocal observation, a reflective journal and a monthly observation calendar, illustrated by two Grade 5 teachers observing each other.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں اسکول میں اساتذہ کے ایک دوسرے کی کلاس کا مشاہدہ کرنے اور مثبت رائے دینے کا عمل بنانے اور چلانے کا طریقہ بتایا گیا ہے۔
symptoms: teacher (in a coaching conversation, not a lesson) asks how to learn from colleagues' classrooms
modules.not_for: Teachers whose report is about their own lesson; this is about organising observation and feedback between colleagues, not a classroom move.

segments.title_en: What peer observation is and why
segments.title_ur: ہم منصب مشاہدہ کیا ہے اور کیوں
segments.summary_en: Peer observation is a structured process where teachers watch each other's classes for learning and support, not judgement, focusing on methods, engagement and management.

segments.title_en: Five steps: purpose, plan, observe facts, feedback, reflect
segments.title_ur: پانچ مراحل: مقصد، منصوبہ، حقائق، رائے، غور
segments.summary_en: Set a focus, plan the visit together, note facts not judgements ('asked 5 open-ended questions'), give feedback that starts with strengths then one suggestion, and reflect together afterwards.

segments.title_en: Checklist, quiet notes, pre-meeting, positive phrasing, journal
segments.title_ur: چیک لسٹ، خاموش نوٹس، پیشگی ملاقات، مثبت الفاظ، ڈائری
segments.summary_en: Use an observation checklist, take notes quietly, agree the focus in a short pre-meeting, say 'you could try…' instead of 'you should not…', observe each other in turn and write a short reflection afterwards.

segments.title_en: Example: two Grade 5 teachers observe each other; start a calendar
segments.title_ur: مثال: گریڈ 5 کے دو اساتذہ کا باہمی مشاہدہ
segments.summary_en: One teacher sees open-ended questions raise participation in a group reading activity, the other praises a group rotation system; the video suggests a monthly peer observation calendar and closes.

modules.title: Mentoring Peers to Design Concept-Based, Activity-Driven Math Lessons
modules.teacher_line_en: Bundle 10 pencils, hunt for shapes, measure with crayons: concept before steps
modules.teacher_line_ur: 10 پنسلوں کا بنڈل، شیپ ہنٹ، پنسل سے پیمائش: پہلے تصور، پھر طریقہ
modules.summary_en: Framed as advice for mentoring colleagues, the middle of the video gives concrete early-maths moves: bundle 10 pencils to show ten ones make one ten before writing symbols, ask '2 bundles and 3 pencils, how many?', link to three 10-rupee notes, and let small groups say what the concept means. Each strand gets one activity: bottle caps or buttons for addition, a classroom shape hunt (door = rectangle, clock = circle), measuring a desk with pencils, and a favourite-fruit survey turned into a chart. The last part is about mentoring a peer (appreciate first, ask reflective questions, share resources).
modules.summary_ur: آپ پنسلوں کے بنڈل، دکان کے نوٹ، شیپ ہنٹ، پنسل سے پیمائش اور پسندیدہ پھل کے سروے جیسی سرگرمیوں سے ریاضی کا تصور پہلے سمجھانا سیکھیں گے۔
symptoms: teacher writes place-value or addition steps on the board with no objects or pictures
children recite '10 ones = 1 ten' but no bundles, sticks or counters are used
no example from money, the classroom or children's lives
children never discuss what a concept means in their own words
modules.not_for: Maths teachers of Grade 6 and above, or teachers looking for help with coaching colleagues only; the classroom activities are early-primary.

segments.title_en: Why concept-based maths, and the mentor's job
segments.title_ur: تصور پر مبنی ریاضی کیوں، اور مینٹور کا کام
segments.summary_en: Children memorise formulas without meaning; the national curriculum asks for understanding, reasoning and problem solving, and a mentor's job is to help colleagues see this.

segments.title_en: Concrete first: bundles of 10 pencils, then symbols
segments.title_ur: پہلے ٹھوس چیزیں: 10 پنسلوں کا بنڈل، پھر علامت
segments.summary_en: Concept before procedure: bundle 10 pencils so children see ten ones make one ten, then write the symbols, and ask a thinking question after each step ('2 bundles and 3 pencils, how many?').

segments.title_en: Real-life money and small-group talk
segments.title_ur: روزمرہ پیسے اور گروپ میں گفتگو
segments.summary_en: Links to local life (three 10-rupee notes, how many rupees?) and lets small groups discuss what the concept means in their own words, with the teacher as facilitator.

segments.title_en: One activity per strand: caps, shape hunt, pencils, survey
segments.title_ur: ہر شعبے کی سرگرمی: ڈھکن، شیپ ہنٹ، پنسل، سروے
segments.summary_en: Bottle caps or buttons for addition and grouping, a classroom shape hunt (door, clock, window), measuring a desk with pencils or crayons, and a favourite-fruit survey made into a chart and discussed.

segments.title_en: Mentoring a peer: appreciate, ask, suggest, share
segments.title_ur: ساتھی کی رہنمائی: سراہیں، پوچھیں، مشورہ، شیئر
segments.summary_en: Mentoring steps for a colleague: appreciate effort first, ask reflective questions, give gentle suggestions, share resources, and three reflection questions about the lesson.

modules.title: Facilitating the Correction of Deep Misconceptions in Mathematics
modules.teacher_line_en: Pupils say 1/8 is bigger than 1/4? Fix it with paper folding and a number line
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے کہتے ہیں 1/8 بڑا ہے 1/4 سے؟ کاغذ موڑ کر اور نمبر لائن سے درست کریں
modules.summary_en: A narrated guide for maths facilitators on running a session where teachers surface and fix pupils' deep misconceptions: '1/8 is bigger than 1/4', '0.25 is bigger than 0.5', 'every four-sided shape is a rectangle'. Teachers learn to ask 'why do your students think that?', then fix each idea with folding one paper into 4 and another into 8, marking 0.25 and 0.5 on a 0–1 number line, and comparing real objects (chalk box, notebook, window), and to ask pupils 'why do you think 1/8 is bigger?'.
modules.summary_ur: یہ ویڈیو ٹرینرز کے لیے ہے کہ اساتذہ کے سیشن میں کسر، اعشاریہ اور جیومیٹری کی عام غلط فہمیاں کیسے سامنے لائیں اور کاغذ موڑنے، نمبر لائن اور اصل چیزوں سے کیسے درست کروائیں۔
symptoms: teacher marks an answer like '1/8 is bigger' wrong and moves on without asking why
fractions or decimals taught only with symbols on the board; no folding, objects or number line
no 'why do you think that?' after a wrong answer
teacher repeats the rule ('bigger denominator, smaller part') louder when pupils stay confused
modules.not_for: Classroom teachers looking for a move to try in their own next period; it is a train-the-trainer guide for maths facilitators.

segments.title_en: Why misconceptions matter, and the facilitator's role
segments.title_ur: غلط فہمیاں کیوں اہم ہیں اور فیسلیٹیٹر کا کردار
segments.summary_en: Introduces the session for facilitators; a teacher reports pupils saying 1/8 is bigger than 1/4 and the facilitator asks 'why do students think that? what is their reasoning?'.

segments.title_en: Surfacing misconceptions: reflection questions and shared cases
segments.title_ur: غلط فہمیاں سامنے لانا: سوالات اور تجربات
segments.summary_en: Facilitator asks teachers where pupils struggle in fractions and decimals, then small groups share cases like '0.5 is smaller than 0.25' and what alternate example they used.

segments.title_en: Paper folding to show 1/4 is bigger than 1/8
segments.title_ur: کاغذ موڑ کر دکھائیں کہ 1/4 بڑا ہے 1/8 سے
segments.summary_en: Pupils fold one paper into 4 equal parts and another into 8 and are asked 'which part looks bigger?', so they see for themselves that 1/4 is bigger than 1/8.

segments.title_en: Number line for decimals; real objects for shapes
segments.title_ur: اعشاریہ کے لیے نمبر لائن، شکلوں کے لیے اصل چیزیں
segments.summary_en: Draw a 0–1 number line, mark 0.25 and 0.5, and discuss why pupils think 0.25 is bigger (value depends on position, not the digit); use chalk boxes, notebooks and windows to prove which four-sided shapes are rectangles or squares.

segments.title_en: Ask pupils why they think it
segments.title_ur: بچوں سے پوچھیں کہ وہ ایسا کیوں سوچتے ہیں
segments.summary_en: Questioning as the main tool to find misconceptions: ask 'why do you think 1/8 is bigger than 1/4?' to reach the pupil's reasoning.

segments.title_en: Session reflection and close
segments.title_ur: سیشن کا اختتام اور غور و فکر
segments.summary_en: Teachers reflect on which misconception they learned to spot and which strategy worked; every wrong answer is a window into pupils' thinking. Sign-off.

modules.title: Designing Effective Math Trainings Using CPA, Math Discourse, and Formative Assessment
modules.teacher_line_en: For trainers: build a maths session on CPA, maths talk and exit tickets
modules.teacher_line_ur: ٹرینرز کے لیے: ٹھوس-تصویری-علامتی، ریاضی گفتگو اور ایگزٹ ٹکٹ پر تربیتی سیشن
modules.summary_en: Addressed to maths trainers: how to design a teacher-training session in three segments, CPA (teachers handle coins, bottle caps or blocks, draw it, then write it in symbols), maths discourse (open questions like 'How do you know 1/2 and 2/4 are the same?', pair talk, 'I think... because...' and 'I agree/disagree because...' starters) and formative assessment (exit tickets, observation checklist, peer feedback), each ending with a reflection on what teachers will apply.
modules.summary_ur: یہ ویڈیو ٹرینرز کے لیے ہے کہ اساتذہ کی ریاضی تربیت کو ٹھوس سے تصویری اور علامتی مرحلے، ریاضی پر گفتگو اور جاری جانچ کے گرد کیسے ترتیب دیں۔
symptoms: children recite steps and formulas but cannot say why
no objects or drawings before symbols in a maths lesson
no student is asked 'how do you know?' in a maths lesson
modules.not_for: Classroom teachers looking for something to try tomorrow; it is a train-the-trainer design guide for maths coaches.

segments.title_en: The trainer's role and three focus areas
segments.title_ur: ٹرینر کا کردار اور تین بنیادی نکات
segments.summary_en: Children memorise steps without understanding; trainers should design activity-based sessions on three elements: CPA, maths discourse and formative assessment, aligned with the national curriculum.

segments.title_en: Demonstrating CPA in a training session
segments.title_ur: تربیت میں ٹھوس-تصویری-علامتی طریقہ
segments.summary_en: Teachers use real objects (rupees, coins, bottle caps, blocks), then represent the experience in a diagram, then in numbers and symbols, and reflect on which stage engaged students most.

segments.title_en: Building maths discourse
segments.title_ur: ریاضی پر گفتگو کو فروغ دینا
segments.summary_en: Practise open questions ('How do you know 1/2 and 2/4 are the same?'), pair talk or group discussion, and sentence starters 'I think... because...' and 'I agree/disagree because...'; the teacher becomes listener and guide.

segments.title_en: Formative assessment tools and the session structure
segments.title_ur: جاری جانچ کے طریقے اور سیشن کی ترتیب
segments.summary_en: Exit tickets ('What did I learn today?'), an observation checklist of who needs support, and peer feedback; then the three-segment session structure with trainer modelling, group practice and a reflection at the end of each segment.

segments.title_en: Reflection and closure for trainers
segments.title_ur: ٹرینرز کے لیے غور و فکر اور اختتام
segments.summary_en: Questions for the trainer (which segment to start with, how to ensure teachers apply it) and a closing message; sign-off.

modules.title: Modeling Facilitation of Math Clubs, Fairs, and Circles to Build a Math Culture
modules.teacher_line_en: Run a maths circle: pose one challenge, then ask 'Why do you think so? Who disagrees?'
modules.teacher_line_ur: ریاضی کا دائرہ: ایک چیلنج دیں، پھر پوچھیں 'آپ کو ایسا کیوں لگتا ہے؟ کون متفق نہیں؟'
modules.summary_en: A presenter describes three ways to build a maths culture: a weekly maths club of 8-10 students with rotating presenter/recorder roles, a school maths fair with parents invited, and in-class maths circles. The classroom part shows how to run a maths circle: seat children in a circle, pose a challenge ('If we want to double a rectangle's area, do we have to double every side?'), let students share ideas while the teacher only asks 'Why do you think so? Does anyone agree or disagree?', and close with 'What did we learn? Which reasoning changed your thinking?'.
modules.summary_ur: آپ دیکھیں گے کہ ریاضی کے دائرے میں ایک سوچنے والا سوال کیسے رکھیں اور خود جواب دینے کے بجائے 'آپ کو ایسا کیوں لگتا ہے؟ کون متفق ہے؟' پوچھ کر بچوں کو دلیل دینے دیں۔
symptoms: maths lesson where the teacher works every sum on the board and children only copy answers
teacher says 'galat' and gives the right answer instead of asking how the child got theirs
no 'why do you think so?' or 'who agrees?' anywhere in a maths lesson
every maths question has one number answer read off the board
modules.not_for: Teachers of non-maths lessons; the club and fair chapters are school-level events, so send only the maths-circle chapters to a teacher whose report is about their own class.

segments.title_en: Intro: what a maths culture is
segments.title_ur: تعارف: ریاضی کا ماحول کیا ہے
segments.summary_en: Greeting; the curriculum goal of interest, curiosity and confidence in maths; maths culture means children enjoy rather than fear maths.

segments.title_en: Running a weekly maths club
segments.title_ur: ہفتہ وار ریاضی کلب چلانا
segments.summary_en: Start with 8-10 students and a short weekly activity; themes such as Maths and Sports or Rupees and Budgeting; rotating presenter and recorder; small projects like a class survey.

segments.title_en: Organising a school maths fair
segments.title_ur: اسکول میں ریاضی میلہ
segments.summary_en: Topics such as Fractions in Daily Life or Geometry in Art; help students explain projects simply; charts and local materials; invite parents.

segments.title_en: Maths circle: seat in a circle, pose a challenge
segments.title_ur: ریاضی کا دائرہ: دائرے میں بٹھائیں، چیلنج دیں
segments.summary_en: Children sit in a circle so all can see and speak; open with 'If we double a rectangle's area, must every side double?' to spark reasoning.

segments.title_en: Facilitate discussion, not answers
segments.title_ur: جواب نہیں، بحث کی رہنمائی
segments.summary_en: Let students share ideas, ask 'Why do you think so? Does anyone agree or disagree?', guide without judging, then reflect together: 'What did we learn? Which reasoning changed your thinking?'.

segments.title_en: Reflection questions and closing
segments.title_ur: سوچ بچار کے سوال اور اختتام
segments.summary_en: Questions for the teacher: what first step will you take, and which format (club, fair, circle) suits your students; closing.

modules.title: Integrating the Four Pillars of Literacy: Phonics, Fluency, Comprehension, and Vocabulary
modules.teacher_line_en: One quick routine each for phonics, fluency, comprehension and vocabulary in Grade 2
modules.teacher_line_ur: دوسری جماعت کے لیے فونکس، روانی، فہم اور الفاظ کی ایک ایک آسان سرگرمی
modules.summary_en: In a two-person English talk show, a literacy trainer gives one short routine for each pillar of early reading: a 'sound of the day' with blending and picture sorting by first sound (phonics), model reading, echo reading, readers' theatre and timed reading (fluency), predict before / question during / retell after plus think-pair-share (comprehension), and a word wall, synonym-antonym hunt and context clues (vocabulary). It closes with a Grade 2 'animals around us' lesson that uses all four in one period, framed as two teachers coaching each other.
modules.summary_ur: آپ ابتدائی جماعتوں میں فونکس، روانی سے پڑھنے، فہم اور ذخیرۂ الفاظ کی ایک ایک آسان سرگرمی دیکھیں گے اور یہ کہ چاروں کو ایک ہی سبق میں کیسے جوڑیں۔
symptoms: English reading lesson where students only repeat the text after the teacher, with no sound-by-sound blending
teacher reads the passage and moves straight to book exercises with no prediction or 'why' question about the story
new words are given only as Urdu meanings to copy, never used in other sentences or guessed from context
no student retells the story in their own words
modules.not_for: Maths, science or Grade 6+ teachers; it is about early English reading, has no classroom footage, and is framed around peer coaching.

segments.title_en: Intro: peer coaching and the four pillars of literacy
segments.title_ur: تعارف: ہم منصب کوچنگ اور خواندگی کے چار ستون
segments.summary_en: Show opening, guest introduction, peer coaching as a way to grow, and one-line definitions of phonics, fluency, comprehension and vocabulary.

segments.title_en: Phonics: sound of the day, blending, sorting games
segments.title_ur: فونکس: آج کی آواز، آوازیں جوڑنا، چھانٹی کے کھیل
segments.summary_en: Introduce one sound with examples (chair, cheese, chicken), say sounds slowly then blend them into a word, and have students sort pictures or words by beginning sound.

segments.title_en: Fluency: model reading, echo reading, readers' theatre
segments.title_ur: روانی: نمونے کی قراءت، دہرائی، کہانی کا کردار ادا کرنا
segments.summary_en: The teacher reads a short text aloud with good speed and tone, students echo it, act out a short story, and timed reading tracks progress over a week.

segments.title_en: Comprehension: predict, question, retell, think-pair-share
segments.title_ur: فہم: اندازہ، سوال، دوبارہ سنانا، سوچو جوڑی بناؤ بتاؤ
segments.summary_en: Before reading ask 'what do you think the story will be about?', during reading ask 'why did the boy go to the market?', after reading students retell in their own words and discuss in pairs before answering.

segments.title_en: Vocabulary: word wall, synonym hunt, context clues
segments.title_ur: ذخیرۂ الفاظ: ورڈ وال، مترادف اور متضاد، سیاق سے معنی
segments.summary_en: A chart-paper word wall with pictures and one word used weekly in different sentences, a synonym-antonym hunt, and guessing meanings from how a word is used.

segments.title_en: One Grade 2 lesson that uses all four
segments.title_ur: دوسری جماعت کا ایک سبق جس میں چاروں شامل ہوں
segments.summary_en: An 'animals around us' lesson: review the 'a' sound (cat, bat, rabbit), echo a poem with expression, ask 'which animals can climb?', and build a word web for 'lion'.

segments.title_en: Reflection questions and close
segments.title_ur: غوروفکر کے سوالات اور اختتام
segments.summary_en: Questions for teachers about using all four skills and sharing plans with peers, peer coaching as a 10-minute chat, and the show's sign-off.

modules.title: Teaching Grammar with Purpose: Linking Form, Function, and Meaning
modules.teacher_line_en: Teach 'is running' vs 'runs' from a picture, not a rule
modules.teacher_line_ur: گرامر اصول سے نہیں، تصویر اور مثال سے سکھائیں: is running بمقابلہ runs
modules.summary_en: A presenter shows how to teach the present continuous through structure, function and meaning instead of a rule: open with a picture ('Look, the boy is running. Is he running now or yesterday?'), put 'He runs every day' next to 'He is running now' and ask what students notice, have children say what they are doing right now ('I'm writing', 'No, you are talking'), and contrast is + verb-ing (happening now) with verb + s (habit). A 'grammar detective' passage has learners underline -ing verbs and say whether each action is now, yesterday or every day.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں انگریزی گرامر (present continuous) کو اصول رٹانے کے بجائے تصویر، موازنہ اور بچوں کی اپنی بات چیت کے ذریعے ساخت، کام اور معنی سے جوڑ کر سکھانا دکھایا گیا ہے۔
symptoms: English grammar lesson starts by writing a rule or formula ('is/am/are + ing') on the board
children copy tense tables or chant verb forms with no sentence about real situations
teacher never asks students what they notice about two sentences
no student produces a sentence of their own using the tense
modules.not_for: Maths, science or Urdu teachers, and teachers of early phonics; parts of the video address teacher-leaders coaching peers.

segments.title_en: Session goals: grammar for communication (intro)
segments.title_ur: مقصد: بات چیت کے لیے گرامر (تعارف)
segments.summary_en: Greeting and goals: teach grammar as a tool for meaningful communication, and coach peers to do the same in line with national learning outcomes.

segments.title_en: Structure, function and meaning of 'He is playing'
segments.title_ur: جاری فعل والے جملے کی ساخت، کام اور معنی
segments.summary_en: Every grammar point has a structure (word pattern), a function (what it does: an action happening now) and a meaning (the message); linking the three makes grammar a tool for expression.

segments.title_en: Start with a picture, then 'what do you notice?'
segments.title_ur: تصویر سے آغاز، پھر پوچھیں: آپ نے کیا دیکھا؟
segments.summary_en: Open with a picture of a boy running and ask if he is running now or yesterday before naming 'is + verb-ing'; then write 'He runs every day' / 'He is running now' and ask students what they notice (habit vs action in progress).

segments.title_en: Children say what they are doing right now
segments.title_ur: بچے بتائیں وہ ابھی کیا کر رہے ہیں
segments.summary_en: Students say what they are doing ('I'm writing', 'I'm listening') and classmates respond ('No, you are talking'); teachers can rehearse it as a role-play first.

segments.title_en: Everyday examples: is + verb-ing vs verb + s
segments.title_ur: روزمرہ مثالیں: ابھی ہونے والا کام بمقابلہ عادت
segments.summary_en: 'I'm reading' = happening at this moment; 'He plays football every day' = routine; each is given with its structure, function and meaning so the rule is understood rather than memorised.

segments.title_en: Grammar detective: find the -ing verbs in a passage
segments.title_ur: گرامر جاسوس: عبارت میں -ing والے افعال ڈھونڈیں
segments.summary_en: Read a short passage, underline verbs ending in -ing and ask whether each action happens now, yesterday or every day. (The narration says 'are talking' but the passage reads 'They talk'.)

segments.title_en: Reflection and peer coaching (close)
segments.title_ur: غور و فکر اور ساتھی کوچنگ (اختتام)
segments.summary_en: Reflection questions for teachers, pairing up to design a grammar mini-lesson and give each other feedback, and a closing message.

modules.title: Developing Grade-Appropriate Reading and Writing Materials for the English Classroom
modules.teacher_line_en: Turn one textbook passage into who/why/what-do-you-think questions plus a writing task
modules.teacher_line_ur: ایک سبق سے کون/کیوں/آپ کیا سوچتے ہیں والے سوال اور لکھنے کا کام بنائیں
modules.summary_en: A trainer shows how to check and build English reading, writing and grammar tasks for the right grade: three test questions (familiar topic? words easy enough to read alone? linked to what they know?), passage examples at two levels ('Noman has a small cat' vs a longer descriptive sentence), and questions that climb from literal (who, what, where) to inferential (why, how) to critical (what do you think, what could happen next). It works one Grade 4 passage ('Fatma wakes up early...') into literal, inferential and personal questions, a 5-sentence writing prompt about the child's own morning, and a find-the-verbs grammar task.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ انگریزی کے پڑھنے، لکھنے اور گرامر کے کام کو بچوں کی جماعت کے مطابق کیسے جانچیں، اور ایک ہی سبق سے آسان سے مشکل سوال، لکھنے کا کام اور گرامر کا کام کیسے بنائیں۔
symptoms: every comprehension question after a reading is 'who' or 'what' with an answer copied from the text
no 'why' or 'what do you think' question about the passage
writing task is unrelated to the passage just read
grammar is taught as a rule and a fill-in-the-blank with no sentence of the children's own
modules.not_for: Teachers of maths, science or Urdu; and English teachers whose need is in-the-moment questioning or feedback rather than preparing tasks.

segments.title_en: Session goals: level-appropriate English materials
segments.title_ur: سیشن کے مقاصد: جماعت کے مطابق انگریزی مواد
segments.summary_en: Introduces the session and its objectives: review and adapt reading, writing and grammar materials for grade level, and help peers do the same.

segments.title_en: Three questions to test if material fits the grade
segments.title_ur: مواد جماعت کے مطابق ہے؟ تین سوال
segments.summary_en: Defines level-appropriate and gives three checks (familiar topic, words children can read alone, linked to prior learning), with what Grades 2, 5 and 8 can handle.

segments.title_en: Passages: familiar themes, right language, climbing questions
segments.title_ur: سبق: مانوس موضوع، مناسب زبان، بتدریج سوال
segments.summary_en: Choose familiar themes, match sentence length to the grade ('Noman has a small cat' vs a longer sentence), and ask literal, then inferential (why, how), then critical (what do you think, what could happen next) questions.

segments.title_en: Writing prompts for each level
segments.title_ur: ہر جماعت کے لیے لکھنے کا کام
segments.summary_en: Picture-guided prompts for Grades 1-3 ('write 3 sentences about what the boy is doing'), a descriptive paragraph for 4-6, an opinion with reasons for 7-8, and a check that instructions are short, real and purposeful.

segments.title_en: Grammar in use: sort, correct, edit
segments.title_ur: استعمال میں گرامر: میچ، درستی، تدوین
segments.summary_en: Matching nouns with pictures for lower grades, sentence correction for middle grades, editing a paragraph with errors for higher grades, always ending in children's own meaningful sentences.

segments.title_en: Worked example: one passage to questions, writing and grammar
segments.title_ur: مثال: ایک سبق سے سوال، تحریر اور گرامر
segments.summary_en: Checks a Grade 4 passage about Fatma's morning for fit, then builds literal, inferential and personal questions, a 'write 5 sentences about your morning' prompt and an underline-the-verbs task.

segments.title_en: Reflection and pair review; close
segments.title_ur: غور و فکر اور جوڑیوں میں جائزہ
segments.summary_en: Reflection questions on one's own materials and a suggestion that teachers review a textbook passage in pairs, then the closing message.

modules.title: تحریر کی درستی اور روانی – ابتدائی اردو کی مؤثر تربیت
modules.teacher_line_en: Find the reason behind a child's Urdu writing error, then fix it together
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچے کی اردو لکھائی کی غلطی کی وجہ سمجھیں اور مل کر درست کریں
modules.summary_en: A narrated guide for coaches of new Urdu teachers on early writing. It shows sorting errors in a sample of pupil writing (sound, harakat or thinking error) and feedback such as 'you wrote this right, just one harakat is missing, let us add it together', a 'match the harakat' drill on ب with colour-coded zabar/zer/pesh, and 'speak first, then write' on 'my school' with guiding questions plus building a sentence from given words. Each step ends with how the coach gives the new teacher feedback.
modules.summary_ur: یہ ویڈیو کوچز کے لیے ہے کہ نئے اردو اساتذہ کو بچوں کی لکھائی کی غلطیوں کا تجزیہ، حرکات کی مشق اور بول کر پھر لکھنے کے ذریعے جملے کا بہاؤ سکھانے میں کیسے مدد دیں۔
symptoms: teacher corrects copy-work by saying 'galat' or rewriting the word, with no reason given
harakat (zabar/zer/pesh) taught only by rote repetition
children asked to write a sentence or paragraph with no talk or guiding questions first
no feedback that names what the child wrote correctly
modules.not_for: Classroom teachers looking for a move to try in their own next period; it is addressed to coaches mentoring new Urdu teachers.

segments.title_en: Coaching new teachers on early Urdu writing
segments.title_ur: نئے اساتذہ کی اردو لکھائی پر کوچنگ
segments.summary_en: Introduces the coach's role: review plans, prepare new teachers and give feedback on error analysis, harakat and sentence flow.

segments.title_en: Writing error analysis and kind, specific feedback
segments.title_ur: لکھائی کی غلطیوں کا تجزیہ اور واضح فیڈبیک
segments.summary_en: Show a sample of pupil writing, ask 'is this a sound, harakat or thinking error?', write down the cause, then model feedback: 'you wrote this right, just one harakat is missing, let us add it together'.

segments.title_en: Teaching harakat: 'match the harakat' drill
segments.title_ur: حرکات سکھانا: حرکت ملاؤ کی مشق
segments.summary_en: Write ب and ask which harakat makes ba, bi or bu; a 5-minute harakat drill at the start of each lesson; colour-code zabar, zer and pesh or use flash cards.

segments.title_en: Sentence flow: speak first, then write
segments.title_ur: جملے کا بہاؤ: پہلے بولیں، پھر لکھیں
segments.summary_en: On the topic 'my school' the teacher asks guiding questions ('what is your school like? what do you like most?') before children write; then children build a sentence from given words.

segments.title_en: Coaching reflection and follow-up
segments.title_ur: کوچنگ کے بعد غور و فکر
segments.summary_en: The coach asks the new teacher whether they analysed errors or only corrected them, how engaging the harakat drill was, and asks them to plan the next class.

segments.title_en: Closing encouragement
segments.title_ur: اختتام اور حوصلہ افزائی
segments.summary_en: Recap of the three strategies and encouragement for coaches.

modules.title: لفلاح سکول میں اردو کا نیا سفر
modules.teacher_line_en: For school leaders: run an Urdu week, story circles and a calligraphy drive
modules.teacher_line_ur: اسکول قیادت کے لیے: اردو ہفتہ، کہانی نشستیں اور خوش خطی مہم کیسے چلائیں
modules.summary_en: A narrated Urdu slide story about a school-wide Urdu campaign led by a principal and a teacher committee: an Urdu language week with a word wall of favourite words brought from home, 'my word, my story' plays, story circles where small groups build stories around local characters and end with reflection questions, a calligraphy campaign with class display boards, writing buddies and Friday thank-you notes, and an evidence-based review meeting. Framed throughout as a lesson in leadership and team mobilisation, ending with planning questions for a school committee.
modules.summary_ur: یہ ویڈیو اسکول کی سطح پر اردو کے فروغ کی مہم (لفظوں کی دیوار، کہانی نشستیں، خوش خطی مہم) کو قیادت اور ٹیم سازی کی مثال کے طور پر دکھاتی ہے۔
symptoms: children hesitate to speak Urdu in class and answer in single words
Urdu period is only reading aloud and copying, no storytelling or performance
teacher never asks students what new Urdu word they learned
modules.not_for: Classroom teachers looking for a move to try in their next period; it is about leading a school-wide campaign and team, not one lesson.

segments.title_en: A principal shares a vision for Urdu
segments.title_ur: پرنسپل اردو کے لیے مشترکہ وژن پیش کرتی ہیں
segments.summary_en: In the staff room the principal announces three initiatives (Urdu language week, story sessions, handwriting drive); the narrator frames this as a shared vision, the first step of leadership.

segments.title_en: Urdu language week: word wall and 'my word, my story'
segments.title_ur: اردو ہفتہ: لفظوں کی دیوار اور 'میرا لفظ، میری کہانی'
segments.summary_en: A teacher committee involves teachers, students and parents; each child brings a favourite Urdu word with its meaning and a sentence for a word wall, then builds short stories or plays from them, with teachers modelling first using idioms and proverbs.

segments.title_en: Story circles with local characters and reflection questions
segments.title_ur: مقامی کرداروں کے ساتھ کہانی نشستیں اور غور و فکر کے سوال
segments.summary_en: Small groups pick a local character (the tailor, grandmother), present their story as a play, poem or picture story, and after each story the teacher runs a short reflection circle ('What did you like most? What new Urdu word did you learn today?').

segments.title_en: Calligraphy campaign and writing buddies
segments.title_ur: خوش خطی مہم اور قلمی دوست
segments.summary_en: Classes display favourite verses in good handwriting with a badge competition for the best board, pair a strong writer with one who needs help, and write Friday thank-you notes in Urdu.

segments.title_en: Review meeting with evidence
segments.title_ur: شواہد کی بنیاد پر جائزہ اجلاس
segments.summary_en: After two weeks the committee reviews checklists, work samples and photos and decides to continue weekly story sessions; framed as evidence-based programme review.

segments.title_en: Celebration and planning questions for your school
segments.title_ur: اختتامی تقریب اور اپنے اسکول کے لیے سوالات
segments.summary_en: The language week ends with a festival for parents; the principal's closing speech, then a training activity: what does your school need, what would a committee do first, how would you judge success.

modules.title: The Art of Assessment: Designing and Implementing Effective Rubrics
modules.teacher_line_en: Marking feels random? Set criteria first, then build a 4-level rubric students understand
modules.teacher_line_ur: نمبر دینا بے ترتیب لگتا ہے؟ پہلے معیار طے کریں اور چار درجوں کا آسان روبرک بنائیں
modules.summary_en: In an Urdu training podcast a teacher trainer walks through designing an assessment: start from a written learning outcome ('students will be able to explain evaporation') and ask which task would show it, pick formative / summative / performance tasks to match, and decide the criteria before the task (writing: content, organisation, grammar, vocabulary). The teacher then learns to build a four-level rubric (excellent, good, developing, beginning) with observable, positive descriptors so feedback tells each student where to improve.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ سبق کے مقصد سے شروع کر کے جانچ کیسے بنائیں، معیار پہلے طے کریں، اور چار درجوں والا روبرک بنائیں تاکہ بچوں کو پتا چلے کہاں بہتری چاہیے۔
symptoms: teacher sets a writing or project task without saying what it will be judged on
feedback on work is only 'good', 'theek hai' or a mark, with no named criterion
students ask 'mere number kyun kam aaye?' and the teacher gives no criterion-based reason
the task given does not match the lesson's stated objective
modules.not_for: Teachers who need help with in-the-moment questioning or checks; it is a planning talk about rubrics, partly framed as running a workshop for colleagues.

segments.title_en: Intro: assessment that improves learning
segments.title_ur: تعارف: ایسی جانچ جو سیکھنے کو بہتر بنائے
segments.summary_en: Podcast opening, guest introduction, and the claim that a well-designed assessment is an engine of learning, not only a source of marks.

segments.title_en: Start from the learning outcome, then pick the task
segments.title_ur: سیکھنے کے مقصد سے شروع کریں، پھر کام چنیں
segments.summary_en: Write one outcome ('students will be able to explain the process of evaporation') and ask which task would show it was learned; design starts from the objective, not the task.

segments.title_en: Formative, summative and performance tasks
segments.title_ur: فارمیٹو، سمیٹو اور کارکردگی پر مبنی جانچ
segments.summary_en: Lists assessment types with examples (exit tickets and peer review; projects and final writing; science models and oral presentations) and says the format should match the kind of learning.

segments.title_en: Decide the criteria before the task
segments.title_ur: کام دینے سے پہلے معیار طے کریں
segments.summary_en: Instead of marking first and inventing reasons later, decide what you will measure: content, organisation, grammar, vocabulary for writing; understanding, creativity, teamwork, presentation for a science project.

segments.title_en: Build a 4-level rubric with clear descriptors
segments.title_ur: واضح وضاحتوں کے ساتھ چار درجوں کا روبرک بنائیں
segments.summary_en: Defines excellent / good / developing / beginning, writes an observable descriptor for each level of a science project, and keeps descriptors positive and measurable so feedback shows the student where to improve.

segments.title_en: Test the rubric with colleagues, recap and close
segments.title_ur: ساتھیوں کے ساتھ روبرک آزمائیں، خلاصہ اور اختتام
segments.summary_en: Try the rubric in a small class activity and review it with colleagues for fairness and simple language, then a recap of the six steps and a call to use them in staff workshops.

modules.title: Reflective Post-Observation Conversation
modules.teacher_line_en: How a mentor gives a teacher feedback after an observation, without blame
modules.teacher_line_ur: مشاہدے کے بعد مینٹور ٹیچر کو بغیر الزام کے فیڈبیک کیسے دیتا ہے
modules.summary_en: An animated role-play of a post-observation debrief between a mentor and a teacher after an English lesson on sentence types. The mentor opens with a specific positive (the 'say one sentence about your morning' starter), shares observations with 'I noticed' (children busy copying missed the explanation; 'good' was said to every answer, including wrong ones), asks reflective questions, and suggests I do / we do / you do, a sentence-card sorting game and asking 'why do you think this is an exclamatory sentence?'.
modules.summary_ur: یہ ایک مینٹور اور ٹیچر کی سبق کے مشاہدے کے بعد کی گفتگو ہے، جس میں مثبت بات سے آغاز، مخصوص مشاہدہ اور سوچنے والے سوالوں سے فیڈبیک دینا دکھایا گیا ہے۔
symptoms: teacher says 'good' to every answer, including wrong ones
children copy from the board while the teacher is still explaining
modules.not_for: Classroom teachers looking for a move to use with their own students; this models how a mentor debriefs another teacher.

segments.title_en: Open the debrief with a specific positive
segments.title_ur: مثبت اور مخصوص بات سے گفتگو کا آغاز
segments.summary_en: The mentor praises the 'say one sentence about your morning' starter and the link from grammar to children's lives before anything else.

segments.title_en: 'I noticed...' and the I do / we do / you do suggestion
segments.title_ur: 'میں نے نوٹ کیا' اور میں کروں، ہم کریں، تم کرو
segments.summary_en: The mentor notes that children busy writing missed the explanation and suggests modelling one example, writing one together, then children writing alone.

segments.title_en: Reflective question, sorting cards and evidence-based praise
segments.title_ur: سوچنے والا سوال، کارڈ سارٹنگ اور ثبوت کے ساتھ تعریف
segments.summary_en: Asks which sentence type children struggled with (exclamation marks), suggests sorting sentence cards into four types, and praises the board chart with the evidence of correct examples in copies.

segments.title_en: From 'good' to specific feedback and 'why?'
segments.title_ur: 'گڈ' کے بجائے مخصوص فیڈبیک اور 'کیوں؟'
segments.summary_en: The mentor points out that 'good' was said to wrong answers too; the teacher decides to ask 'why do you think this is an exclamatory sentence?' and give specific feedback next time.
segments.recommendable_reason: opened: ped-panel 18:28Z + lead-converge 18:29Z: the module's one classroom chapter

segments.title_en: The steps of a no-blame debrief
segments.title_ur: بغیر الزام کے گفتگو کے مراحل
segments.summary_en: Recaps the debrief steps (positives, 'I noticed', reflective questions, specific examples) and frames feedback as learning, not judgement.

modules.title: Differentiation in Action: Helping Every Student Learn Better
modules.teacher_line_en: For mentors: model a lesson for colleagues, then reflect and give feedback
modules.teacher_line_ur: مینٹورز کے لیے: ساتھیوں کو نمونہ سبق دکھائیں، پھر سوچ بچار اور فیڈبیک
modules.summary_en: A podcast with a teacher mentor on how to coach colleagues in 'differentiation': have teachers sort three of their students into visual, auditory and hands-on learners, model a Parts of a Plant lesson taught three ways (diagram and colour flash cards, a short story, touching a real plant), follow up with reflective questions and feedback, and set up peer learning circles where teachers share lesson materials. The differentiation taught is learning-styles matching, not tasks by level.
modules.summary_ur: یہ ویڈیو مینٹور اساتذہ کے لیے ہے کہ ساتھی اساتذہ کو مشاہدہ، نمونہ سبق، فیڈبیک اور باہمی سیکھنے کے حلقوں کے ذریعے کیسے رہنمائی دیں۔
symptoms: teacher labels children as 'visual' or 'auditory' learners instead of checking what they understood
the same explanation is given to the whole class with no visual or object
modules.not_for: Classroom teachers looking for a move for tomorrow's lesson; it is about mentoring colleagues and its differentiation rests on the learning-styles myth.

segments.title_en: Podcast intro: mentoring colleagues on differentiation
segments.title_ur: تعارف: ساتھی اساتذہ کی رہنمائی
segments.summary_en: The host introduces differentiated instruction and a guest mentor; both frame students as learning by seeing, hearing or doing.

segments.title_en: Know your students (learning-styles sorting)
segments.title_ur: اپنے طلبہ کو جانیں
segments.summary_en: The mentor asks teachers to observe their class and write three students' names with how each learns (visual, auditory, hands-on) as a workshop activity.

segments.title_en: Modelling a Parts of a Plant lesson three ways
segments.title_ur: پودے کے حصوں کا نمونہ سبق تین طریقوں سے
segments.summary_en: The mentor teaches the same science topic with a diagram and colour flash cards, a short story, and real plant parts children can touch.
segments.recommendable_reason: opened: ped-panel 18:28Z + lead-converge 18:29Z: the module's one classroom chapter

segments.title_en: Coaching and feedback for teachers
segments.title_ur: اساتذہ کے لیے کوچنگ اور فیڈبیک
segments.summary_en: After teachers try visuals or different methods the mentor asks reflective questions (did everyone understand, who still struggled) and gives praise plus improvement ideas.

segments.title_en: Peer learning circles in school
segments.title_ur: اسکول میں باہمی سیکھنے کے حلقے
segments.summary_en: Set up teaching corners or peer learning circles where teachers share lesson plans and materials (reading picture cards, a model-making science lesson).

segments.title_en: Recap of the four mentoring steps
segments.title_ur: رہنمائی کے چار مراحل کا خلاصہ
segments.summary_en: Recaps know your students, model teaching, reflect and guide, share and grow together; sign-off.

modules.title: Facilitating Teacher Training on Grouping Strategies for Mixed-Ability Classrooms
modules.teacher_line_en: One topic, three tasks: paragraph, sentence starters, picture cards, all in one lesson
modules.teacher_line_ur: ایک موضوع، تین کام: پیراگراف، جملے کا آغاز اور تصویری کارڈ، ایک ہی سبق میں
modules.summary_en: A trainer shows how to give groups different tasks at different levels: in a Grade 4 English lesson on 'My Favourite Season', an advanced group writes a paragraph with a topic sentence, a middle group writes short sentences from a prompt ('I like winter because...'), and a support group describes picture cards aloud while the teacher writes their sentences on the board; each group shares and gets one next-step comment ('add one more reason'). It also shows skill-based grouping in Urdu (readers discuss a story, the teacher blends letters with beginners), mixed-ability groups with roles in maths, and interest-based groups in social studies. A 'learning style' grouping section repeats the visual/auditory/kinaesthetic myth.
modules.summary_ur: آپ سیکھیں گے کہ کلاس کے بچوں کو ان کی سطح کے مطابق گروپ کر کے ہر گروپ کو الگ کام کیسے دیں، جیسے پیراگراف، مختصر جملے یا تصویری کارڈ سے زبانی بیان۔
symptoms: whole class gets one task; fast finishers sit idle and weak readers copy
teacher says 'tez bachay aagay' but gives no different task
no support (picture, sentence starter) for children who cannot write a full sentence
groups are formed but every group does the same worksheet
modules.not_for: Teachers whose class cannot yet work in groups at all, or who need a whole-class questioning or attention routine first.

segments.title_en: Why one task for all does not work
segments.title_ur: سب کے لیے ایک کام کیوں کافی نہیں
segments.summary_en: Introduces differentiated grouping: with one task some children are bored and others struggle.

segments.title_en: Different tasks for one topic: 'Describing People'
segments.title_ur: ایک موضوع، مختلف کام: لوگوں کو بیان کرنا
segments.summary_en: Grouping means targeted activities, not just groups: fast learners write a descriptive paragraph while beginners practise simple spoken sentences ('He is tall').

segments.title_en: Skill-based grouping in an Urdu reading lesson
segments.title_ur: مہارت کے مطابق گروپ: اردو پڑھائی
segments.summary_en: Group fluent readers to read and discuss a story while the teacher does letter-blending practice with the group still learning letters.

segments.title_en: 'Learning style' grouping (myth)
segments.title_ur: 'لرننگ اسٹائل' کے مطابق گروپ
segments.summary_en: Groups children as visual, auditory or kinaesthetic for a parts-of-a-plant lesson; this is the learning-styles myth and is not a move to recommend.

segments.title_en: Mixed-ability groups with roles, interest-based groups
segments.title_ur: ملے جلے گروپ کردار کے ساتھ، دلچسپی کے مطابق گروپ
segments.summary_en: Mixed-ability maths groups where one solves, one writes and one checks; then children choose a police, doctor or teacher group in social studies and prepare a short skit.

segments.title_en: Grade 4 example: three groups, three tasks, next-step feedback
segments.title_ur: گریڈ 4 مثال: تین گروپ، تین کام، اگلے قدم کا فیڈبیک
segments.summary_en: For 'My Favourite Season': advanced group writes a paragraph, middle group uses 'I like winter because...', support group describes picture cards aloud; groups share and get feedback like 'add one more reason'.

segments.title_en: Reflect and close
segments.title_ur: غور و فکر اور اختتام
segments.summary_en: Asks which grouping strategy suits your class, to share with colleagues, and closes.

modules.title: Inclusive Classrooms: Teaching Every Child Together
modules.teacher_line_en: Same lesson, three levels: extension, guided worksheet, word cards and starters
modules.teacher_line_ur: ایک ہی سبق، تین سطحیں: اضافی کام، رہنما ورک شیٹ، لفظی کارڈ اور جملوں کے آغاز
modules.summary_en: A two-voice podcast with a school leader on making a school inclusive. The usable classroom part is a Grade 5 English 'write a paragraph' lesson planned in three tiers: strong writers expand their paragraph, average learners get a guided worksheet, and pupils who need support get word cards and sentence starters ('same content, different support'). It also shows flexible grouping that moves between mixed-ability and same-level groups. The rest covers staff awareness meetings, grade-team planning and sharing monthly success stories.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ ایک ہی سبق میں مضبوط، اوسط اور مدد چاہنے والے بچوں کو الگ الگ کام اور سہارا کیسے دیں اور گروپ بدل بدل کر کیسے بنائیں۔
symptoms: one task for the whole class; finishers sit idle while others are stuck
teacher says some children are weak but gives everyone the same worksheet
no word cards, sentence starters or extension task offered during writing
the same seating groups all year; strong pupils never help others
modules.not_for: Teachers who already plan tiered tasks; half of it is about leading a school-wide inclusion initiative and staff meetings.

segments.title_en: Podcast intro: inclusive education
segments.title_ur: پوڈکاسٹ کا تعارف: شمولیتی تعلیم
segments.summary_en: Introduces inclusive education (every child learns at their own level) and a school-wide initiative led by a school leader.

segments.title_en: Staff awareness and a common vision
segments.title_ur: عملے میں آگاہی اور مشترکہ مقصد
segments.summary_en: In a staff meeting teachers list which children need extra support (reading difficulty, low confidence) to see that every class has different learners.

segments.title_en: Same content, different support: three-tier task
segments.title_ur: ایک ہی مواد، مختلف مدد: تین سطحی کام
segments.summary_en: For a Grade 5 'write a paragraph' lesson: strong writers expand their paragraph, average learners get a guided worksheet, pupils needing support get word cards and sentence starters.

segments.title_en: Flexible grouping in class
segments.title_ur: کلاس میں لچکدار گروپ بندی
segments.summary_en: Alternate mixed-ability and same-level groups; strong pupils guide classmates, and a support teacher (if any) works with those who need extra help.

segments.title_en: Sustaining inclusion: monthly reflection and success stories
segments.title_ur: شمولیت جاری رکھنا: ماہانہ جائزہ اور کامیابی کی کہانیاں
segments.summary_en: The leader collects monthly teacher feedback (were all children engaged? who needed extra support?) and staff share success stories.

segments.title_en: Key points and sign-off
segments.title_ur: اہم نکات اور اختتام
segments.summary_en: Recap of four points: awareness, collaborative planning, flexible grouping, reflect and celebrate.

modules.title: Enhancing Collaboration through Google Docs and Slides: A School-Wide Initiative
modules.teacher_line_en: Groups write one shared Google Doc and present it as slides
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچوں کے گروپ ایک مشترکہ گوگل ڈاک لکھیں اور سلائیڈز سے پیش کریں
modules.summary_en: A presenter explains Google Docs (a shared online notebook where each child writes a part and the teacher comments) and Google Slides (each child makes a slide and the group presents). It suggests a Grade 4 'My favourite animal' shared doc (one child writes the heading, one the features, one pastes a picture) and a Grade 5 'Our helpers' project in three groups. The rest is school-wide: a staff-meeting demo, student 'tech helpers' and a digital sharing day.
modules.summary_ur: آپ دیکھیں گے کہ گوگل ڈاکس اور سلائیڈز پر بچوں کے گروپ مل کر کیسے لکھیں اور پیش کریں، اور اسکول میں یہ سلسلہ کیسے شروع کریں۔
symptoms: teacher mentions a computer lab or tablets but group work is only on paper
group tasks have no division of parts, so one child writes everything
modules.not_for: Not a next-step clip for a classroom report: it needs devices and internet for every group and is framed as a school-wide initiative led through staff meetings.

segments.title_en: Intro: Google tools and the curriculum
segments.title_ur: تعارف: گوگل ٹولز اور نصاب
segments.summary_en: Greeting; follow-up to the earlier Google tools session; link to the National Curriculum Framework 2023 goals of communication, collaboration, creativity and digital literacy.

segments.title_en: What Docs and Slides do for group work
segments.title_ur: گروپ کام میں ڈاکس اور سلائیڈز کا کردار
segments.summary_en: Docs: each child writes a part, it auto-saves, the teacher sees who writes and comments; Slides: each child makes a slide with a picture and the group presents.

segments.title_en: School-wide strategies
segments.title_ur: پورے اسکول کے لیے حکمت عملیاں
segments.summary_en: Start with a Grade 4 'My favourite animal' shared doc with split parts and live comments ('Add one more detail'); a staff-meeting demo; student tech helpers; a digital sharing day.

segments.title_en: Grade 5 example and planning with staff
segments.title_ur: گریڈ 5 کی مثال اور عملے کے ساتھ منصوبہ
segments.summary_en: Three groups write about police, doctors and teachers in shared docs, get a comment, then present as slides; plan a digital project with colleagues; closing.
segments.recommendable_reason: opened: ped-panel 18:28Z + lead-converge 18:29Z: the module's one classroom chapter

modules.title: Peer Mentoring for Effective Classroom Management
modules.teacher_line_en: How to help a colleague whose class gets noisy: observe, demo, co-plan, follow up
modules.teacher_line_ur: شور والی کلاس میں ساتھی کی مدد: مشاہدہ، مظاہرہ، مشترکہ منصوبہ، فالو اپ
modules.summary_en: A trainer explains how one teacher can mentor a colleague in classroom management: observe when students get distracted and debrief calmly, demonstrate a proven technique such as a silent signal or attention clap, co-plan shared routines (entry, lining up, rewards), pass on quick tips such as a movement break every 15 minutes, and follow up to reinforce progress. A short story shows a colleague's noisy group work fixed by writing rules on the board and naming a group leader before starting.
modules.summary_ur: یہ ویڈیو بتاتی ہے کہ ایک ٹیچر کلاس روم مینجمنٹ میں اپنے ساتھی ٹیچر کی مشاہدے، عملی مظاہرے، مشترکہ منصوبہ بندی اور فالو اپ سے کیسے مدد کر سکتا ہے۔
symptoms: group work dissolves into noise with no rules stated beforehand
teacher has no attention signal and shouts over the class
modules.not_for: Classroom teachers looking for a management move for their own class; this is about mentoring colleagues.

segments.title_en: What peer mentoring in classroom management is
segments.title_ur: کلاس روم مینجمنٹ میں ساتھی کی رہنمائی کیا ہے
segments.summary_en: Introduces peer mentoring: a calm, organised teacher gives a colleague specific, helpful advice on behaviour and engagement.

segments.title_en: Observe and reflect together
segments.title_ur: مشاہدہ اور مل کر غور
segments.summary_en: The mentor observes when students get distracted and how the teacher responds, then a calm debrief; e.g. write class rules such as 'one person speaks at a time' before group work.

segments.title_en: Demonstrate a technique: silent signal, attention clap
segments.title_ur: مظاہرہ: خاموش اشارہ، توجہ کی تالی
segments.summary_en: The mentor shows a proven technique in a real class, such as a silent signal or attention clap, and stresses consistent use.
segments.recommendable_reason: opened: ped-panel 18:28Z + lead-converge 18:29Z: the module's one classroom chapter

segments.title_en: Co-plan shared routines; quick tips
segments.title_ur: مشترکہ معمولات کی منصوبہ بندی؛ فوری مشورے
segments.summary_en: Mentor and colleague plan next week's routines (entry, lining up, reward system) so rules are consistent, and share short tips like a movement break every 15 minutes.

segments.title_en: Reinforce and follow up
segments.title_ur: حوصلہ افزائی اور فالو اپ
segments.summary_en: The mentor follows up each new strategy and credits the colleague's consistency for better cooperation; ends with about 30 s without speech.

segments.title_en: Example: rules and a leader before group work
segments.title_ur: مثال: گروپ کام سے پہلے اصول اور لیڈر
segments.summary_en: A colleague's noisy group work becomes calm after rules are written on the board and a leader is assigned before groups start.

segments.title_en: Reflect and close
segments.title_ur: غور و فکر اور اختتام
segments.summary_en: Asks which colleague you could mentor and what trick you could share at the next staff meeting, and closes.

modules.title: Helping Students Set Long-Term Behavioral Goals
modules.teacher_line_en: Tired of repeating rules? Let pupils set and track their own behaviour goal
modules.teacher_line_ur: بار بار اصول دہرانے سے تھک گئے؟ بچوں کو اپنا رویے کا ہدف خود طے کرنے دیں
modules.summary_en: A narrated guide to helping pupils set their own long-term behaviour goals. The teacher writes a specific, time-bound goal on the board ('I will stay in my seat every period for the next 5 days') and turns 'I will never talk' into 'I will answer only when the teacher asks'. Pupils then choose a positive habit in a short discussion, tick or star a class goal-tracker chart at the end of each day, reflect weekly and get a 'goal buddy' who reminds and supports them.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ بچوں سے رویے کا واضح اور قابلِ پیمائش ہدف خود طے کروا کے چارٹ، ہفتہ وار جائزے اور ساتھی کی مدد سے اس پر عمل کیسے کروائیں۔
symptoms: teacher repeats the same behaviour warning ('apni seat par baitho', 'chup') many times
rules are only imposed; pupils are never asked what they will work on
behaviour is only punished or scolded; no progress is noticed or praised
the same few pupils disrupt every lesson with no plan beyond warnings
modules.not_for: Teachers looking for help with questioning or subject explanation; it is about pupils' behaviour habits over weeks, not one lesson's content.

segments.title_en: Why pupils should set their own behaviour goals
segments.title_ur: بچے اپنے رویے کے ہدف خود کیوں طے کریں
segments.summary_en: Introduces goal setting as a social-emotional skill that builds self-control, responsibility and ownership.

segments.title_en: A clear, measurable, realistic behaviour goal
segments.title_ur: واضح، قابلِ پیمائش اور حقیقت پسندانہ ہدف
segments.summary_en: Goals are about habits, not only marks; the teacher writes 'I will stay in my seat every period for the next 5 days' and turns 'I will never talk' into 'I will answer when the teacher asks'.

segments.title_en: Goal discussion, tracker chart, weekly reflection, goal buddy
segments.title_ur: ہدف پر گفتگو، چارٹ، ہفتہ وار جائزہ اور ساتھی
segments.summary_en: Pupils choose one positive habit in a short discussion, tick or star a class goal chart daily, reflect weekly with teacher feedback, and pair with a goal buddy who reminds them.

segments.title_en: Your class's goals and close
segments.title_ur: اپنی کلاس کے ہدف اور اختتام
segments.summary_en: The teacher reflects on which behaviour goal their own class needs most (focus or respectful talk). Closing summary.

modules.title: School-wide Behavior Management Program
modules.teacher_line_en: Rules ignored? Let groups write the class rules themselves, then pick weekly leaders
modules.teacher_line_ur: اصول نہیں مانے جاتے؟ بچوں سے گروپوں میں خود کلاس کے اصول لکھوائیں
modules.summary_en: An English-narrated slide story about a noisy Class 5 in a government girls' school: instead of giving rules, the teacher claps and says 'Today you will make the rules', groups write three things that disturb the class and a solution for each on an old chart paper (indoor voice, straight line, keep it clean, raise hand, no bullying), the class decorates and hangs the chart, and two weekly class leaders help monitor it; the next day children remind each other. The story then shows the head teacher scaling it school-wide with a good-news wall, and ends with discussion and planning questions.
modules.summary_ur: اس ویڈیو میں آپ دیکھیں گے کہ بچوں سے گروپوں میں کلاس کے مسائل اور ان کے حل لکھوا کر کلاس کے اصول مل کر کیسے بنائیں اور ہفتہ وار کلاس لیڈر کیسے چنیں۔
symptoms: teacher repeats 'shor mat karo' or 'chup' many times and children keep talking
rules are announced by the teacher; children are never asked what disturbs the class
children push or fight in the line and the teacher only scolds
no student has any responsibility for class order
modules.not_for: Teachers whose class is already orderly, or who need help with instruction rather than behaviour; the later school-wide part is for head teachers.

segments.title_en: A noisy school and a tired teacher
segments.title_ur: شور والا اسکول اور تھکی ہوئی ٹیچر
segments.summary_en: Sets the scene: a government girls' elementary school known for noisy corridors, and a soft-spoken Class 5 teacher whose peaceful days are rare.

segments.title_en: Children write their own class rules
segments.title_ur: بچے خود کلاس کے اصول بناتے ہیں
segments.summary_en: The teacher claps and says the class will make the rules; groups list three disturbances and a solution for each on a reused chart paper, decorate and hang it, two weekly class leaders monitor it, and next day children remind each other ('raise hand, don't shout').

segments.title_en: The head teacher takes it school-wide
segments.title_ur: ہیڈ ٹیچر اسے پورے اسکول میں لاگو کرتی ہیں
segments.summary_en: The head teacher notices the quiet class; every class makes its own rules, weekly leaders are chosen, and a good-news wall of teacher praise is made from leftover cardboard; fights, litter and noise drop.

segments.title_en: Discussion and planning questions
segments.title_ur: گفتگو اور منصوبہ بندی کے سوالات
segments.summary_en: Reflection questions on the story and planning questions for starting a similar programme in your school and keeping students motivated.

modules.title: Student-Led Behavior Committees
modules.teacher_line_en: Give children jobs like line captain and peacemaker so they run the discipline
modules.teacher_line_ur: بچوں کو لائن کیپٹن اور صلح کروانے والے جیسی ذمہ داریاں دیں تاکہ نظم وہ خود سنبھالیں
modules.summary_en: A narrated story of a Grade 5 class in a noisy government middle school where the teacher stops shouting 'Oye, sukoon karo!' and forms a 'Rescue Team' from old chart paper: line captain, peacemaker, cleanliness hero, break monitor and a help desk for younger children, with the most restless child made line captain. It ends with a low-cost plan: list the commonest problems, give the team an exciting name, write each role on a chart or card, start with one class, review and praise the committee daily or weekly, guide without taking control, and rotate roles so new children join.
modules.summary_ur: آپ دیکھیں گے کہ کم وسائل میں بچوں کی 'ریسکیو ٹیم' بنا کر لائن، صفائی، جھگڑے اور بریک کی ذمہ داریاں انہیں کیسے دیں تاکہ نظم بچے خود سنبھالیں۔
symptoms: teacher shouts 'chup', 'oye sukoon karo' or 'line seedhi karo' over and over
fights or pushing at line-up and break time are mentioned in the lesson
no child has any classroom responsibility; the teacher handles every disruption alone
modules.not_for: Teachers whose report is about questioning, explanation or subject content; this is a behaviour and class-roles video, mostly told as a story.

segments.title_en: Story: a school in daily chaos
segments.title_ur: کہانی: روز کا شور شرابا
segments.summary_en: Noise in class, pushing in line, fights at break and a teacher who only says 'Oye, sukoon karo!'; a break-time accident makes the teacher decide to change things.

segments.title_en: Forming a 'Rescue Team' with clear roles
segments.title_ur: واضح ذمہ داریوں والی 'ریسکیو ٹیم' بنانا
segments.summary_en: The teacher tells the class they will be discipline heroes; with only chart paper and markers, roles are shared out: line captain, peacemaker, cleanliness hero, break monitor, help desk; the most restless child becomes line captain.

segments.title_en: Story: children run the school
segments.title_ur: کہانی: بچے اسکول سنبھالتے ہیں
segments.summary_en: The line captain calls 'Qadam barabar!', the peacemaker says 'Talk first', the help desk walks a sad younger child to class; the head teacher spreads it school-wide and fights drop over two months.

segments.title_en: Plan: problems, a team name, roles on a chart
segments.title_ur: منصوبہ: مسائل، ٹیم کا نام، چارٹ پر ذمہ داریاں
segments.summary_en: Reflection questions, then steps: list the commonest problems (noise, fights, litter, line-breaking), introduce the team with a story and a name, give clear volunteer roles written on a chart or card, start with one class.

segments.title_en: Review, praise and rotate roles
segments.title_ur: جائزہ، تعریف اور ذمہ داریوں کی تبدیلی
segments.summary_en: Review the committee daily or weekly and praise good work, let children make charts and badges, guide without full control, use a good-news wall, reflect monthly and rotate roles to new children.
